catalog.name: General Ledger calculations
catalog.description: Every formula, algorithm, rounding rule and worked example of the general ledger domain, in a structured form a rebuild can test against: the rounding conventions, the balance and its two derived columns, the foreign-currency amounts, the balance invariant, the entry totals, the lock dates and the accounting date rule, the whole numbering grammar and its assignment, the inalterability hash chain, the reconciliation algorithm with its exchange differences, the fiscal year, the opening entry, the partner ledger figures, the account code generation, the dashboard figures of a liquidity journal, the automatic transfers, and the end-to-end walkthrough that ties them together.

records.name: Rounding a monetary amount to the rounding step of its currency
records.purpose: Reduces any intermediate monetary result to a value that the currency can actually represent, so that every stored amount of the ledger sits on the smallest representable increment of its currency.

operands.name: value
operands.source: the intermediate result of any monetary computation of the domain
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rounding step
operands.source: the rounding step recorded on the currency, for example 0.01, or 0.05 for a currency whose smallest coin is five cents, or 1 for a currency with no subdivision
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero

preconditions.condition: The currency to round to is known: the company currency for the balance, the debit, the credit, every signed total and the matched amount of a partial reconciliation; the document currency or the item currency for amounts expressed in those.
preconditions.otherwise: No rounding can be applied and the amount cannot be stored; the calculation that needed it is not meaningful.

preconditions.condition: The rounding step of that currency is strictly greater than zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The value is left unchanged.

procedure: Take the absolute value of the amount and remember its sign.

When the rounding step is smaller than one, normalise the absolute value by multiplying it by the inverse of the rounding step, so that the division is performed on whole units and binary representation error cannot shift the result across a half step.
Divide the absolute value by the rounding step, add one half, and take the whole part downwards.
Multiply the whole part obtained by the rounding step, denormalising when the value was normalised.
Restore the remembered sign.
records.formula: rounded_value = sign( value ) × floor( | value | ÷ rounding_step + 0.5 ) × rounding_step

rounding.what: Every monetary quantity of the domain, at the moment it is written or compared.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency the amount is expressed in, and the number of decimal places derived from that step.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied on the rounding step; the alternative methods always away from zero, always towards zero, half towards zero and half to even exist and are specified in the multi-currency documents.
rounding.step: At the end of each monetary computation, before the value is stored or compared, and after the normalisation by the inverse of the rounding step when that step is smaller than one.

result.name: rounded value
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the field that carries the amount, and displayed with the number of decimal places derived from the rounding step.

edge_cases.case: The value is exactly on a half step, for example 0.005 with a rounding step of 0.01.
edge_cases.outcome: The half is carried away from zero: 0.005 becomes 0.01 and −0.005 becomes −0.01.

edge_cases.case: The rounding step is one, for a currency with no subdivision.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is a whole number of currency units.

edge_cases.case: The rounding step is 0.05.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is a multiple of five hundredths; 1.23 becomes 1.25 and 1.22 becomes 1.20.

edge_cases.case: The value is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero and the sign is immaterial.

edge_cases.case: The quantity is not monetary.
edge_cases.outcome: A percentage of an analytic distribution is handled with two decimals; a quantity uses the product-unit precision, which belongs to the units of measure and packaging documents.

worked_examples.description: Converting one thousand United States dollars into euros at a rate of one point one
worked_examples.narrative: Nine hundred and nine point zero nine zero nine and so on divided by the step of one hundredth gives 90 909.09; adding one half gives 90 909.59; the whole part downwards is 90 909; multiplied by the step of one hundredth this is 909.09.

worked_examples.description: A half step carried away from zero on a negative amount
worked_examples.narrative: The absolute value of five thousandths divided by one hundredth is 0.5; adding one half gives 1.0; the whole part is 1; multiplied by the step this is 0.01; the remembered sign makes it minus one hundredth.

records.name: The zero test of an amount for a currency
records.purpose: Decides whether an amount is nothing at the precision of a currency; this is the test behind the reconciled flag, behind the decision to produce an exchange difference, and behind the balance invariant.

operands.name: amount
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency the test is made for
operands.source: any monetary quantity of the domain, typically a residual or the sum of the balances of an entry
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rounding step
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency the test is made for
operands.source: the rounding step recorded on that currency
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero

preconditions.condition: A currency is named for the test.
preconditions.otherwise: The test is not meaningful; the company currency is the currency used whenever the specification does not say otherwise.

procedure: Take the absolute value of the amount.
Round that absolute value to the rounding step of the currency, half away from zero.
Answer yes when the rounded absolute value is zero and no otherwise.
records.formula: is_zero( amount , currency ) = ( round_to_currency( | amount | ) = 0 )

rounding.what: The absolute value of the amount, before the comparison with zero.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the named currency.
rounding.step: Once, immediately before the comparison.

result.name: is zero
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored on its own; it feeds the reconciled flag of a Journal Item, the balance check of a Journal Entry and the decision to create an exchange difference.

edge_cases.case: The amount is smaller than half the rounding step, for example 0.004 with a step of 0.01.
edge_cases.outcome: The rounded absolute value is zero, so the answer is yes: the amount is nothing at that precision.

edge_cases.case: The amount is exactly half a rounding step, for example 0.005 with a step of 0.01.
edge_cases.outcome: The rounded absolute value is 0.01, so the answer is no.

edge_cases.case: The amount is expressed in one currency but tested against another.
edge_cases.outcome: The answer follows the rounding step of the currency named in the test, which is why the residual in the company currency and the residual in the item currency are tested separately and each against its own currency.

worked_examples.description: A residual left open by an exchange rate movement
worked_examples.narrative: Forty-three euros and twenty-nine cents rounded to one hundredth is itself, which is not zero, so the item is not reconciled in the company currency and an exchange difference is prepared.

worked_examples.description: The residual of an item that has been matched in full
worked_examples.narrative: The rounded absolute value is zero, so the item counts as reconciled in the company currency.

records.name: The comparison of two amounts for a currency
records.purpose: Orders two monetary amounts at the precision of a currency, so that a difference smaller than the rounding step never makes one amount look greater than the other.

operands.name: first amount
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency the comparison is made for
operands.source: any monetary quantity of the domain
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: second amount
operands.source: any monetary quantity of the domain
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rounding step
operands.source: the rounding step recorded on that currency
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero

preconditions.condition: Both amounts are expressed in the same currency.
preconditions.otherwise: One of them is converted first at the applicable rate; comparing amounts of two currencies directly is not meaningful.

procedure: Subtract the second amount from the first.
Round the difference to the rounding step of the currency, half away from zero.
Answer minus one when the rounded difference is negative, zero when it is zero, and plus one when it is positive.
records.formula: compare( first , second , currency ) = sign( round_to_currency( first − second ) ) , giving −1 , 0 or +1

rounding.what: The difference of the two amounts, not the two amounts themselves.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the named currency.
rounding.step: Once, after the subtraction and before the sign is read.

result.name: comparison outcome
result.unit_or_currency: minus one, zero or plus one
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it drives the choice of the smaller of two residuals when a partial match is computed and the tolerance tests of a foreign-currency match.

edge_cases.case: The two amounts differ by less than half a rounding step.
edge_cases.outcome: The rounded difference is zero and the answer is zero: the two amounts are equal at that precision.

edge_cases.case: Both amounts are zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The answer is zero.

edge_cases.case: The difference is exactly half a rounding step.
edge_cases.outcome: The rounded difference is one whole step and the answer carries its sign.

worked_examples.description: Comparing the two company-currency sides of a foreign-currency match
worked_examples.narrative: The difference of forty-three euros and twenty-nine cents is far larger than one hundredth, so the first amount is strictly greater and the smaller of the two, 909.09, is the matched amount.

worked_examples.description: Two amounts that differ only by rounding noise
worked_examples.narrative: The two differ by two hundredths, so the comparison answers plus one; whether that difference is genuine is then decided by the tolerance ranges of the foreign-currency match, not by this comparison.

records.name: The debit and the credit of a journal item under normal accounting
records.purpose: Derives the two presentation columns of a Journal Item from the single authoritative balance, for a company that does not use storno accounting.

operands.name: balance
operands.source: the authoritative amount written on the Journal Item
operands.constraints: rounded to the company currency; may be positive, negative or zero

preconditions.condition: The item is not flagged as storno.
preconditions.otherwise: The storno derivation applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The item is not a section, a subsection or a note.
preconditions.otherwise: The debit, the credit, the balance and the foreign amount are all zero and no account is carried.

procedure: Round the balance to the company currency.
When the balance is strictly positive, set the debit to the balance and the credit to zero.
When the balance is strictly negative, set the debit to zero and the credit to the balance with its sign reversed.
When the balance is zero, set both the debit and the credit to zero.
records.formula:
debit  = balance          when balance > 0, otherwise 0
credit = − balance        when balance < 0, otherwise 0

rounding.what: The balance, and therefore the debit and the credit derived from it.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: On the balance, before the two columns are derived; no further rounding takes place in the derivation itself.

result.name: the pair debit and credit
result.stored_or_displayed: Both are stored on the Journal Item and are the columns shown in every ledger list and report.

edge_cases.case: The balance is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Both columns are zero, which is the only situation in which neither column carries an amount.

edge_cases.case: Both columns would be non-zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Impossible: the product of the debit and the credit is always zero for an item that is not a section, a subsection or a note.

edge_cases.case: A creation supplies a debit or a credit and no balance.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance written is the debit minus the credit and the two supplied values are discarded, after which this derivation reproduces them.

worked_examples.description: A miscellaneous entry booking an expense against a payable
worked_examples.narrative: The expense balance is positive, so it becomes a debit of 1 250.00 with a zero credit; the payable balance is negative, so it becomes a credit of 1 250.00 with a zero debit.

worked_examples.description: The ordinary reversal of that entry
worked_examples.narrative: Reversing the balances gives a credit of 1 250.00 on the expense account and a debit of 1 250.00 on the payable account.

records.name: The debit and the credit of a journal item under storno accounting
records.purpose: Derives the two presentation columns of a Journal Item that is flagged as storno, so that a reversal appears as a negative debit on the original debit side instead of as a credit and the gross turnover of the account stays correct.

operands.name: balance
operands.source: the authoritative amount written on the Journal Item
operands.constraints: rounded to the company currency; may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: storno flag
operands.source: the item, set by the company accounting style or by a negative amount typed into the debit or the credit box
operands.constraints: must be yes for this derivation to apply

preconditions.condition: The item is flagged as storno.
preconditions.otherwise: The normal derivation applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The item is not a section, a subsection or a note.
preconditions.otherwise: The debit, the credit, the balance and the foreign amount are all zero.

procedure: Round the balance to the company currency.
When the balance is strictly negative, set the debit to the balance, which is therefore negative, and the credit to zero.
When the balance is strictly positive, set the credit to the balance with its sign reversed, which is therefore negative, and the debit to zero.
When the balance is zero, set both columns to zero.
records.formula:
debit  = balance          when balance < 0, otherwise 0
credit = − balance        when balance > 0, otherwise 0

rounding.what: The balance, and therefore the debit and the credit derived from it.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: On the balance, before the two columns are derived.

result.name: the pair debit and credit, either of which may be negative
result.stored_or_displayed: Both are stored on the Journal Item; a negative column is displayed as such.

edge_cases.case: A negative number is typed into the debit or the credit box.
edge_cases.outcome: The storno flag is set on the item and this derivation applies from then on.

edge_cases.case: The balance is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Both columns are zero, exactly as under normal accounting.

edge_cases.case: A storno reversal of an expense.
edge_cases.outcome: The expense account keeps a single debit column whose total returns to zero, instead of showing a debit and a credit of the same size.

worked_examples.description: The storno reversal of an entry that booked an expense of 1 250.00 against a payable
worked_examples.narrative: The reversal gives a debit of minus 1 250.00 on the expense account rather than a credit of 1 250.00, so that the gross debit turnover of the expense account returns to zero.

records.name: The balance of a journal item derived from a typed debit and credit
records.purpose: Turns the two figures a user may type into the authoritative balance, which is the only amount the ledger stores as the source of truth.

operands.name: debit
operands.source: the debit box of the item, as typed
operands.constraints: may be negative, which sets the storno flag

operands.name: credit
operands.source: the credit box of the item, as typed
operands.constraints: may be negative, which sets the storno flag

preconditions.condition: At least one of the two boxes carries a value.
preconditions.otherwise: The default balance of a new item of a miscellaneous entry is proposed instead.

preconditions.condition: The item is not a section, a subsection or a note.
preconditions.otherwise: Both boxes are forced to zero.

procedure: Read the debit and the credit as typed, treating an empty box as zero.
Subtract the credit from the debit.
Round the difference to the company currency and write it as the balance.
Set the storno flag when a negative number was typed into either box.
Discard the two typed values: they are rebuilt from the balance by the derivation that matches the accounting style.
records.formula: balance = debit − credit

rounding.what: The difference of the typed debit and the typed credit.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once, before the balance is written.

result.name: balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Item as the authoritative amount; the debit and the credit are then derived from it.

edge_cases.case: Both boxes carry a value.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance is their difference; the two typed values are discarded, so an item can never keep a non-zero debit and a non-zero credit at the same time.

edge_cases.case: A negative number is typed into a box.
edge_cases.outcome: The storno flag is set and the storno derivation rebuilds the columns.

edge_cases.case: A creation supplies a debit or a credit together with a balance.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance supplied wins and the two columns are rebuilt from it.

worked_examples.description: A debit typed on the expense line of a miscellaneous entry
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand two hundred and fifty minus zero is 1 250.00, which is written as the balance and rebuilt as a debit of 1 250.00.

worked_examples.description: A credit typed on the payable line of the same entry
worked_examples.narrative: Zero minus one thousand two hundred and fifty is minus 1 250.00, which is written as the balance and rebuilt as a credit of 1 250.00.

records.name: The default balance proposed for a new item of a miscellaneous entry
records.purpose: Proposes, for a new item added to a non-invoice entry with no amount supplied, the amount that makes the entry balance, so that the balance invariant is satisfied without the user computing the difference.

operands.name: balance of every other item of the entry
operands.source: the items already present on the Journal Entry, excluding the new one
operands.constraints: each rounded to the company currency

preconditions.condition: The entry is a plain entry, that is not an invoice-like document.
preconditions.otherwise: The proposed balance is zero, because the amount of an invoice line comes from the price and the quantity.

preconditions.condition: No amount was supplied for the new item.
preconditions.otherwise: The supplied amount is kept and nothing is proposed.

procedure: Add up the balances of every item of the entry other than the new one.
Reverse the sign of that sum.
Round the result to the company currency and propose it as the balance of the new item.
records.formula: proposed_balance = − ( sum of the balances of every other item of the entry )

rounding.what: The proposed balance.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: After the sum has been reversed in sign, before the value is placed in the new item.

result.name: proposed balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Placed in the balance box of the new item as a proposal; the user may overwrite it.

edge_cases.case: The entry is already balanced.
edge_cases.outcome: The proposed balance is zero.

edge_cases.case: The entry has no other item.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is zero and the proposed balance is zero.

edge_cases.case: The entry is an invoice-like document.
edge_cases.outcome: The proposed balance is zero regardless of the other items.

worked_examples.description: A third line added to an entry that already carries an expense debit and a partial payable credit
worked_examples.narrative: The other items sum to 250.00, so the proposal is minus 250.00, which is a credit of 250.00 and brings the entry to zero.

worked_examples.description: A line added to a customer invoice
worked_examples.narrative: For an invoice-like document the proposal is zero, because the amount is produced by the price and the quantity of the line.

records.name: The currency rate of a journal item
records.purpose: Fixes the rate that links the company-currency balance of an item to the amount expressed in the currency of the item, so that both amounts of the item describe the same economic value.

operands.name: stored rate of an invoice-like document
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the item currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the rate recorded on the invoice-like Journal Entry when it was issued
operands.constraints: strictly positive; when absent the value one is used

operands.name: conversion rate of the currency table
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the item currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the rate that converts the company currency into the item currency at the rate date
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: rate date
operands.source: the document date of the entry when it has one, otherwise the accounting date, otherwise the current date
operands.constraints: a valid date

preconditions.condition: The item carries a currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is one.

preconditions.condition: A rate exists in the currency table for the pair of currencies at the rate date.
preconditions.otherwise: The nearest applicable rate of the currency table is used, as the multi-currency documents specify.

procedure: When the entry is an invoice-like document, take the rate stored on that document, and take one when it stores none.
Otherwise determine the rate date: the document date of the entry when it has one, otherwise the accounting date, otherwise the current date.
Otherwise take the conversion rate of the currency table from the company currency into the item currency at that rate date.
When the item carries no currency at all, take one.
records.formula:
currency_rate = invoice_currency_rate                      when the entry is an invoice-like document
currency_rate = conversion_rate( company_currency → item_currency, at the rate date )   otherwise
currency_rate = 1                                          when the item has no currency

rounding.what: Nothing: the rate itself is not rounded.
rounding.precision: The rate is carried at the precision of the currency table; only the amounts derived from it are rounded.
rounding.step: Rounding is applied to the converted amount, never to the rate.

result.name: currency rate of the item
result.unit_or_currency: units of the item currency per unit of the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held on the item for the conversion between the balance and the foreign amount; the rate of an invoice-like document is stored on the entry.

edge_cases.case: The entry is an invoice-like document with no stored rate.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is one.

edge_cases.case: The item currency equals the company currency and the entry is not an invoice-like document.
edge_cases.outcome: The foreign amount is forced to be exactly equal to the balance, whatever the currency table says.

edge_cases.case: The entry has neither a document date nor an accounting date.
edge_cases.outcome: The current date is used as the rate date.

worked_examples.description: An item in United States dollars on a plain entry, the company keeping its books in euros

inputs.rate_date: the accounting date of the entry

worked_examples.narrative: One euro buys one point one United States dollars on the rate date, so the rate of the item is 1.10 dollars per euro.

worked_examples.description: An item of a customer invoice issued at a fixed rate
worked_examples.narrative: The invoice froze the rate at 1.05 foreign units per euro when it was issued, so every item of that invoice uses 1.05 whatever the currency table says later.

records.name: The foreign amount of a journal item derived from its balance
records.purpose: Produces the amount in the currency of the item from the company-currency balance, which is the direction used whenever the accountant types a company-currency figure on an item that carries a foreign currency.

operands.name: balance
operands.source: the authoritative amount of the Journal Item
operands.constraints: rounded to the company currency

operands.name: currency rate of the item
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the item currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the rate of the item
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The item carries a currency different from the company currency, or the entry is an invoice-like document.
preconditions.otherwise: The foreign amount is forced to be exactly equal to the balance.

preconditions.condition: The rate of the item is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate one is used and the two amounts are equal.

procedure: Take the balance of the item in the company currency.
Multiply it by the rate of the item.
Round the product to the rounding step of the item currency, half away from zero.
Write the result as the foreign amount of the item.
records.formula: amount_currency = round_to_item_currency( balance × currency_rate )

rounding.what: The product of the balance and the rate.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the item currency.
rounding.step: After the multiplication, before the foreign amount is written.

result.name: foreign amount of the item
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Item and shown in the amount-in-currency column.

edge_cases.case: The balance is zero and the foreign amount is not.
edge_cases.outcome: Permitted: this is exactly what an exchange-difference item looks like.

edge_cases.case: The balance and the foreign amount would carry opposite signs.
edge_cases.outcome: Refused by a database check on any accountable item; both may be zero, and one may be zero while the other is not.

edge_cases.case: The item currency is the company currency on a plain entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The foreign amount is set exactly equal to the balance without any multiplication.

worked_examples.description: A receivable of 952.38 euros on an invoice issued at 1.05 foreign units per euro
worked_examples.narrative: Nine hundred and fifty-two point three eight multiplied by one point zero five is 1 000.00 foreign units, which is already on the rounding step of the foreign currency.

records.name: The balance of a journal item derived from its foreign amount
records.purpose: Produces the company-currency balance from the amount typed in the currency of the item, which is the direction used whenever the accountant records a foreign-currency document or payment.

operands.name: foreign amount
operands.source: the amount typed on the Journal Item in its own currency
operands.constraints: rounded to the item currency

operands.name: currency rate of the item
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the item currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the rate of the item
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The rate of the item is strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The division cannot be performed; the rate one is used and the balance equals the foreign amount.

preconditions.condition: The item carries a currency different from the company currency, or the entry is an invoice-like document.
preconditions.otherwise: The balance is exactly the typed amount.

procedure: Take the amount typed in the currency of the item.
Divide it by the rate of the item.
Round the quotient to the rounding step of the company currency, half away from zero.
Write the result as the balance, and derive the debit and the credit from it.
records.formula: balance = round_to_company_currency( amount_currency ÷ currency_rate )

rounding.what: The quotient of the foreign amount by the rate.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: After the division, before the balance is written and before the debit and the credit are derived.

result.name: balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Item as the authoritative amount; the debit and the credit follow from it.

edge_cases.case: The quotient falls exactly on a half step.
edge_cases.outcome: It is carried away from zero, so a foreign amount that converts to 0.005 becomes 0.01.

edge_cases.case: The foreign amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance is zero; an item with a zero foreign amount and a non-zero balance is nevertheless permitted, and is what a company-currency exchange correction looks like.

edge_cases.case: The balance and the foreign amount would carry opposite signs.
edge_cases.outcome: Refused by a database check on any accountable item.

worked_examples.description: One thousand United States dollars entered at a rate of 1.10 dollars per euro, the company keeping its books in euros
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand divided by one point one is 909.0909 and so on, which rounds to 909.09 euros; the stored triple is a balance of 909.09, a debit of 909.09 and a credit of 0.00, with a foreign amount of 1 000.00 United States dollars.

records.name: The balance invariant of a journal entry
records.purpose: States the condition every Journal Entry must satisfy in the company currency, which is the single property that makes the ledger a double-entry ledger.

operands.name: balance of each item of the entry
operands.source: the stored balance of every Journal Item of the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: the stored value is used, never a computed field, so that the check is valid in the middle of a recomputation

operands.name: debit of each item of the entry
operands.source: the derived debit column
operands.constraints: used only for the equivalent form of the check

operands.name: credit of each item of the entry
operands.source: the derived credit column
operands.constraints: used only for the equivalent form of the check

preconditions.condition: The internal flag that suspends the check is not set.
preconditions.otherwise: The check is skipped for the duration of that explicit suspension.

preconditions.condition: The entry has at least one item.
preconditions.otherwise: The sum is zero and the entry balances trivially.

procedure: Add up the stored balances of every item of the entry.
Round the sum to the company currency.
Require the rounded sum to be zero.
Run this check around every creation, every write and every deletion of an entry or of its items, and around every reconciliation.

When one entry fails, refuse with the message "The entry is not balanced."; when several fail, refuse with "The following entries are unbalanced:" followed by one line per entry, indented by two spaces and a hyphen, carrying the entry number.
records.formula:
for each entry:  round_to_company_currency( sum over its items of balance ) = 0
equivalently:    round_to_company_currency( sum of debit ) = round_to_company_currency( sum of credit )

rounding.what: The sum of the stored balances of the items of the entry.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once, on the sum, immediately before the comparison with zero; the individual balances are already rounded when they are written.

result.name: the entry balances
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; a negative answer refuses the write and shows the failure message.

edge_cases.case: The entry is unbalanced in the document currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Permitted: there is no invariant in the document currency, and that imbalance is exactly what an exchange-difference entry later corrects.

edge_cases.case: Individual balances each round cleanly but their sum does not.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is rounded once before the comparison, so a residue smaller than half a rounding step never fails the check.

edge_cases.case: The entry has no item at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is zero and the entry balances.

worked_examples.description: A balanced miscellaneous entry
worked_examples.narrative: The two balances cancel exactly, so the rounded sum is zero and the write is accepted.

worked_examples.description: A foreign imbalance that is tolerated
worked_examples.narrative: A payment of 1 000.00 dollars at 1.10 matched against an invoice of 1 000.00 dollars booked at 1.05 gives 909.09 and 952.38 euros; the difference of 43.29 euros is booked by an exchange-difference entry, and each entry on its own balances in euros.

records.name: The direction sign of a journal entry
records.purpose: Gives the multiplier that turns the internal signed totals of an entry into the positive amounts a user expects to read on a document, and that makes a purchase reduce the signed turnover in the reports.

operands.name: document type of the entry
operands.unit_or_currency: one of the document types of the domain
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: one of plain entry, customer invoice, customer credit note, vendor bill, vendor credit note, sales receipt, purchase receipt

preconditions.condition: The document type of the entry is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The entry is treated as a plain entry and the sign is plus one.

procedure: Answer plus one when the document type is a plain entry.
Answer plus one when the document is outbound, that is a vendor bill, a purchase receipt or a customer credit note.
Answer minus one otherwise, that is when the document is inbound: a customer invoice, a sales receipt or a vendor credit note.
records.formula:
direction_sign = +1    when the document type is a plain entry, or the document is outbound
direction_sign = −1    otherwise (the document is inbound)

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded.
rounding.precision: Not applicable: the result is plus one or minus one.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: direction sign
result.stored_or_displayed: Held on the entry and used as a multiplier by every published amount field of the entry.

edge_cases.case: A customer credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: It is an outbound document, so the sign is plus one, the opposite of the customer invoice it reverses.

edge_cases.case: A vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: It is an inbound document, so the sign is minus one, the opposite of the vendor bill it reverses.

edge_cases.case: A plain entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is plus one and the grand total is taken as an absolute value.

worked_examples.description: The four ordinary document types
worked_examples.narrative: Only the inbound documents, of which the customer invoice is the ordinary case, carry minus one.

records.name: The running totals of an invoice-like document
records.purpose: Accumulates, in one walk over the items of an invoice-like document, the four pairs of totals from which every published amount of the document is produced.

operands.name: balance of each item
operands.source: the Journal Items of the entry
operands.constraints: rounded to the company currency

operands.name: foreign amount of each item
operands.source: the Journal Items of the entry
operands.constraints: rounded to the document currency

operands.name: residual amounts of each payment-term item
operands.source: the residual in the company currency and the residual in the item currency of the payment-term items
operands.constraints: used instead of the balance for payment-term items

operands.name: display type of each item
operands.unit_or_currency: one of the display types of a Journal Item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: one of product, tax, non-deductible tax, rounding, non-deductible product, non-deductible product total, payment term, section, subsection, note

preconditions.condition: The entry is an invoice-like document.
preconditions.otherwise: The plain-entry accumulation applies instead.

procedure: Start the four pairs of running totals — untaxed, tax, grand total and residual — at zero, each pair holding one company-currency figure taken from the balance and one document-currency figure taken from the foreign amount.
Walk the items once, in their natural order.
Add an item whose display type is tax, non-deductible tax, or a rounding produced by a tax distribution line, to the tax total and to the grand total.
Add an item whose display type is product, a rounding without a tax distribution line, non-deductible product, or non-deductible product total, to the untaxed total and to the grand total.
Add an item whose display type is payment term to the residual total only, and using the residual amounts of the item rather than its balance and its foreign amount.
Ignore an item whose display type is a section, a subsection or a note, and every other display type.
records.formula:
total_untaxed_company  = sum of balance over the product, rounding-without-tax-distribution, non-deductible product and non-deductible product total items
total_tax_company      = sum of balance over the tax, non-deductible tax and rounding-from-tax-distribution items
total_company          = total_untaxed_company + total_tax_company
total_residual_company = sum of amount_residual over the payment term items
and the same four sums over amount_currency and amount_residual_currency for the document currency

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded during the walk: the item amounts are already rounded when they are stored.
rounding.precision: The company-currency figures carry the precision of the company currency, the document-currency figures that of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each item amount.
rounding.step: No rounding step inside the accumulation; the published fields are produced from these totals without further rounding.

result.name: the four pairs of running totals — untaxed, tax, grand total and residual
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored as such; they are the intermediate values from which the published amount fields of the entry are computed.

edge_cases.case: The document carries only sections and notes.
edge_cases.outcome: Every total stays at zero.

edge_cases.case: A rounding item produced by a tax distribution line.
edge_cases.outcome: It counts as tax; a rounding item that has no tax distribution line counts as untaxed.

edge_cases.case: A payment-term item that has been partly matched.
edge_cases.outcome: Only its residual amounts enter the residual total, so the total falls as payments are matched.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice with one product line of 100.00 and a tax of twenty-one per cent, in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The product line gives an untaxed total of minus 100.00, the tax line a tax total of minus 21.00, the two together a grand total of minus 121.00, and the payment-term line a residual total of plus 121.00 because nothing has been matched yet.

records.name: The running totals of a plain entry
records.purpose: Accumulates the grand total of an entry that is not an invoice-like document, where only the debit side is counted so that the total reads as the size of the entry rather than as zero.

operands.name: balance of each item whose debit is non-zero
operands.source: the Journal Items of the plain entry
operands.constraints: only items with a non-zero debit contribute

operands.name: foreign amount of each item whose debit is non-zero
operands.source: the same items
operands.constraints: only items with a non-zero debit contribute

preconditions.condition: The entry is a plain entry, that is not an invoice-like document.
preconditions.otherwise: The invoice-like accumulation applies instead.

procedure: Walk the items of the entry once.
Keep only the items whose debit is non-zero.
Add their balances into the company-currency grand total and their foreign amounts into the document-currency grand total.
Leave the untaxed, tax and residual totals at zero: a plain entry contributes to the grand total only.
records.formula:
total_company  = sum of balance over items whose debit is non-zero
total_document = sum of amount_currency over items whose debit is non-zero

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded during the walk.
rounding.precision: The company-currency figure carries the precision of the company currency, the document-currency figure that of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each item amount.
rounding.step: No rounding step inside the accumulation.

result.name: the grand total of the plain entry, in the company currency and in the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored as such; it feeds the published grand total and signed grand total of the entry.

edge_cases.case: Every item of the entry has a zero debit.
edge_cases.outcome: The grand total is zero.

edge_cases.case: The entry uses storno accounting and its debit column is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The debit is non-zero, so the item contributes, and it contributes its negative balance.

edge_cases.case: The entry carries sections or notes.
edge_cases.outcome: They have a zero debit and therefore contribute nothing.

worked_examples.description: A plain entry with an expense debit and a payable credit
worked_examples.narrative: Only the debit item counts, so the grand total is 1 250.00; the direction sign of a plain entry is plus one, the published grand total is 1 250.00 and the signed grand total is the absolute value, 1 250.00.

records.name: The published amount fields of a journal entry
records.purpose: Turns the four pairs of running totals and the direction sign into the amounts stored on the entry and shown to the user, in both the reader-friendly orientation and the signed orientation the reports aggregate.

operands.name: direction sign
operands.source: the direction sign of the entry
operands.constraints: plus one or minus one

operands.name: total untaxed, in the company currency and in the document currency
operands.source: the running totals of the entry
operands.constraints: already rounded

operands.name: total tax, in the company currency and in the document currency
operands.source: the running totals of the entry
operands.constraints: already rounded

operands.name: grand total, in the company currency and in the document currency
operands.source: the running totals of the entry
operands.constraints: already rounded

operands.name: total residual, in the company currency and in the document currency
operands.source: the running totals of the entry
operands.constraints: already rounded

preconditions.condition: The running totals of the entry have been accumulated.
preconditions.otherwise: The published fields cannot be produced.

preconditions.condition: The direction sign of the entry is known.
preconditions.otherwise: Plus one is used, which is the value for a plain entry.

procedure: Multiply the document-currency untaxed total by the direction sign to obtain the published untaxed amount.
Multiply the document-currency tax total by the direction sign to obtain the published tax amount.
Multiply the document-currency grand total by the direction sign to obtain the published grand total.
Multiply the document-currency residual total by minus the direction sign to obtain the published residual amount.
Reverse the sign of each company-currency total, and of the document-currency untaxed total, to obtain the four signed fields that the reports aggregate.
Take the absolute value of the company-currency grand total for the signed grand total of a plain entry, and the reversed sign of that total for every other document type.

Take the absolute value of the published grand total for the signed grand total in currency of a plain entry, and minus the product of the direction sign and the published grand total for every other document type.
records.formula:
amount_untaxed                    = direction_sign × total_untaxed_document
amount_tax                        = direction_sign × total_tax_document
amount_total                      = direction_sign × total_document
amount_residual                   = − direction_sign × total_residual_document
amount_untaxed_signed             = − total_untaxed_company
amount_untaxed_in_currency_signed = − total_untaxed_document
amount_tax_signed                 = − total_tax_company
amount_total_signed               = | total_company |            for a plain entry
amount_total_signed               = − total_company               otherwise
amount_residual_signed            = total_residual_company
amount_total_in_currency_signed   = | amount_total |              for a plain entry
amount_total_in_currency_signed   = − ( direction_sign × amount_total )   otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: the totals entering these formulas are already at the precision of their currency.
rounding.precision: Company-currency fields at the precision of the company currency, document-currency fields at the precision of the document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each item amount.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the publication itself.

result.name: the eleven published amount fields of the entry
result.unit_or_currency: company currency for the fields with a company-currency total behind them, document currency for the others
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry and displayed on the document and in every report that aggregates entries.

edge_cases.case: A plain entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The signed grand total is the absolute value of the company-currency grand total, and the signed grand total in currency is the absolute value of the published grand total.

edge_cases.case: A purchase document.
edge_cases.outcome: The signed company total is negative, which is what makes a purchase reduce the signed turnover in the reports.

edge_cases.case: Nothing has been matched against the document yet.
edge_cases.outcome: The published residual equals the published grand total.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice with one product line of 100.00 and a tax of twenty-one per cent
worked_examples.narrative: The direction sign of a customer invoice is minus one, so the untaxed amount is minus one times minus 100.00, that is 100.00; the tax is 21.00; the grand total is 121.00; the residual is minus minus one times 121.00, that is 121.00; the signed grand total is minus minus 121.00, that is 121.00; and the signed untaxed amount is 100.00.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill with the same figures and the opposite item signs
worked_examples.narrative: The direction sign is plus one, so the untaxed amount is 100.00 and the grand total is 121.00, while the signed company total is minus 121.00: the signed total of a purchase document is negative, which is what makes a purchase reduce the signed turnover in the reports.

worked_examples.description: A plain entry of 1 250.00
worked_examples.narrative: Only the debit item counts, so the grand total is 1 250.00, the published grand total is 1 250.00 and the signed grand total is the absolute value 1 250.00.

records.name: The cumulated balance of a list of journal items
records.purpose: Produces the running total column of a list of Journal Items, so that the newest row of a list shows the closing balance of the ledger extract the user is looking at.

operands.name: balance of each displayed item
operands.source: the Journal Items that the current ordering and the current filter of the list select
operands.constraints: the whole ledger is not used: only the rows the list actually shows

operands.name: position of the item in the reversed ordering
operands.unit_or_currency: a whole number counted from one
operands.source: the displayed ordering of the list, read backwards
operands.constraints: one for the last displayed row, increasing towards the first displayed row

preconditions.condition: The list explicitly requests the running total column.
preconditions.otherwise: The value is zero for every row.

preconditions.condition: An ordering is defined for the list.
preconditions.otherwise: The running total is not meaningful, because it depends on the order.

procedure: Take the items in the reverse of the displayed ordering, so that the last displayed row comes first.
Walk that reversed sequence and keep a running sum of the balances.
Assign to each item the running sum up to and including it.
Show the values against the displayed ordering, so that the running total reads correctly from the bottom of the list upwards.
records.formula: cumulated_balance( item at position k ) = sum of balance over the items at positions 1 … k , where the positions follow the reverse of the displayed ordering

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: each balance is already at the precision of the company currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each balance.
rounding.step: No rounding step inside the accumulation.

result.name: cumulated balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as a column of the journal-item list; it is computed by the database over the current ordering and the current filter and is not stored.

edge_cases.case: The list does not request the column.
edge_cases.outcome: Every value is zero.

edge_cases.case: The filter of the list changes.
edge_cases.outcome: The running totals change with it, because the computation is over the filtered rows and not over the whole ledger.

edge_cases.case: The ordering of the list changes.
edge_cases.outcome: The running totals are recomputed against the new order.

worked_examples.description: Three items displayed in descending date order
worked_examples.narrative: Reversing the order gives plus 25, minus 40, plus 100, whose running totals are 25, minus 15 and 85; displayed newest first the column reads 85, minus 15, 25, so the newest row shows the closing balance.

records.name: The effective value of a soft lock date for a user
records.purpose: Computes the date up to and including which one soft lock closes the books for one acting user, taking the company chain and any exception granted to that user into account.

operands.name: company value of the lock date in each company of the chain
operands.source: the company of the entry and every ancestor company up to the root
operands.constraints: a company with no value for that lock date is skipped

operands.name: relaxed value of each candidate exception
operands.source: the active lock exceptions of that company for that lock date field
operands.constraints: must be strictly smaller than the company value; an exception that removes the lock date entirely counts as the smallest possible value

operands.name: beneficiary of each exception
operands.source: the lock exception record
operands.constraints: the exception is a candidate when its beneficiary is the acting user or nobody

preconditions.condition: The company of the entry and its chain of ancestors are known.
preconditions.otherwise: The effective value is the minimal representable date, that is nothing is locked.

preconditions.condition: The acting user is known.
preconditions.otherwise: Only exceptions whose beneficiary is nobody are candidates.

procedure: Start the running value at the minimal representable date.
Walk every company in the chain from the company of the entry up to the root company.
Skip a company that has no value for this lock date.
Otherwise look for an active exception of that company, for that lock date field, whose beneficiary is the acting user or nobody, and whose relaxed value is strictly smaller than the company value.
Among those candidates take the one with the smallest relaxed value, treating an exception that removes the lock date entirely as the smallest.
Take the relaxed value of that exception, or the minimal date when the exception removes the lock date entirely; take the company value when no such exception exists.
Keep the greater of the running value and the value just obtained.
Return the running value once the chain has been walked; performing the same walk with exceptions ignored gives the regular lock date.
records.formula: effective_soft_lock_date = maximum over the company and all its ancestors of ( the relaxed value of the smallest applicable exception , or the company value when there is none )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the values are whole dates.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: effective soft lock date for this user
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is the value against which a candidate date is tested and the value quoted in the refusal message.

edge_cases.case: No company in the chain has a value for the lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: The effective value stays at the minimal representable date and nothing is locked.

edge_cases.case: An exception relaxes the lock date to no value at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The minimal representable date is used for that company, which removes its contribution.

edge_cases.case: An exception whose relaxed value is not strictly smaller than the company value.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not a candidate and the company value is used.

edge_cases.case: A parent company locks later than the child.
edge_cases.outcome: The maximum is kept, so the stricter parent value wins.

worked_examples.description: A bookkeeper with an exception on the Global Lock Date

inputs.acting_user: the bookkeeper who holds the exception

worked_examples.narrative: The exception is active on the third of February, its relaxed value of 30 November 2025 is strictly smaller than the company value of 31 December 2025, so the effective value for that bookkeeper is 30 November 2025 while the regular value stays 31 December 2025.

worked_examples.description: A colleague without an exception, on the same company
worked_examples.narrative: No candidate exception exists, so the company value is taken unchanged.

records.name: The effective hard lock date
records.purpose: Computes the date up to and including which the books are closed irrevocably, which no exception and no user can relax.

operands.name: hard lock date of the company and of each of its ancestors
operands.source: the company of the entry and every ancestor company
operands.constraints: a company with no value contributes the minimal representable date

preconditions.condition: The company of the entry and its chain of ancestors are known.
preconditions.otherwise: The effective value is the minimal representable date.

procedure: Take the hard lock date of the company of the entry and of every ancestor company.
Return the greatest of those values.
Consult no exception at any point: the hard lock admits none.
records.formula: effective_hard_lock_date = maximum over the company and all its ancestors of their hard lock date

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the values are whole dates.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: effective hard lock date
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is the value against which a candidate date is tested, and it is quoted in the refusal message.

edge_cases.case: A user holds an exception on the hard lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: It is ignored: no exception is consulted.

edge_cases.case: No company of the chain sets a hard lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: The effective value is the minimal representable date and no entry is hard locked.

edge_cases.case: An attempt to lower the hard lock date of a company.
edge_cases.outcome: Refused: the hard lock date never decreases and is never cleared.

worked_examples.description: A single company that has closed the first half of the year irrevocably

expected_outputs.entry_dated_20_June_2025: refused for everybody, because 20 June is on or before the hard lock date and no exception can relax it
expected_outputs.entry_dated_15_December_2025: accepted, because 15 December is after the hard lock date

worked_examples.narrative: The maximum over the chain is 30 June 2025; a date on or before it is locked for every user without exception, and a later date is free of the hard lock.

records.name: The violation test for one soft lock date
records.purpose: Decides whether a candidate date falls inside a period closed by one soft lock for the acting user, and reports the date that closes it when it does.

operands.name: tested date
operands.source: the accounting date the entry is being given
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: regular lock date
operands.source: the effective value of the lock date computed with exceptions ignored
operands.constraints: may be the minimal representable date

operands.name: effective lock date
operands.source: the effective value of the lock date computed with the exceptions of the acting user applied
operands.constraints: smaller than or equal to the regular lock date

preconditions.condition: The lock date being tested applies to the entry: the Global Lock Date always; the Sales Lock Date only in a sale journal; the Purchase Lock Date only in a purchase journal; the Tax Return Lock Date only when the entry affects the tax report.
preconditions.otherwise: The lock is not consulted and there is no violation from it.

procedure: Compute the regular lock date with exceptions ignored.
When the tested date is strictly after the regular lock date, report no violation and stop.
Otherwise compute the effective lock date with the exceptions of the acting user applied.
When the tested date is strictly after the effective lock date, report no violation: the exception covers the user.
Otherwise report a violation whose date is the effective lock date, remembering that the comparison is on or before, so a date exactly equal to the lock date is locked.
records.formula:
violation = none                        when tested_date > regular_lock_date
violation = none                        when tested_date > effective_lock_date
violation = effective_lock_date         otherwise, the comparison being on or before

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the comparison is between whole dates.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the violated lock date, or nothing
result.unit_or_currency: a date, or the absence of one
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it enters the violation list of the entry, the refusal message and the accounting date rule.

edge_cases.case: The tested date is exactly the lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: It is locked: the comparison is on or before.

edge_cases.case: The user holds an exception that covers the tested date.
edge_cases.outcome: No violation, even though the regular lock date would have produced one.

edge_cases.case: The user holds an exception that does not reach far enough back.
edge_cases.outcome: A violation is reported and its date is the relaxed value, not the company value.

worked_examples.description: The bookkeeper with the exception, entering an entry dated 15 December 2025

expected_outputs.first_test: 15 December is not after 31 December, so the test continues

worked_examples.narrative: The regular lock date would close 15 December, but the exception relaxes the lock to 30 November, and 15 December is strictly after it, so the entry is accepted.

worked_examples.description: A colleague without an exception, entering the same entry
worked_examples.narrative: 15 December is on or before 31 December in both tests, so a violation is reported and its date is 31 December 2025.

records.name: The violation list of a journal entry
records.purpose: Collects every lock that closes the period of an entry, in the order in which they must be reported, so that the user is told which locks apply and the accounting date rule knows how far forward to push the entry.

operands.name: tested date
operands.source: the accounting date the entry is being given
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: journal kind of the entry
operands.source: the journal of the entry
operands.constraints: sale, purchase, bank, cash, credit card or miscellaneous

operands.name: whether the entry affects the tax report
operands.source: the items of the entry
operands.constraints: yes when at least one item carries a tax, is a tax line, or carries at least one tax grid

operands.name: effective hard lock date
operands.source: the hard lock computation
operands.constraints: no exception applies to it

preconditions.condition: The journal and the company of the entry are known.
preconditions.otherwise: Only the Global Lock Date and the Hard Lock Date can be consulted.

procedure: Run the soft violation test for the Global Lock Date, which applies to every entry.
Run it for the Sales Lock Date when the journal is a sale journal.
Run it for the Purchase Lock Date when the journal is a purchase journal.
Run it for the Tax Return Lock Date when the entry affects the tax report.
Add the Hard Lock Date when the tested date is on or before the effective hard lock date.
Sort the pairs of date and lock name chronologically.
Render the list for the user as a list of items of the shape label followed by the date in parentheses, joined by commas and the word and, in chronological order.
records.formula: violations = the chronologically sorted pairs ( violated date , lock name ) among the Global Lock Date, the Sales Lock Date (sale journals), the Purchase Lock Date (purchase journals), the Tax Return Lock Date (entries affecting the tax report) and the Hard Lock Date

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the values are whole dates.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the chronologically sorted list of violated locks
result.unit_or_currency: pairs of a date and a lock name
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is quoted in the refusal message, shown in the warning before posting and consumed by the accounting date rule.

edge_cases.case: No lock is violated.
edge_cases.outcome: The list is empty and the entry keeps its candidate date.

edge_cases.case: The entry is in a sale journal and affects the tax report.
edge_cases.outcome: Up to four soft locks are consulted, plus the hard lock.

edge_cases.case: Two locks are violated on the same date.
edge_cases.outcome: Both appear in the list; the chronological sort keeps them together.

worked_examples.description: An entry of a sale journal that carries a tax, dated inside two closed periods
worked_examples.narrative: The tested date of 15 June is on or before the three soft locks and after the hard lock, so three violations are reported in chronological order and the accounting date rule will move the entry to the day after 30 June 2026.

records.name: The fiscal lock date used for deletions and copies
records.purpose: Gives the single date, per journal, below which an entry may no longer be deleted or copied, by combining the locks that apply to that journal.

operands.name: effective Global Lock Date
operands.source: the soft lock computation for the acting user
operands.constraints: may be the minimal representable date

operands.name: effective Hard Lock Date
operands.source: the hard lock computation
operands.constraints: no exception applies to it

operands.name: effective Sales Lock Date
operands.source: the soft lock computation for the acting user
operands.constraints: consulted only for a sale journal

operands.name: effective Purchase Lock Date
operands.source: the soft lock computation for the acting user
operands.constraints: consulted only for a purchase journal

preconditions.condition: The journal is known, because the sales and purchase locks are consulted according to its kind.
preconditions.otherwise: Only the Global and the Hard Lock Dates enter the maximum.

procedure: Take the greater of the effective Global Lock Date and the effective Hard Lock Date.
When the journal is a sale journal, take the greater of that value and the effective Sales Lock Date.
When the journal is a purchase journal, take the greater of that value and the effective Purchase Lock Date.
Return the value obtained.
records.formula:
fiscal_lock_date( journal ) = max( effective Global Lock Date , effective Hard Lock Date )
fiscal_lock_date( sale journal )     = max( previous , effective Sales Lock Date )
fiscal_lock_date( purchase journal ) = max( previous , effective Purchase Lock Date )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the values are whole dates.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: fiscal lock date of the journal
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it guards deletion and copying, and it is the grouping key of the numbering-holes indicator when it is computed with exceptions ignored.

edge_cases.case: A miscellaneous journal.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the Global and the Hard Lock Dates enter the maximum.

edge_cases.case: The Tax Return Lock Date.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not enter this value; it is consulted only by the violation list of an entry.

edge_cases.case: No lock is set at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The value is the minimal representable date and nothing is blocked.

worked_examples.description: A sale journal in a company that closes globally at the end of June and for sales at the end of May
worked_examples.narrative: The greater of 30 June 2026 and 31 December 2025 is 30 June 2026, and the sales lock of 31 May 2026 does not raise it, so the fiscal lock date of the journal is 30 June 2026.

records.name: The accounting date rule for a sale document
records.purpose: Determines the accounting date a sale document takes when it is recorded, so that a sale document keeps its own date unless a lock forces a move and, when it does move, lands at the end of its numbering period or today, whichever comes first.

operands.name: candidate date
operands.source: the document date typed by the user, or the accounting date proposed for the entry
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: whether the entry affects the tax report
operands.source: the items of the entry
operands.constraints: drives whether the Tax Return Lock Date is consulted

operands.name: the list of violated lock dates
operands.unit_or_currency: pairs of a date and a lock name
operands.source: the violation list of the entry, computed for the candidate date unless it was supplied by the caller
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: the current date in the time zone of the user
operands.source: the clock, read in the time zone of the acting user
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: the highest number already used in the numbering chain of the entry
operands.source: the chain search, falling back to the relaxed search when the current period has no number
operands.constraints: may be absent when the chain is empty

preconditions.condition: The document is a sale document.
preconditions.otherwise: The rule for a purchase document, a plain entry or any other document applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The candidate date is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The current date is used as the candidate.

procedure: Compute the violated lock dates for the candidate date, unless the caller supplied them.
Let the current date in the time zone of the user be the value called today.

Let the highest number already used in the numbering chain of this entry be the value called the last number, falling back to the relaxed search, which accepts a number of a previous period, when the current period has none.
Deduce the reset periodicity from the last number.
When at least one lock date is violated, replace the candidate date with the day after the latest violated lock date.
When no lock date was violated, return the candidate date unchanged: a sale document keeps its own date.
Otherwise, when there is no last number at all or the periodicity is monthly, return the earlier of today and the last day of the month of the candidate date.
Otherwise, when the periodicity is yearly, return the earlier of today and the last day of the year of the candidate date.
Otherwise return the candidate date.
records.formula:
accounting_date = candidate_date                                                    when no lock date is violated
candidate_date  = the day after the latest violated lock date                       when at least one is violated
accounting_date = min( today , last day of the month of candidate_date )            when there is no last number, or the periodicity is monthly
accounting_date = min( today , last day of the year of candidate_date )             when the periodicity is yearly
accounting_date = candidate_date                                                    otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a whole date.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: accounting date of the sale document
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry as its accounting date, and used to pick the numbering period.

edge_cases.case: No lock is violated and the invoice date is in the past.
edge_cases.outcome: The invoice keeps its own date; sale documents are not pushed forward by the numbering alone.

edge_cases.case: The chain has no number at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The monthly branch is used, so the result is the earlier of today and the last day of the month of the candidate date.

edge_cases.case: The candidate date, after the lock shift, is later than today.
edge_cases.outcome: The earlier of the two is today only when today is earlier; a candidate later than today and inside the same period is returned as the end of the period or as today, whichever is earlier.

edge_cases.case: A violation exists at the moment the form is shown.
edge_cases.outcome: The form warns: the date is being set prior to the list of lock dates, and the Journal Entry will be accounted on the resulting accounting date upon posting.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice in the past with nothing locked
worked_examples.narrative: No lock date is violated, so the rule returns the candidate date unchanged: sale documents keep their own date unless a lock forces a move.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice in a locked period
worked_examples.narrative: The lock shift moves the candidate to 1 February; the yearly branch then returns the earlier of 10 March and 31 December, that is 10 March.

records.name: The accounting date rule for a purchase document, a plain entry or any other document
records.purpose: Determines the accounting date every document that is not a sale document takes when it is recorded, so that the numbering stays increasing and no closed period is touched even when the document itself is dated in the past.

operands.name: candidate date
operands.source: the document date typed by the user, or the accounting date proposed for the entry
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: whether the entry affects the tax report
operands.source: the items of the entry
operands.constraints: drives whether the Tax Return Lock Date is consulted

operands.name: the list of violated lock dates
operands.unit_or_currency: pairs of a date and a lock name
operands.source: the violation list of the entry, computed for the candidate date unless it was supplied by the caller
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: the current date in the time zone of the user
operands.source: the clock, read in the time zone of the acting user
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: the highest number already used in the numbering chain of the entry
operands.source: the chain search, falling back to the relaxed search when the current period has no number
operands.constraints: may be absent when the chain is empty

preconditions.condition: The document is not a sale document: it is a purchase document, a plain entry or anything else.
preconditions.otherwise: The rule for a sale document applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The candidate date is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The current date is used as the candidate.

procedure: Compute the violated lock dates for the candidate date, unless the caller supplied them.
Let the current date in the time zone of the user be the value called today.
Let the highest number already used in the numbering chain of this entry be the value called the last number, falling back to the relaxed search when the current period has none.
Deduce the reset periodicity from the last number.
When at least one lock date is violated, replace the candidate date with the day after the latest violated lock date.

When there is no last number at all, or the periodicity is monthly or year-range-monthly: return the last day of the month of the candidate date if the year and month of today are later than the year and month of the candidate date, and otherwise return the later of the candidate date and today.

When the periodicity is yearly: return the thirty-first of December of the year of the candidate date if the year of today is later than the year of the candidate date, and otherwise return the later of the candidate date and today.
Otherwise return the candidate date.
records.formula:
candidate_date  = the day after the latest violated lock date                                when at least one lock date is violated
accounting_date = last day of the month of candidate_date                                  when there is no last number, or the periodicity is monthly or year-range-monthly, and ( year , month ) of today is later than ( year , month ) of candidate_date
accounting_date = max( candidate_date , today )                                            in the same periodicities otherwise
accounting_date = the thirty-first of December of the year of candidate_date               when the periodicity is yearly and the year of today is later than the year of candidate_date
accounting_date = max( candidate_date , today )                                            when the periodicity is yearly otherwise
accounting_date = candidate_date                                                           otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a whole date.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: accounting date of the document
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry as its accounting date, and used to pick the numbering period.

edge_cases.case: The document date is in the current month.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry is dated today rather than at its document date, because the numbering of the current month is already in use.

edge_cases.case: The candidate date falls in a locked period.
edge_cases.outcome: It is first moved to the day after the latest violated lock date, and only then pushed forward by the periodicity branch.

edge_cases.case: The month of the candidate date has twenty-eight or twenty-nine days.
edge_cases.outcome: The last day of the month is used as it falls in that year, so February gives 28 February or 29 February in a leap year.

edge_cases.case: A violation exists at the moment the form is shown.
edge_cases.outcome: The form warns: the date is being set prior to the list of lock dates, and the Journal Entry will be accounted on the resulting accounting date upon posting.

worked_examples.description: A late vendor bill

inputs.journal: a purchase journal numbering monthly that already has January numbers

worked_examples.narrative: March is later than January, so the monthly branch returns the last day of the month of the candidate date, that is 31 January; the bill is numbered in the January chain and lands in the January period.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill of the current month
worked_examples.narrative: March 2026 is not later than March 2026, so the rule returns the later of 3 March and 10 March, that is 10 March: the bill is dated today, not at its document date, because the March numbering is already in use.

worked_examples.description: A vendor bill in a locked period

expected_outputs.accounting_date: 28 February, or 29 February in a leap year

worked_examples.narrative: The lock shift moves the candidate to 1 February; the monthly branch then sees that March is later than February and returns the last day of February.

records.name: The decomposition of a document number by the five shapes
records.purpose: Reads a document number as a sequence of named parts, which is what lets the system recognise the period a number belongs to, rebuild the next number of the chain and refuse a number that is not aligned with its date.

operands.name: document number
operands.source: the number stored on a Journal Entry
operands.constraints: not the placeholder and not empty

operands.name: the numbering pattern override of the journal
operands.unit_or_currency: a pattern over the named parts
operands.source: the journal, when it defines one
operands.constraints: when present it replaces all five shapes and may define the parts named first prefix, year, second prefix, month, third prefix, counter and suffix

preconditions.condition: The number is not the placeholder and is not empty.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to read and the entry is treated as having no number.

preconditions.condition: At least one of the five shapes, or the override of the journal, reads the number.
preconditions.otherwise: The reading fails with the message that the sequence pattern should at least contain the counter grouping keys, followed by the example pattern.

procedure: Name the parts: the first prefix is any characters, as few as possible; the year is either four digits beginning with nineteen, twenty or twenty-one, or exactly two digits followed by a non-digit, and is preceded either by a non-digit or by the start of the number; the end year has the same shape and is used for a year range; the second prefix is one non-digit, or in some shapes zero or more non-digits, as few as possible; the third prefix is one or more non-digits, as few as possible; the month is two digits from zero one to one two; the counter is a run of digits; the suffix is zero or more non-digits, as few as possible.

Try the year-range-monthly shape: first prefix, year, one non-digit, end year, one non-digit, month, one or more non-digits, counter, suffix; its required parts are the counter, the year, the end year and the month.
Try the monthly shape: first prefix, year, zero or more non-digits, month, one or more non-digits, counter, suffix; its required parts are the counter, the month and the year.

Try the year-range shape: optionally a first prefix, a year, one non-digit, an end year and one or more non-digits, then the counter and the suffix; its required parts are the counter, the year and the end year.
Try the yearly shape: first prefix, a two- or four-digit year, one or more non-digits, counter, suffix; its required part list is the counter and the year.
