Try the fixed shape: first prefix, up to nine digits as the counter, suffix; its only required part is the counter, and the limit of nine digits is what caps the counter width.
When the journal defines a numbering pattern override, use it instead of all five shapes.
records.formula: number = first_prefix + year + second_prefix + end_year + third_prefix + month + counter + suffix , the parts present depending on which of the five shapes reads the number, tried in the order year range monthly, monthly, year range, yearly, fixed

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the parts are read as text and converted to whole numbers.
rounding.precision: The counter, the year, the end year and the month are whole numbers; a part that is absent is read as zero.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the named parts of the number
result.unit_or_currency: text for the prefixes and the suffix, whole numbers for the counter, the year, the end year and the month
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored as such; the parts drive the periodicity deduction, the format extraction and the date-alignment test.

edge_cases.case: A number of only text, such as three letters.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the fixed shape reads it, and its counter is empty.

edge_cases.case: A counter of more than nine digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The fixed shape caps the counter at nine digits, which is what limits the counter width.

edge_cases.case: The journal defines a numbering pattern override.
edge_cases.outcome: The override replaces all five shapes, and the prefix exclusion of the chain search is switched off.

worked_examples.description: A number of the year-range-monthly shape
worked_examples.narrative: The first shape tried reads the year twenty-five, the end year twenty-six, the month eleven and the counter one, and all four required parts are present, so it is the shape that wins.

worked_examples.description: A number of the monthly shape
worked_examples.narrative: The year-range-monthly shape does not fit because there is no end year, so the monthly shape reads the year two thousand and twenty-six, the month three and the counter seven.

records.name: The numbering prefix and the counter stored on an entry
records.purpose: Produces the two values stored on every Journal Entry that make the chain searchable: the text before the counter and the counter itself as a whole number.

operands.name: document number
operands.source: the number stored on the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: may be empty, may be the placeholder

preconditions.condition: The number is read with the fixed shape only, independently of the shape that gave the periodicity.
preconditions.otherwise: The two stored values would not be comparable between entries of different periodicities.

procedure: Read the number with the fixed shape: a first prefix, up to nine digits as the counter, and a suffix.
Store as the numbering prefix the part of the number that comes before the counter.
Read the counter as a whole number and store it as the sequence number.
Store zero as the sequence number when the number carries no counter.
records.formula:
sequence_prefix = the part of the number before the counter
sequence_number = the counter read as an integer, or 0 when there is none

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counter is read as a whole number.
rounding.precision: A whole number; leading zeros are dropped by the reading and restored by the format when the number is rebuilt.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the numbering prefix and the sequence number of the entry
result.unit_or_currency: a text and a whole number
result.stored_or_displayed: Both are stored on the Journal Entry; they are the ordering keys of the chain search, of the gap detection and of the hash verification.

edge_cases.case: The number is the placeholder, a single oblique stroke.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix is that stroke and the sequence number is zero.

edge_cases.case: The number is only digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix is empty and the sequence number is the digits read as a whole number.

edge_cases.case: The number is only text with no digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix is the whole text and the sequence number is zero.

worked_examples.description: The six decompositions the document lists
worked_examples.narrative: In every case the prefix is everything before the trailing run of digits and the counter is that run read as a whole number; a number with no digits at all, such as the placeholder, has a counter of zero.

records.name: Deducing the reset periodicity from a reference number
records.purpose: Decides at which rhythm the counter of a chain restarts, which fixes the period boundaries of the chain search, the branch of the accounting date rule and the partition used when entries are renumbered.

operands.name: reference number
operands.source: the previous number of the chain, or the first number given to a renumbering operation
operands.constraints: not the placeholder and not empty

preconditions.condition: At least one of the five shapes reads the reference number.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation is refused with the message "The sequence regex should at least contain the seq grouping keys. For instance:" followed by the example pattern.

procedure: Take the five shapes in the order year range monthly, monthly, year range, yearly, fixed.
Try to read the reference number with the shape; when it does not fit, continue with the next shape.
When the shape produced both a year and an end year, reject the shape when the end year is written with more characters than the year.
When the shape produced both a year and an end year, reject the shape when the year plus one, truncated to the number of characters of the end year, is not equal to the end year.
When every required part of the shape is present, return the periodicity of that shape: year range monthly, month, year range, year or never.
When no shape fits, raise the refusal message.
records.formula: periodicity = the periodicity of the first of the five shapes, tried in the order year range monthly, monthly, year range, yearly, fixed, that reads the reference number, has all its required parts, and — when it produced a year and an end year — satisfies truncate( year + 1 , length of the end year ) = end_year and length of the end year ≤ length of the year

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the year consistency test uses the remainder of a division, not a rounding.
rounding.precision: Whole numbers.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: reset periodicity
result.unit_or_currency: one of year range monthly, month, year range, year, never
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it drives the period boundaries, the accounting date rule, the resequencing partition and the date-alignment test.

edge_cases.case: A number whose year range is not consecutive, such as twenty-five to twenty-seven.
edge_cases.outcome: The year-range shape is rejected because twenty-five plus one is twenty-six and not twenty-seven; the next shape that fits is used.

edge_cases.case: A number made only of digits.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the fixed shape fits and the periodicity is never.

edge_cases.case: A number made only of letters.
edge_cases.outcome: The fixed shape fits with an empty counter and the periodicity is never.

edge_cases.case: A number that no shape reads.
edge_cases.outcome: The refusal message is raised.

worked_examples.description: The six reference numbers the document lists
worked_examples.narrative: For the first number the monthly shape would need a month of two digits after the year, and the counter zero zero zero four two read as zero zero plus zero four two does not satisfy the month range and the required parts, so the yearly shape wins; for the third, twenty-five plus one truncated to two characters equals twenty-six, so the year-range-monthly shape is accepted; for the fourth, twenty-five plus one is twenty-six and not twenty-seven, so the year-range shape is rejected and the yearly shape reads the year twenty-five; the last two are read only by the fixed shape.

records.name: Truncating a year to a number of characters
records.purpose: Reduces a full year to the number of digits it occupies inside a document number, which is what lets a two-digit year range be compared with a four-digit calendar year.

operands.name: year
operands.source: a calendar year, or the start or end year of a period
operands.constraints: a non-negative whole number

operands.name: length
operands.source: the number of characters the year occupies inside the reference number
operands.constraints: a positive whole number, in practice two or four

preconditions.condition: The length is known from the reference number.
preconditions.otherwise: The year is used unchanged.

procedure: Raise ten to the power of the length.
Take the remainder of the division of the year by that power of ten.
Use the remainder wherever the truncated year is required: in the year-range consistency test, in the forced year values of a new chain, in the resequencing partition and in the date-alignment test.
records.formula: truncate( year , length ) = year modulo 10^length

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the operation is a remainder, not a rounding.
rounding.precision: A whole number of at most the given number of digits.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: truncated year
result.unit_or_currency: a whole number of at most the given number of digits
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is written into the year field of a rebuilt number and compared in the consistency and alignment tests.

edge_cases.case: The length is four and the year is four digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder is the year itself.

edge_cases.case: The length is two.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the last two digits survive, so the year two thousand and twenty-six becomes twenty-six.

edge_cases.case: A year range crossing a century.
edge_cases.outcome: The truncation keeps the two last digits on both sides, so ninety-nine and zero are consecutive in the two-digit reading.

worked_examples.description: The consistency test of the year range twenty-five to twenty-six
worked_examples.narrative: Twenty-five plus one is twenty-six; twenty-six modulo one hundred is twenty-six, which equals the end year, so the year-range reading is accepted.

worked_examples.description: The consistency test of the year range twenty-five to twenty-seven
worked_examples.narrative: Twenty-six is not twenty-seven, so the year-range shape is rejected and the next shape is tried.

records.name: Extracting the format and the values from a previous number
records.purpose: Turns a previous document number into a template with holes and a set of whole-number values, so that filling the template with the values reproduces the previous number exactly and increasing the counter produces the next one.

operands.name: previous number
operands.source: the previous number of the chain, or the starting number of a fresh chain
operands.constraints: not the placeholder and not empty

operands.name: deduced periodicity
operands.unit_or_currency: one of year range monthly, month, year range, year, never
operands.source: the periodicity deduction applied to the same number
operands.constraints: fixes the shape used to read the number a second time

preconditions.condition: The periodicity has been deduced from the same number.
preconditions.otherwise: The shape to read the number with is unknown and the extraction cannot run.

procedure: Read the previous number with the shape of the deduced periodicity.
Record the length of the counter, the length of the year and the length of the end year exactly as they appear in the previous number.

When the shape produced no counter but did produce a first prefix and a suffix, move the suffix into the first prefix and empty the suffix, because a number that is only text is a prefix and not a suffix.
Convert the counter, the year, the month and the end year to whole numbers, using zero when the part is absent.

Build the template by walking the parts of the shape in order and emitting, for the counter, a field padded with zeros to the recorded counter length; for the month, a field padded with zeros to two characters; for the year, a field padded with zeros to the recorded year length; for the end year, a field padded with zeros to the recorded end-year length; and for every prefix or suffix part, the part itself.
Check the invariant on which the whole numbering relies: filling the template with the values reproduces the previous number exactly.
records.formula:
template = the parts of the shape in order, each variable part replaced by a field padded with zeros to its recorded length
values   = ( counter , year , end year , month ) read as whole numbers, zero when absent
fill( template , values ) = previous_number

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the values are whole numbers and the padding restores the original widths.
rounding.precision: The counter carries the recorded counter length, the month two characters, the year and the end year their recorded lengths.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the template and the values of the number
result.unit_or_currency: a template of text and fields, and whole numbers
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; they are the working values of the next-number assignment, the chain-end test, the resequencing and the proposed number shown before posting.

edge_cases.case: The previous number has no counter at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The suffix is moved into the first prefix and emptied, so the template is a pure prefix followed by a counter field.

edge_cases.case: The counter of the previous number carries leading zeros.
edge_cases.outcome: The recorded counter length preserves them, so the rebuilt number keeps the same width.

edge_cases.case: The number carries no month.
edge_cases.outcome: The month value is zero and no month field is emitted.

worked_examples.description: A monthly number of a purchase journal

expected_outputs.template: BILL/ then the year on four digits then / then the month on two digits then / then the counter on four digits

worked_examples.narrative: The parts are the first prefix, the year, the second prefix, the month, the third prefix and the counter, with an empty suffix; the recorded lengths are four for the counter and four for the year; filling the template with the year two thousand and twenty-six, the month three and the counter seven gives back the previous number exactly.

records.name: Finding the previous number of a numbering chain
records.purpose: Locates the number from which the next one is derived, by restricting the search to the entries that share the chain of the entry being numbered and taking the greatest counter among those that share the prefix of the most recently created entry.

operands.name: the entry being numbered
operands.source: the entry whose number is being assigned or proposed
operands.constraints: carries a journal, a document type and an accounting date

operands.name: the relaxed flag
operands.source: the caller: the strict search is used first and the relaxed search only when the strict one finds nothing
operands.constraints: when it is set, the restriction to the period is dropped

operands.name: the numbers of the candidate entries
operands.source: the entries of the same journal whose number is neither the placeholder nor empty
operands.constraints: the entry being numbered is excluded

operands.name: the identifier of each candidate entry
operands.source: the entries considered
operands.constraints: used to find the most recently created entry

preconditions.condition: The journal of the entry is known.
preconditions.otherwise: No chain can be built and the starting number of a fresh chain is used.

preconditions.condition: For a self-billing journal, the entry has a commercial counterpart.
preconditions.otherwise: The restriction is made impossible so that a fresh chain is started.

procedure: Restrict the search to the same journal, to entries whose number is neither the placeholder nor empty, and exclude the entry being numbered.
When the journal has a dedicated credit-note numbering, restrict to credit notes if the entry is one and to non-credit-notes otherwise.
When the journal has a dedicated payment numbering, restrict to entries of a payment if the entry being numbered is one, and to entries that are not otherwise.
When the journal is a self-billing journal, restrict to the same commercial counterpart, and make the restriction impossible when the entry has no counterpart yet.

When the flag is not relaxed, take the number of the latest entry of the chain dated on or before the entry date, or the number of the earliest entry of the chain when there is none, deduce the periodicity from that number, compute the period boundaries for that periodicity and restrict the search to entries dated within them.

When the flag is not relaxed, exclude the prefixes belonging to a finer periodicity: for the yearly or year-range periodicities exclude every prefix that the monthly shape can read up to the counter; for the fixed periodicity exclude every prefix that the yearly shape can read up to the counter, which also excludes the monthly, year-range and year-range-monthly prefixes; for the monthly and year-range-monthly periodicities exclude nothing; and switch the exclusion off entirely when the journal overrides the grammar.
Among the remaining entries take the prefix of the one with the highest identifier, that is the most recently created one.
Among the entries with that prefix return the number with the highest counter.
records.formula: previous_number = the number with the greatest counter among the entries of the chain whose prefix equals the prefix of the entry of the chain with the greatest identifier

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the search compares whole counters and texts.
rounding.precision: Whole numbers for the counters.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: previous number of the chain
result.unit_or_currency: a text, or the absence of one
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is the input of the format extraction and therefore of the next number, and its absence marks the chain as new.

edge_cases.case: The strict search finds nothing.
edge_cases.outcome: The chain is marked as new and the search is run again with the relaxed flag, which accepts a number of a previous period.

edge_cases.case: Both searches find nothing.
edge_cases.outcome: The starting number of a fresh chain is used.

edge_cases.case: A user has manually created a number with a different prefix.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix of the most recently created entry wins, so the chain follows the manual prefix rather than the alphabetically greatest one.

edge_cases.case: The journal overrides the numbering grammar.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix exclusion is switched off.

worked_examples.description: A manually created number that changes the prefix of a sale chain

inputs.entry_being_numbered: the next invoice of the same period

worked_examples.narrative: The most recently created entry is the manual one, whose prefix is FACT followed by the year, so the next number continues that prefix; had the search compared numbers alphabetically it would have produced the third number of the other prefix, because those letters sort later, and the rule is deliberately the prefix of the newest entry and not the alphabetically greatest one.

records.name: The period boundaries of a numbering periodicity
records.purpose: Gives the two dates between which the entries of one numbering period fall, which is what restricts the chain search and what fixes the year and month values forced into a rebuilt number.

operands.name: periodicity
operands.unit_or_currency: one of never, month, year, year range, year range monthly
operands.source: the periodicity deduced from the reference number
operands.constraints: one of the five values

operands.name: entry date
operands.source: the accounting date of the entry being numbered
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: the fiscal year end day and month of the company
operands.unit_or_currency: a day of a month, and a month
operands.source: the company of the entry
operands.constraints: used for the two year-range periodicities

preconditions.condition: The entry date is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The boundaries cannot be computed and the whole representable range is used.

preconditions.condition: For a year-range periodicity, the fiscal year end of the company is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The thirty-first of December is used, which makes the fiscal year the calendar year.

procedure: For the periodicity never, take the first representable day and the last representable day.
For the monthly periodicity, take the first and the last day of the month of the entry date.
For the yearly periodicity, take the first of January and the thirty-first of December of the year of the entry date.
For the year-range periodicity, take the first and the last day of the fiscal year of the company that contains the entry date.

For the year-range-monthly periodicity, take the month of the entry date and cut it at the fiscal year boundary: when the day of the entry is at most the fiscal year end day, the range runs from the first of the month to that end day; when the day of the entry is after the end day, the range runs from the day after the end day to the last day of the month.
In both year-range cases force, as the year and the end year of the number, the years of the fiscal year that contains the entry date.
records.formula:
boundaries( never )              = the first representable day … the last representable day
boundaries( month )              = the first day of the month of the entry date … the last day of that month
boundaries( year )               = the first of January … the thirty-first of December of the year of the entry date
boundaries( year range )         = the first day … the last day of the fiscal year containing the entry date
boundaries( year range monthly ) = the first of the month … day D            when the entry day ≤ D
boundaries( year range monthly ) = day D + 1 … the last day of the month     when the entry day > D , where D is the fiscal year end day and the entry falls in the fiscal year end month M

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the boundaries are whole dates.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the first and the last day of the numbering period, and the forced year range
result.unit_or_currency: two dates and, for the year-range periodicities, two years
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; the two dates restrict the chain search and the two years are written into the rebuilt number.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year ends inside the month of the entry, and the entry falls on or before the end day.
edge_cases.outcome: The period runs from the first of the month to the end day, so the last days of the month belong to the next fiscal year.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year ends inside the month of the entry, and the entry falls after the end day.
edge_cases.outcome: The period runs from the day after the end day to the last day of the month.

edge_cases.case: The periodicity is never.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole representable range is used, so the chain has one single period.

worked_examples.description: A year-range-monthly chain in a company whose fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of March
worked_examples.narrative: The entry day, the third, is at most the fiscal year end day, the thirty-first, so the range runs from the first of March to the thirty-first of March, and the years forced into the number are those of the fiscal year running from April two thousand and twenty-five to March two thousand and twenty-six.

worked_examples.description: A monthly chain
worked_examples.narrative: The month of the entry date is February two thousand and twenty-six, which has twenty-eight days in that year.

records.name: The starting number of a fresh chain in a sale or liquidity journal
records.purpose: Composes the synthetic number, with a counter of zero, from which the first entry of a sale, bank, cash or credit-card journal takes the number one; such a journal numbers yearly by default.

operands.name: the reference date
operands.source: the accounting date of the entry, falling back to the document date, falling back to the current date
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: journal code
operands.source: the short code of the journal
operands.constraints: reproduced exactly in the number

operands.name: fiscal year end day and month of the company
operands.unit_or_currency: a day of a month, and a month
operands.source: the company of the entry
operands.constraints: decides between a four-digit year and a two-digit year range

operands.name: whether the journal has a dedicated credit-note numbering
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: adds a leading letter when the document is a credit note

operands.name: whether the journal has a dedicated payment numbering
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: adds a leading letter when the entry is the entry of a payment

preconditions.condition: No previous number exists in the chain, neither under the strict search nor under the relaxed one.
preconditions.otherwise: The previous number found is used and no starting number is composed.

preconditions.condition: The journal is a sale, bank, cash or credit-card journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The self-billing composition or the ordinary composition applies instead.

procedure: Take the accounting date, falling back to the document date, falling back to the current date, and call it the reference date.
When the fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of December, the year part is the four digits of the year of the reference date.

Otherwise let the last day be the fiscal-year end day, capped at the number of days of the fiscal-year end month in the year of the reference date; when the reference date is after the date made of the year of the reference date, the fiscal end month and that last day, the year part is the two digits of the year of the reference date, a hyphen and the two digits of the following year; otherwise it is the two digits of the previous year, a hyphen and the two digits of the year of the reference date.

Compose the number as the journal code, an oblique stroke, the year part, an oblique stroke, and then four zeros for a staggered fiscal year or five zeros otherwise; the counter is shortened to four digits for a staggered fiscal year because the year part is then six characters instead of four.
Prefix the result with the letter R when the journal has a dedicated credit-note numbering and the document is a credit note.
Prefix the result with the letter P when the journal has a dedicated payment numbering and the document is the entry of a payment.
records.formula:
starting_number = [ R ] [ P ] + journal_code + "/" + year_part + "/" + ( "0000" for a staggered fiscal year, otherwise "00000" )
first_number_assigned = the same number with the counter increased by one

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counter is a whole number padded with zeros.
rounding.precision: Four digits of counter for a staggered fiscal year, five otherwise; two digits per year in a year range, four digits for a calendar year.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the starting number of the chain
result.unit_or_currency: a text whose counter is zero
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is the input of the format extraction, so that the first number actually assigned carries the counter one.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year ends on the twenty-ninth of February and the reference year is not a leap year.
edge_cases.outcome: The end day is capped at the number of days of that month in that year, that is the twenty-eighth.

edge_cases.case: The document is a credit note in a journal with a dedicated credit-note numbering.
edge_cases.outcome: The letter R is placed in front of the journal code, so the credit notes form their own chain.

edge_cases.case: The entry is the entry of a payment in a journal with a dedicated payment numbering.
edge_cases.outcome: The letter P is placed in front, so the payments form their own chain.

worked_examples.description: The first invoice of a sale journal whose company closes on the thirty-first of December
worked_examples.narrative: The fiscal year is the calendar year, so the year part is four digits and the counter is five digits; the first number assigned carries the counter one.

worked_examples.description: The first credit note of the same journal, which has a dedicated credit-note numbering
worked_examples.narrative: The letter R is placed in front of the journal code, which separates the credit notes from the invoices.

worked_examples.description: The first payment of a bank journal in a company whose fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of March
worked_examples.narrative: The third of March is not after the thirty-first of March of the same year, so the year part is the two digits of the previous year, a hyphen and the two digits of the year of the reference date; the counter is shortened to four digits because the year part is six characters, and the letter P marks the payment chain.

records.name: The starting number of a fresh chain in a self-billing journal
records.purpose: Composes the synthetic number of a self-billing journal, where each commercial counterpart has its own monthly chain, so that the numbering of one counterpart is independent of every other.

operands.name: the reference date
operands.source: the accounting date of the entry, falling back to the document date, falling back to the current date
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: journal code
operands.source: the short code of the journal
operands.constraints: reproduced exactly in the number

operands.name: identifier of the commercial counterpart
operands.source: the counterpart of the entry
operands.constraints: padded with zeros to five characters; when the entry has no counterpart yet the literal text "[Partner id]" is used in its place

operands.name: fiscal year end day and month of the company
operands.unit_or_currency: a day of a month, and a month
operands.source: the company of the entry
operands.constraints: decides between a four-digit year and a two-digit year range

preconditions.condition: No previous number exists in the chain, neither under the strict search nor under the relaxed one.
preconditions.otherwise: The previous number found is used.

preconditions.condition: The journal is a self-billing journal and is not a sale, bank, cash or credit-card journal.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two compositions applies.

procedure: Take the accounting date, falling back to the document date, falling back to the current date, and call it the reference date.

Compute the year part exactly as for any other journal: four digits of the year of the reference date when the fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of December, and otherwise the two-digit year range of the fiscal year that contains the reference date.

Compose the number as the journal code, then the counterpart identifier padded with zeros to five characters, an oblique stroke, the year part, an oblique stroke, the month of the reference date on two digits, an oblique stroke and four zeros.
Use the literal text "[Partner id]" in place of the identifier when the entry has no counterpart yet.

Prefix the result with the letter R when the journal has a dedicated credit-note numbering and the document is a credit note, and with the letter P when the journal has a dedicated payment numbering and the entry is the entry of a payment.
records.formula: starting_number = [ R ] [ P ] + journal_code + counterpart_identifier padded with zeros to five characters + "/" + year_part + "/" + month on two digits + "/0000"

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counter and the counterpart identifier are whole numbers padded with zeros.
rounding.precision: Four digits of counter, two digits of month, five digits of counterpart identifier.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the starting number of the chain of that counterpart
result.unit_or_currency: a text whose counter is zero
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is the input of the format extraction, so that the first number of that counterpart carries the counter one.

edge_cases.case: The entry has no commercial counterpart yet.
edge_cases.outcome: The literal text "[Partner id]" is used in place of the identifier, and the chain restriction of the search is made impossible so that a fresh chain is started.

edge_cases.case: The counterpart identifier is longer than five digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The padding adds nothing and the identifier is written in full.

edge_cases.case: The company has a staggered fiscal year.
edge_cases.outcome: The year part is the two-digit year range of the fiscal year containing the reference date.

worked_examples.description: The first self-billed document of a counterpart whose identifier is forty-two, in a company closing on the thirty-first of December
worked_examples.narrative: The composition rule places the counterpart identifier padded to five characters immediately after the journal code, then the year part, then the month on two digits, then a counter of four zeros; the first number assigned carries the counter one.

worked_examples.description: The same journal before a counterpart has been chosen
worked_examples.narrative: The literal text is used in place of the identifier, and the chain restriction is made impossible so that a fresh chain will be started once the counterpart is known.

records.name: The starting number of a fresh chain in any other journal
records.purpose: Composes the synthetic number of every journal that is neither a sale or liquidity journal nor a self-billing journal, which therefore numbers monthly by default.

operands.source: the accounting date of the entry, falling back to the document date, falling back to the current date
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: journal code
operands.source: the short code of the journal
operands.constraints: reproduced exactly in the number

operands.name: fiscal year end day and month of the company
operands.unit_or_currency: a day of a month, and a month
operands.source: the company of the entry
operands.constraints: decides between a four-digit year and a two-digit year range

preconditions.condition: No previous number exists in the chain, neither under the strict search nor under the relaxed one.
preconditions.otherwise: The previous number found is used.

preconditions.condition: The journal is neither a sale, bank, cash or credit-card journal, nor a self-billing journal.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two compositions applies.

procedure: Take the accounting date, falling back to the document date, falling back to the current date, and call it the reference date.
When the fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of December, the year part is the four digits of the year of the reference date.

Otherwise let the last day be the fiscal-year end day, capped at the number of days of the fiscal-year end month in the year of the reference date; when the reference date is after the date made of the year of the reference date, the fiscal end month and that last day, the year part is the two digits of the year of the reference date, a hyphen and the two digits of the following year; otherwise it is the two digits of the previous year, a hyphen and the two digits of the year of the reference date.
Compose the number as the journal code, an oblique stroke, the year part, an oblique stroke, the month of the reference date on two digits, an oblique stroke and four zeros.

Prefix the result with the letter R when the journal has a dedicated credit-note numbering and the document is a credit note, and with the letter P when the journal has a dedicated payment numbering and the entry is the entry of a payment.
records.formula: starting_number = [ R ] [ P ] + journal_code + "/" + year_part + "/" + month on two digits + "/0000"

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counter and the month are whole numbers padded with zeros.
rounding.precision: Four digits of counter and two digits of month; two digits per year in a year range, four digits for a calendar year.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the starting number of the chain
result.unit_or_currency: a text whose counter is zero

edge_cases.case: The company has a staggered fiscal year.
edge_cases.outcome: The year part becomes a two-digit year range, and the number therefore carries a six-character year part with a four-digit counter.

edge_cases.case: The reference date falls after the fiscal year end inside the same calendar year.
edge_cases.outcome: The year range runs from the year of the reference date to the following year.

edge_cases.case: The reference date falls on or before the fiscal year end.
edge_cases.outcome: The year range runs from the previous year to the year of the reference date.

worked_examples.description: The first entry of a miscellaneous journal in a company closing on the thirty-first of December
worked_examples.narrative: The fiscal year is the calendar year, so the year part is four digits, the month is written on two digits and the counter on four.

worked_examples.description: The same journal in a company closing on the thirty-first of March, for a date before the close
worked_examples.narrative: The third of March is not after the thirty-first of March, so the year range is the two digits of the previous year, a hyphen and the two digits of the current year.

worked_examples.description: The same journal in the same company, for a date after the close
worked_examples.narrative: The third of April is after the thirty-first of March, so the year range is the two digits of the year of the reference date, a hyphen and the two digits of the following year.

records.name: Assigning the next number of a chain under concurrency
records.purpose: Produces the number an entry takes at posting and guarantees, without a counter table, that two users posting at the same instant neither skip a number nor duplicate one.

operands.name: the previous number of the chain
operands.source: the strict chain search, then the relaxed one, then the starting number of a fresh chain
operands.constraints: the first of the three that yields a value is used

operands.name: the template and the values extracted from that number
operands.unit_or_currency: a template of text and fields, and whole numbers
operands.source: the format extraction
operands.constraints: filling the template with the values reproduces the previous number

operands.name: the period boundaries and the forced year range
operands.source: the period boundaries of the deduced periodicity
operands.constraints: used only when the chain is new

operands.name: the accounting date of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: supplies the month value when the chain is new

preconditions.condition: The entry satisfies the partial condition of the uniqueness index: it is posted and its number differs from the placeholder.
preconditions.otherwise: The exclusive lock on the index entry is not taken, which is why numbering happens as part of the write that sets the state to posted.

preconditions.condition: The journal of the entry is known.
preconditions.otherwise: No chain can be identified.

procedure: Find the previous number of the chain with the relaxed flag off.
When none was found, mark the chain as new and find the previous number again with the relaxed flag on; when that also fails, use the starting number of a fresh chain.
Extract the template and the values from the number obtained.

When the chain is new, deduce the periodicity from that number, compute the period boundaries and the forced year range, set the counter value to zero, set the year value to the start year of the period truncated to the recorded year length, set the end year value to the end year of the period truncated likewise, and set the month value to the month of the entry date.
Build a cache key from the template filled with a counter of zero and from the grouping value of the entry, which is its journal.
When that key is already in the transaction cache, increase the cached counter, return the number built from it, and touch the database not at all.

Otherwise open a savepoint and loop: increase the counter by one, build the candidate number, write it directly into the number column of this entry; when the write succeeds, remember the counter in the transaction cache and return the candidate; when the write violates the uniqueness constraint, roll back to the savepoint and loop again.
Store the number on the record, schedule the recomputation of every stored computed field that depends on it, and recompute the numbering prefix and the counter.
records.formula:
next_number = fill( template , values with counter = previous counter + 1 )
repeated with counter increased by one on each uniqueness violation until the direct write succeeds

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counter is a whole number and the padding restores its width.
rounding.precision: The recorded counter length of the chain.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the number assigned to the entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Written directly into the number column of the Journal Entry, and shown as the legal number of the document.

edge_cases.case: Two transactions try the same candidate number.
edge_cases.outcome: The direct write takes an exclusive lock on the index entry, so the second transaction blocks until the first commits or rolls back, then discovers the conflict and retries with the next value; correctness comes from the unique index and not from a counter table.

edge_cases.case: Several numbers of the same chain are taken in one transaction.
edge_cases.outcome: After the first lock the further numbers come from the in-memory counter of the transaction cache, because opening one savepoint per number would be prohibitively slow; the cache is cleared whenever the number field is written by an ordinary write.

edge_cases.case: The chain is new.
edge_cases.outcome: The counter is reset to zero and the year, end year and month values are forced from the period, so the first number of the period carries the counter one.

worked_examples.description: Two users posting an invoice at the same instant on a chain that has reached the counter seven

inputs.template: INV/ then the year on four digits then / then the counter on five digits

expected_outputs.second_transaction_outcome: uniqueness violation, roll back to the savepoint, retry

worked_examples.narrative: Both read the previous number and both build the same template with the counter seven; the first writes the counter eight and holds the index lock; the second tries the counter eight, blocks, receives a uniqueness violation when the first commits, rolls back to its savepoint and succeeds with the counter nine, so no number is skipped and no number is duplicated.

records.name: Whether an entry is the last of its numbering chain
records.purpose: Decides whether an entry may be deleted or renumbered without leaving a hole, by rebuilding the number that would follow the previous one and comparing it with the number of the entry.

operands.name: the number of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: not the placeholder and not empty

operands.name: the previous number of the chain restricted to the prefix of this entry
operands.unit_or_currency: a text, or the absence of one
operands.source: the chain search restricted to the numbering prefix of the entry
operands.constraints: may be absent when the entry is the only one

preconditions.condition: The entry carries a real number.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no chain position to test.

procedure: Find the previous number of the chain restricted to the prefix of this entry.
When there is none, answer yes: the entry is the last because it is the only one.
Otherwise extract the template and the values from that previous number.
Increase the counter by one and rebuild the number from the template.
Answer yes exactly when the rebuilt number equals the number of this entry.
records.formula:
is_last( entry ) = ( fill( template of the previous number , values with counter + 1 ) = the number of the entry )
is_last( entry ) = yes  when the chain has no previous number

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counter is a whole number.
rounding.precision: The recorded counter length of the chain.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the entry is the last of its chain
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; a negative answer refuses the deletion with "You cannot delete this entry, as it has already consumed a sequence number and is not the last one in the chain. You should probably revert it instead."

edge_cases.case: The entry is the only one of its chain.
edge_cases.outcome: The answer is yes, because there is no previous number.

edge_cases.case: A hole precedes the entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The rebuilt number still equals the number of the entry when the entry follows the greatest counter, so a hole below it does not by itself make it not the last.

edge_cases.case: An entry with a greater counter exists in the same prefix.
edge_cases.outcome: The rebuilt number differs and the answer is no.

worked_examples.description: The third entry of a monthly chain
worked_examples.narrative: The previous counter is two, increasing it by one and refilling the template gives exactly the number of the entry, so the entry is the last of its chain and may be deleted.

worked_examples.description: The second entry of the same chain, which still has a third one
worked_examples.narrative: The greatest counter of the prefix is three, so the rebuilt number carries the counter four, which is not the number of the entry, and the deletion is refused.

records.name: Whether a set of entries are the last ones of their chains
records.purpose: Decides whether a whole selection may be deleted without leaving a hole, by requiring each group of the selection to be contiguous and to end at the end of its chain.

operands.name: the numbers of the selected entries
operands.source: the Journal Entries selected for deletion
operands.constraints: each carries a real number

operands.name: the template and the values of each number
operands.unit_or_currency: a template of text and fields, and whole numbers
operands.source: the format extraction applied to each number
operands.constraints: the grouping key is the template together with every value except the counter

preconditions.condition: Every selected entry carries a real number.
preconditions.otherwise: An entry without a number consumes no chain position and does not constrain the deletion.

procedure: Group the entries by the template together with all the values except the counter.
For each group, take the set of counter values it contains.
Answer no for the whole selection when, in any group, the largest counter minus the smallest is not equal to the size of the group minus one, because the group is then not contiguous.
For each group, take the entry with the largest counter and apply the single-entry chain-end test to it.
Answer no for the whole selection when that entry is not the last of its chain.
Answer yes when every group passes both tests.
records.formula:
contiguous( group ) = ( max counter of the group − min counter of the group = size of the group − 1 )
are_last( selection ) = every group is contiguous and its greatest-counter entry is the last of its chain

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counters are whole numbers.
rounding.precision: Whole numbers.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the selection may be deleted without leaving a hole
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; a negative answer refuses the deletion of the selection.

edge_cases.case: The selection spans two periods.
edge_cases.outcome: It forms two groups, and each must be contiguous and end at the end of its own chain.

edge_cases.case: The selection skips a counter inside a period.
edge_cases.outcome: The largest minus the smallest exceeds the size minus one, so the answer is no.

edge_cases.case: A group holds a single entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The largest minus the smallest is zero and the size minus one is zero, so the group is contiguous and only the chain-end test remains.

worked_examples.description: Selecting the last two entries of a monthly chain that holds three
worked_examples.narrative: The two counters are consecutive and the greatest of them is the last of the chain, so the selection may be deleted.

worked_examples.description: Selecting the first and the third entry of the same chain
worked_examples.narrative: The group is not contiguous, so the selection would leave a hole and the deletion is refused.

records.name: Gap detection on a numbering chain
records.purpose: Maintains, on each entry, the stored flag that marks the entry which opens a hole in its chain, so that the dashboard and a dedicated filter can show the journals whose numbering is not continuous.

operands.name: the numbering prefix, the counter and the suffix of the entry
operands.unit_or_currency: a text and a whole number
operands.source: the Journal Entry being updated
operands.constraints: the same suffix is tested by requiring the number to end with the counter followed by the suffix of the entry

operands.name: the two entries with the highest counters below the entry
operands.source: the same journal, the same prefix and the same suffix
operands.constraints: either may be absent

operands.name: the two entries with the lowest counters above the entry
operands.source: the same journal, the same prefix and the same suffix
operands.constraints: either may be absent

operands.name: the posted state of the entry and of its neighbours
operands.source: the Journal Entries concerned
operands.constraints: used by the second branch of the predicate

preconditions.condition: The prefix, the counter, the journal or the number of the entry has changed, or entries have been deleted.
preconditions.otherwise: The flags are left as they are.

preconditions.condition: The entry carries a real number.
preconditions.otherwise: The predicate answers no, because an entry without a real number occupies no chain position.

procedure: For the entry being updated, find in the same journal, the same prefix and with the same suffix the two entries with the highest counters below it and the two entries with the lowest counters above it.

Define the predicate that an entry made a gap, given its previous neighbour and its next neighbour: the entry has a real number, and either the previous neighbour exists, has a real number and the counter of the entry is not the counter of the previous neighbour plus one; or the next neighbour exists, the entry is not posted and the previous neighbour is posted.
Set the flag of the entry itself to the predicate, unless the entry was numbered through the locked increment in this transaction while being posted, because that path cannot produce a gap.

Set the flag of the next neighbour: when the update invalidates the current entry, flag the next neighbour as soon as a previous neighbour exists; otherwise apply the predicate to the next neighbour with the current entry as its previous neighbour and the second next entry as its next neighbour.

Set the flag of the previous neighbour by applying the predicate to it, with the second previous entry as its previous neighbour and either nothing, when the update invalidates the current entry, or the current entry as its next neighbour.
Invalidate the indicator of the journal that reports whether it has numbering holes.
records.formula:
made_a_gap( X , previous P , next N ) = X has a real number and (
    ( P exists and has a real number and counter( X ) ≠ counter( P ) + 1 )
 or ( N exists and X is not posted and P is posted ) )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counters are whole numbers.
rounding.precision: Whole numbers.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the flag that marks the entry opening a gap
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry; a dashboard indicator and a dedicated filter use it to show the journals with holes.

edge_cases.case: The entry was numbered through the locked increment in this transaction while being posted.
edge_cases.outcome: Its own flag is not set, because that path cannot produce a gap.

edge_cases.case: A draft entry sits between two posted ones.
edge_cases.outcome: The second branch of the predicate flags it, because a next neighbour exists, the entry is not posted and the previous neighbour is posted.

edge_cases.case: The entry is the first of its prefix.
edge_cases.outcome: No previous neighbour exists, so the first branch cannot fire.

worked_examples.description: The middle entry of a chain of three is deleted
worked_examples.narrative: After the deletion the previous neighbour of the third entry is the first one, whose counter is one, and three is not one plus one, so the third entry is flagged as having made a gap; the journal then reports a hole.

records.name: Resequencing a set of entries keeping the current order
records.purpose: Renumbers a selection of entries of one journal from a chosen first number, keeping the order the entries already have, so that the numbering is made continuous without changing which entry precedes which.

operands.name: the selected entries
operands.source: the selection the user renumbers
operands.constraints: all of one journal

operands.name: the first number
operands.source: typed by the user
operands.constraints: its periodicity, template and counter drive the whole operation

operands.name: the accounting date of each selected entry
operands.source: the Journal Entries
operands.constraints: used to partition the selection into periods

operands.name: the current number and the numbering prefix of each selected entry
operands.unit_or_currency: a text and a whole number
operands.source: the Journal Entries
operands.constraints: the sort keys of this ordering choice

preconditions.condition: The journal does not secure its entries with a hash, when the ordering choice is by date.
preconditions.otherwise: Not applicable here: this record covers the ordering choice that keeps the current order, which is permitted in every journal.

preconditions.condition: The first number can be read by one of the five shapes.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation is refused with the message that the sequence pattern should at least contain the counter grouping keys.

procedure: Deduce the periodicity from the first number and extract its template and values.

Partition the entries into periods, the key of an entry being the year of its accounting date for the yearly periodicity; the start year and the end year of its fiscal year joined by a hyphen for the year-range periodicity; the same followed by an oblique stroke and the month for the year-range-monthly periodicity; the pair of year and month for the monthly periodicity; and a single constant for the fixed periodicity.
Take the periods in the order in which they were first met.
For each period compute the period boundaries and the forced year range.

Build the list of new numbers: for the position counted from zero within the period, fill the template with the month of the period start, the forced start year or the year of the period start truncated to the recorded year length, the forced end year or the year of the period end truncated to the recorded end-year length, and the counter equal to the position plus the counter of the first number when this is the last period of the partition, or the position plus one otherwise.
Assign those numbers to the entries of the period sorted by the numbering prefix and then by the counter, which is the order they already have.
Clear the number of every selected entry and flush that to the database, so that the uniqueness constraint does not fire while the numbers are being swapped.
Write the new numbers one entry at a time.
records.formula:
new_number( position i within the period ) = fill( template , month = month of the period start , year = forced start year or the truncated year of the period start , end year = forced end year or the truncated year of the period end , counter = i + ( counter of the first number for the last period , otherwise 1 ) )
with the entries of a period taken in the order ( numbering prefix , counter )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counters are whole numbers and the years are truncated by a remainder.
rounding.precision: The recorded counter length, the recorded year lengths and two digits of month.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the new number of each selected entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the Journal Entries, one at a time, after every selected number has been cleared.

edge_cases.case: The selection spans several periods.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the last period met starts at the counter of the first number; every earlier period starts at one.

edge_cases.case: The numbers are swapped between two entries.
edge_cases.outcome: Clearing every selected number and flushing that first is what keeps the uniqueness constraint from firing during the swap.

edge_cases.case: The journal secures its entries with a hash.
edge_cases.outcome: This ordering choice is still permitted; only renumbering by date is refused with "You can not reorder sequence by date when the journal is locked with a hash."

worked_examples.description: Three entries of a monthly miscellaneous journal renumbered from the first number of February, keeping the current order
worked_examples.narrative: February is not the last period, so its counters start at one and its two entries are taken in the order of their prefix and counter, which puts the counter three before the counter seven; March is the last period, so its single entry starts at the counter of the first number, that is one.

records.name: Resequencing a set of entries reordering them by accounting date
records.purpose: Renumbers a selection of entries of one journal from a chosen first number and, at the same time, puts the numbering back in date order, which is what a date-based numbering requires after entries have been entered out of order.

operands.name: the selected entries
operands.source: the selection the user renumbers
operands.constraints: all of one journal

operands.name: the first number
operands.source: typed by the user
operands.constraints: its periodicity, template and counter drive the whole operation

operands.name: the accounting date of each selected entry
operands.source: the Journal Entries
operands.constraints: the first sort key of this ordering choice, and the partition key

operands.name: the current number and the identifier of each selected entry
operands.unit_or_currency: a text and a whole number
operands.source: the Journal Entries
operands.constraints: the second and third sort keys of this ordering choice

preconditions.condition: The journal does not secure its entries with a hash.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation is refused with "You can not reorder sequence by date when the journal is locked with a hash."

preconditions.condition: The first number can be read by one of the five shapes.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation is refused with the message that the sequence pattern should at least contain the counter grouping keys.

procedure: Deduce the periodicity from the first number and extract its template and values.

Partition the entries into periods, the key of an entry being the year of its accounting date for the yearly periodicity; the start year and the end year of its fiscal year joined by a hyphen for the year-range periodicity; the same followed by an oblique stroke and the month for the year-range-monthly periodicity; the pair of year and month for the monthly periodicity; and a single constant for the fixed periodicity.
Take the periods in the order in which they were first met.
For each period compute the period boundaries and the forced year range.

Build the list of new numbers exactly as for the other ordering choice: the counter of the position counted from zero, plus the counter of the first number for the last period met and plus one for every earlier period.
Assign those numbers to the entries of the period sorted by the accounting date, then by the current number, then by the identifier.
Clear the number of every selected entry and flush that to the database, so that the uniqueness constraint does not fire while the numbers are being swapped.
Write the new numbers one entry at a time.
records.formula:
new_number( position i within the period ) = fill( template , month = month of the period start , year = forced start year or the truncated year of the period start , end year = forced end year or the truncated year of the period end , counter = i + ( counter of the first number for the last period , otherwise 1 ) )
with the entries of a period taken in the order ( accounting date , current number , identifier )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counters are whole numbers and the years are truncated by a remainder.
rounding.precision: The recorded counter length, the recorded year lengths and two digits of month.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the new number of each selected entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the Journal Entries, one at a time, after every selected number has been cleared.

edge_cases.case: Two entries of the period share an accounting date.
edge_cases.outcome: The current number breaks the tie, and the identifier breaks it when the numbers are equal or absent.

edge_cases.case: The journal secures its entries with a hash.
edge_cases.outcome: The operation is refused outright.

edge_cases.case: The selection spans several periods.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the last period met starts at the counter of the first number.

worked_examples.description: Three entries of a monthly miscellaneous journal renumbered from the first number of February, reordered by accounting date

expected_outputs.template: MISC/ then the year on four digits then / then the month on two digits then / then the counter on four digits

worked_examples.narrative: The partition has two periods, February with two entries and March with one, and March is the last period met; February is not the last period, so its counters start at one and are assigned by date, giving the second of February the counter one and the fifth of February the counter two; March is the last period, so its counter starts at the counter of the first number, that is one.

records.name: Rendering one hashed value as text
records.purpose: Turns the value of each field that enters the inalterability hash into the exact text that is placed in the mapping, so that two independent implementations build character-for-character the same input string and therefore the same digest.

operands.name: value of the field being rendered
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency for a monetary field, a whole identifier for a link field, a date or a text otherwise
operands.source: one of the hashed fields: the number, the accounting date, the journal and the company of the entry, and the label, the debit, the credit, the account and the counterpart of each item
operands.constraints: may be empty, in which case it is rendered as the word False

operands.name: kind of the field
operands.source: the definition of the field in the entity documents
operands.constraints: exactly one of the three kinds applies to each hashed field

operands.name: number of decimal places of the currency of the record
operands.source: the number of decimals derived from the rounding step of the currency of the record
operands.constraints: two for a currency whose rounding step is one hundredth, zero for a currency with no subdivision

preconditions.condition: The field is one of the fields that enter the hash at the current hash version: on the entry the number, the accounting date, the journal and the company; on each item the label, the debit, the credit, the account and the counterpart.
preconditions.otherwise: The field is not rendered at all and takes no part in the digest; an earlier hash version omitted the two label fields, and the verification retries the older versions when the current one does not match.

preconditions.condition: The currency of the record is known, so that the number of decimal places of a monetary field is determined.
preconditions.otherwise: The number of decimals cannot be fixed and the digest cannot be reproduced; the company currency of the entry is the currency used for the debit and the credit of every item.

procedure: Take the value of the field and decide which of the three kinds it belongs to.
Render a link field as the decimal identifier of the record it points at, and as the word False when the link is empty, because the identifier of an empty link is the boolean false.
Render a monetary field with exactly the number of decimal places of the currency of the record, with no thousands separator and with a dot as the decimal separator.

Render every other field with the ordinary textual representation of its value: a date as four digits for the year, a hyphen, two digits for the month, a hyphen and two digits for the day; a text as itself; an empty value as the word False.
Place the rendered text as the value of the key of that field in the mapping that is later serialised and hashed.
records.formula:
rendered_text( link field )      = the decimal identifier of the target record, or "False" when the link is empty
rendered_text( monetary field )  = the amount written with exactly ( the number of decimals of the currency of the record ) decimal places, no thousands separator, a dot as the decimal separator
rendered_text( any other field ) = the ordinary textual representation of the value: a date as "YYYY-MM-DD", a text as itself, an empty value as "False"

rounding.what: The monetary fields of the item, that is the debit and the credit.
rounding.precision: Exactly the number of decimal places of the currency of the record, so an amount of one thousand in a currency of two decimals is written as the text 1000.00.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier when the amount was stored; the rendering itself does not round, it only fixes the number of decimal places written.
rounding.step: At rendering time, after the amounts have been stored and before the mapping is serialised.

result.name: rendered text of one field value
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored on its own: it is the value of one key of the mapping whose serialisation is hashed and whose digest is stored on the entry.

edge_cases.case: The link is empty, for example an item with no counterpart.
edge_cases.outcome: The rendered text is the word False, not an empty text and not a zero.

edge_cases.case: A monetary amount of zero in a currency of two decimals.
edge_cases.outcome: The rendered text is 0.00, with both decimal places written.

edge_cases.case: A monetary amount of one thousand in a currency of two decimals.
edge_cases.outcome: The rendered text is 1000.00; no thousands separator is written and the decimal separator is a dot.

edge_cases.case: The currency of the record has no subdivision, so its rounding step is one.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is rendered with no decimal places at all.

edge_cases.case: A value of another kind is empty, for example a label that was never filled.
edge_cases.outcome: The rendered text is the word False, exactly as for an empty link.

edge_cases.case: A character outside the basic Latin alphabet appears in a label.
edge_cases.outcome: It survives the rendering unchanged and is escaped as an escape sequence when the mapping is serialised.

worked_examples.description: The nine values of the first entry of the worked hash example, in a company whose currency has two decimals
worked_examples.narrative: The two links to the journal and to the company become the decimal identifiers 3 and 1; the accounting date becomes the text 2026-03-05; the debit of one thousand becomes 1000.00 and the credit of zero becomes 0.00, both with exactly two decimal places and no thousands separator; the two empty counterpart links become the word False; the labels and the number are rendered as themselves.

records.name: The inalterability hash of a secured entry
records.purpose: Binds the hash of the previous secured entry of the same chain to the exact content of this entry, so that any later modification of a hashed field breaks the verification and the archive is provably unaltered.

operands.name: the hashed fields of the entry
operands.unit_or_currency: a number, a date and two links
operands.source: the Journal Entry, in this exact order of naming: the number, the date, the journal and the company
operands.constraints: an earlier hash version omitted the two label fields, which is how historical hashes remain verifiable

operands.name: the hashed fields of each item
operands.unit_or_currency: a label, two monetary amounts and two links
operands.source: each Journal Item, in this exact order of naming: the label, the debit, the credit, the account and the counterpart
operands.constraints: the items are taken in their natural order

operands.name: the number of decimals of the currency of the record
operands.source: the currency of the record
operands.constraints: fixes exactly how a monetary field is rendered

operands.name: the hash of the previous entry of the chain
operands.source: the previous secured entry of the same chain
operands.constraints: the empty text when the chain has no previous hash

preconditions.condition: The entry is flagged for accounting data inalterability and belongs to a journal that secures its entries.
preconditions.otherwise: No hash is taken.

preconditions.condition: The previous entry of the chain, when there is one, carries a hash.
preconditions.otherwise: The previous digest is the empty text.

procedure: Create an empty mapping from key to text.
For each entry field, in the order the number, the date, the journal and the company, add an item whose key is the storage name of the field and whose value is the rendered text.

For each item of the entry, in the natural order of the items, and for each item field in the order the label, the debit, the credit, the account and the counterpart, add an item whose key is the word line, an underscore, the decimal identifier of the item, an underscore and the storage name of the field, and whose value is the rendered text.
Render a link field as the decimal identifier of the target record, or as the text "False" when it is empty, because the identifier of an empty link is the value false.
Render a monetary field with exactly the number of decimals of the currency of the record, without a thousands separator and with a dot as the decimal separator.
Render every other field with the ordinary textual representation of its value: a date in the year, month and day order separated by hyphens, a text as itself, an empty value as "False".

Serialise the mapping as a textual object notation document with the keys sorted in ascending lexical order of their characters, only the characters of the basic Latin alphabet escaped as needed and any character outside that range escaped as an escape sequence, no indentation, a comma and no space between items, a colon and no space between a key and its value, and every value written as a text string.

Take the hash of the previous entry of the chain and, when it begins with a dollar sign, strip the leading marker made of a dollar sign, the version and a dollar sign, keeping only the digest, because the version marker never enters the computation.

Concatenate the previous digest, which is the empty text when the chain has no previous hash, and the serialised document, encode the result in the eight-bit Unicode transformation format, and compute the two-hundred-and-fifty-six-bit secure hash of that byte string, rendered as lowercase hexadecimal.

Store the result as a dollar sign, the hash version number, a dollar sign and the hexadecimal digest, and use the digest just computed, without the marker, as the previous digest of the next entry of the chain.
records.formula:
hash( entry ) = "$" + version + "$" + secure_hash_256( previous_digest + serialised_mapping )
where previous_digest is the digest of the previous entry of the chain without its version marker, or the empty text

rounding.what: Every monetary field entering the hash.
rounding.precision: Exactly the number of decimals of the currency of the record.
rounding.method: The stored amount is rendered at that number of decimals, with a dot as the decimal separator and no thousands separator.
rounding.step: At the moment each value is rendered as text, before the mapping is serialised.

result.name: the inalterability hash of the entry
result.unit_or_currency: a text made of a dollar sign, the version, a dollar sign and sixty-four hexadecimal characters
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry and shown by the integrity report; the entry receives the message "This journal entry has been secured."

edge_cases.case: An item has no counterpart.
edge_cases.outcome: The link renders as the text "False", because the identifier of an empty link is the value false.

edge_cases.case: The chain has no previous hash.
edge_cases.outcome: The previous digest is the empty text and the input is exactly the serialised mapping.

edge_cases.case: An earlier hash version.
edge_cases.outcome: It omitted the two label fields; the verification retries the older versions when the current one does not match.

edge_cases.case: A hashed entry is modified.
edge_cases.outcome: It cannot be: a hashed entry never changes its number, its date, its journal, its company, nor the label, debit, credit, account or counterpart of any of its items, is never reset to draft and is never deleted.

worked_examples.description: The first entry of a chain in journal number three of company number one

expected_outputs.stored_value_shape: a dollar sign, the digit 4, a dollar sign and the sixty-four hexadecimal characters of the digest

worked_examples.narrative: The mapping is serialised as one line, an opening brace, then each key in double quotes, a colon, the value in double quotes, separated by commas, then a closing brace; the chain has no previous hash, so the previous digest is the empty text and the input to the hash function is exactly that serialised line; the monetary values are rendered with the two decimals of the company currency.

worked_examples.description: The second entry of the same chain

expected_outputs.input_to_the_hash_function: the digest of the first entry, without its version marker, followed by the serialised line of the second entry

worked_examples.narrative: Each entry of the chain therefore carries the whole history of the chain, which is what makes a later modification detectable.

records.name: Verifying the hash chain of a journal
records.purpose: Walks the secured entries of each journal, recomputes their hashes and reports, per numbering prefix, the range of entries that verify and the first entry that does not.

operands.name: the secured entries of the journal
operands.source: the journal being verified
operands.constraints: ordered by the legacy securing number ascending with empty values last, then by numbering prefix, then by counter ascending

operands.name: the stored hash of each entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: carries its version marker

operands.name: the hash version range
operands.source: the versions the system knows
operands.constraints: the recomputation starts at version one and increases until it matches or the maximum version is reached

preconditions.condition: The acting user belongs to the accounting user group.
preconditions.otherwise: The report is refused with "Please contact your accountant to print the Hash integrity result."

preconditions.condition: The journal has at least one hashed entry.
preconditions.otherwise: The report says "There is no journal entry flagged for accounting data inalterability yet."

procedure: For each journal of the company, select every entry of the journal that carries a hash, ordered by the legacy securing number ascending with empty values last, then by numbering prefix, then by counter ascending.
Walk the entries in batches, keeping per prefix the first verified entry, the last verified entry and the first corrupted entry.
For each entry, take as its previous entry the last verified entry of the same prefix, or, when the entry carries a legacy securing number, the last verified entry overall.
Recompute the hash starting at hash version one and increasing the version until it matches or the maximum version is reached.
Mark the prefix as corrupted at the first entry whose hash cannot be reproduced, and stop checking the remaining entries of that prefix.

Report, per journal and prefix, either "Entries are correctly hashed" together with the first and last verified entry, their hashes and their dates, or "Corrupted data on journal entry with id *the identifier* (*the number*)."
records.formula: verified( entry ) = there exists a hash version v , from one up to the maximum version, such that recompute( entry , previous verified entry of the same prefix , v ) = the stored hash of the entry

rounding.what: Every monetary field entering each recomputed hash.
rounding.precision: Exactly the number of decimals of the currency of the record.
rounding.method: The stored amount is rendered at that number of decimals, as in the hash computation itself.
rounding.step: At the moment each value is rendered as text during the recomputation.

result.name: the verification report per journal and prefix
result.unit_or_currency: a range of entries with their hashes and dates, or the identifier and number of the first corrupted entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the integrity report; nothing is stored.

edge_cases.case: An entry carries a legacy securing number.
edge_cases.outcome: Its previous entry is the last verified entry overall rather than the last verified entry of the same prefix.

edge_cases.case: An entry was hashed under an earlier version that omitted the two label fields.
edge_cases.outcome: The recomputation retries the older versions, so the historical hash still verifies.

edge_cases.case: An entry of a prefix fails.
edge_cases.outcome: The prefix is marked corrupted and its remaining entries are not checked.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no hashed entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The report states that there is no journal entry flagged for accounting data inalterability yet.

worked_examples.description: A miscellaneous journal holding two chains after the half-year has been secured

inputs.acting_user: a member of the accounting user group

expected_outputs.prefix_one_report: Entries are correctly hashed, first and last verified entry MISC/2025/12/0001
expected_outputs.prefix_two_report: Entries are correctly hashed, first verified entry MISC/2026/03/0001 and last verified entry MISC/2026/03/0003
