worked_examples.narrative: Both chains are contiguous, so each entry verifies against the previous verified entry of its own prefix and the report names the first and the last verified entry of each prefix with their hashes and their dates.

records.name: The residual amounts and the reconciled flag of a journal item
records.purpose: Gives what is still open on an item after everything already matched against it, in both the company currency and the currency of the item, and decides whether the item counts as reconciled.

operands.name: balance
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: rounded to the company currency

operands.name: foreign amount
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: rounded to the item currency

operands.name: matched amounts where the item is the debit side
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the item
operands.source: the Partial Reconciliations in which the item is the debit item
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: matched amounts where the item is the credit side
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the item
operands.source: the Partial Reconciliations in which the item is the credit item
operands.constraints: always positive

preconditions.condition: The account of the item allows matching, or is a bank-and-cash or credit-card account.
preconditions.otherwise: Both residuals are forced to zero and the item is never considered reconciled.

preconditions.condition: The matched amounts in the item currency are themselves rounded to the item currency before being subtracted.
preconditions.otherwise: The residual in the item currency would drift by a fraction of a rounding step.

procedure: Take the balance of the item and subtract the sum of the matched amounts in which the item is the debit side.
Add the sum of the matched amounts in which the item is the credit side.
Round the result to the company currency: that is the residual in the company currency.
Take the foreign amount of the item and subtract the sum of the matched debit-side amounts expressed in the item currency, each already rounded to the item currency.
Add the sum of the matched credit-side amounts expressed in the item currency, each already rounded to the item currency.
Round the result to the item currency: that is the residual in the item currency.
Answer that the item is reconciled exactly when the residual in the company currency is zero for the company currency and the residual in the item currency is zero for the item currency.
records.formula:
amount_residual          = round_to_company_currency( balance − sum of the matched amounts where the item is the debit side + sum of the matched amounts where the item is the credit side )
amount_residual_currency = round_to_item_currency( amount_currency − sum of the matched debit-side amounts in the item currency + sum of the matched credit-side amounts in the item currency )
reconciled = ( amount_residual is zero for the company currency ) and ( amount_residual_currency is zero for the item currency )

rounding.what: Each of the two residuals, and each matched amount in the item currency before it is subtracted.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the first residual, the currency of the item for the second.
rounding.step: On each matched amount in the item currency before the subtraction, and once on each residual after the additions and subtractions.

result.name: the residual in the company currency, the residual in the item currency and the reconciled flag
result.unit_or_currency: company currency, the currency of the item, and a yes or no value
result.stored_or_displayed: All three are stored on the Journal Item; they drive the payment status of the document, the aged balances and the outstanding widgets.

edge_cases.case: The account neither allows matching nor is a bank-and-cash or credit-card account.
edge_cases.outcome: Both residuals are forced to zero and the item is never considered reconciled.

edge_cases.case: Reconciliation is switched on for an account.
edge_cases.outcome: For every item on the account that has no Full Reconciliation, the reconciled flag becomes yes when the debit, the credit and the foreign amount are all zero and no otherwise, the residual in the company currency becomes the debit minus the credit, and the residual in the item currency becomes the foreign amount.

edge_cases.case: Reconciliation is switched off for an account.
edge_cases.outcome: The operation is first refused when a pending partial reconciliation exists, and then both residuals of every item without a Full Reconciliation are set to zero.

edge_cases.case: An item has a zero balance and a non-zero foreign amount.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not reconciled, because only one of the two residuals is zero; this is what an exchange-difference item looks like.

worked_examples.description: A receivable of 1 210.00 in the company currency matched twice
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand two hundred and ten minus eight hundred is 410.00 in both currencies, which is not zero, so the item is not reconciled.

worked_examples.description: An item matched in full
worked_examples.narrative: Both residuals are zero at their own precision, so the item counts as reconciled.

records.name: Building the reconciliation plan
records.purpose: Turns a reconciliation request into the ordered tree of nodes that the pairing loop walks, so that items meet in a defined order and items of two currencies are never paired inside one node.

operands.name: the members of the plan
operands.unit_or_currency: sets of Journal Items, or nested plans
operands.source: the reconciliation request
operands.constraints: a nested plan is processed before the set that contains it, and then the union of everything is processed once more so that leftovers match each other

operands.name: the due date of each item, falling back to its accounting date
operands.source: the Journal Items
operands.constraints: the first sort key

operands.name: the currency, the foreign amount and the balance of each item
operands.unit_or_currency: a currency, the currency of the item and the company currency
operands.source: the Journal Items
operands.constraints: the second, third and fourth sort keys

operands.name: the counterpart of each item
operands.source: the Journal Items
operands.constraints: an additional sort key inside a node when more than one counterpart is present

preconditions.condition: No remaining item is already reconciled; items that are already reconciled are dropped unless they carry a partial matching number shared with an unreconciled item of the set, which means the group is being extended.
preconditions.otherwise: The request is refused with "You are trying to reconcile some entries that are already reconciled."

preconditions.condition: No item belongs to a cancelled entry.
preconditions.otherwise: The request is refused with "You can not reconcile cancelled entries."

preconditions.condition: Every item uses the same account.
preconditions.otherwise: The request is refused with "Entries are not from the same account: *the account display names*"

preconditions.condition: Every item belongs to the same company hierarchy.
preconditions.otherwise: The request is refused with "Entries don't belong to the same company: *the company display names*"

preconditions.condition: The account allows matching, or is a bank-and-cash or credit-card account.
preconditions.otherwise: The request is refused with "Account *the account display name* does not allow reconciliation. First change the configuration of this account to allow it."

procedure: Walk the members of the plan in order.

When a member is a set of items, sort it by the due date falling back to the accounting date, then by currency, then by foreign amount, then by balance; in the reduced sorting mode use only the first two keys.
When the sorted set uses more than one currency, create one child node per currency holding the items of that currency in the sorted order.
When a member is a nested plan, process its members recursively and take the union of their items as the node.
Check the preconditions on every node.
Discard empty nodes.

Process a node by processing its children first, then the items of the node itself that are not yet fully matched; inside a node, when more than one counterpart is present, sort the items additionally by counterpart identifier so that items of the same counterpart meet first.
records.formula: node order = sort by ( due date or accounting date , currency , foreign amount , balance ) , then one child node per currency when the set uses several , then, inside a node with several counterparts, by counterpart identifier

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded during the planning: the amounts are used only as sort keys.
rounding.precision: The amounts are already at the precision of their currency.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the ordered tree of reconciliation nodes
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is the working structure of the pairing loop.

edge_cases.case: The reduced sorting mode is requested.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the due date, falling back to the accounting date, and the currency are used as sort keys.

edge_cases.case: An already reconciled item shares a partial matching number with an unreconciled item of the set.
edge_cases.outcome: It is kept, because the group is being extended rather than reconciled twice.

edge_cases.case: A node becomes empty after the discarding.
edge_cases.outcome: It is removed and never processed.

edge_cases.case: The set uses one currency only.
edge_cases.outcome: No child node per currency is created and the node is processed directly.

worked_examples.description: A request holding one set of four items of two currencies and of two counterparts
worked_examples.narrative: The set is sorted by due date, then currency, then foreign amount, then balance, and because it uses two currencies one child node is created per currency, each holding its items in the sorted order; the children are processed first and the union of everything is processed afterwards so that any leftovers can still meet.

records.name: The accounting rate of a journal item
records.purpose: Gives the rate implied by the item itself, which is the rate at which the item is willing to be matched in its own currency and the rate an invoice adopts when it is matched against a payment.

operands.name: foreign amount
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: must not be zero for the rate to be computable

operands.name: balance
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: must not be zero for the rate to be computable

preconditions.condition: Neither the balance nor the foreign amount is zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The accounting rate is not computed and the item publishes no residual at that rate.

procedure: Divide the foreign amount of the item by its balance.
Take the absolute value of the quotient, so that the rate is positive whichever side of the ledger the item is on.
Use the value only when neither the balance nor the foreign amount is zero.
records.formula: accounting_rate = | amount_currency ÷ balance |

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the rate is kept at full precision.
rounding.precision: Full precision; only the amounts converted with the rate are rounded, each to its own currency.
rounding.step: Rounding happens on the converted amounts, never on the rate.

result.name: accounting rate of the item
result.unit_or_currency: units of the item currency per unit of the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is published together with the residual the item offers in its own currency, and it is the rate an invoice adopts when the counterpart is a payment.

edge_cases.case: The balance is zero and the foreign amount is not.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is not computable, so the item publishes no residual at an accounting rate; this is the shape of an exchange-difference item.

edge_cases.case: The foreign amount is zero and the balance is not.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is not computable for the same reason.

edge_cases.case: The item is in the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is one, and the item publishes the company currency at that rate.

worked_examples.description: An invoice item booked at 1.05 foreign units per euro
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand divided by nine hundred and fifty-two point three eight is 1.05, the rate at which the invoice was booked.

worked_examples.description: A payment item booked at 1.10 foreign units per euro
worked_examples.narrative: Minus one thousand divided by minus nine hundred and nine point zero nine is 1.10, and the absolute value keeps it positive.

records.name: The rate to the counterpart currency in a reconciliation
records.purpose: Chooses the rate at which an item kept in the company currency is offered in the currency of its counterpart, so that an invoice can be matched in the currency of the payment at the rate of that payment.

operands.name: a rate forced by the caller
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the counterpart currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the caller, for example the payment register operation, which forces the rate it displayed
operands.constraints: takes precedence over everything else when present

operands.name: the accounting rate of the counterpart item
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the counterpart currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the counterpart item
operands.constraints: used when the item is not a payment or bank transaction and the counterpart is one

operands.name: the rate of the currency table
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the counterpart currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the currency table on the relevant date
operands.constraints: the relevant date is the document date for an invoice-like document and the accounting date otherwise

preconditions.condition: The item is expressed in the company currency, sits on a receivable or payable account, has a non-zero residual in the company currency, and the counterpart is in another currency.
preconditions.otherwise: This rate is not needed: the item publishes its own currency at its own accounting rate instead.

procedure: Use the rate forced by the caller when there is one.
Otherwise, when the item is not a payment or a bank transaction and the counterpart is one, use the accounting rate of the counterpart, so that the invoice adopts the rate of the payment.
Otherwise use the rate of the currency table on the relevant date, which is the document date for an invoice-like document and the accounting date otherwise.
records.formula:
rate_to_counterpart_currency = the rate forced by the caller
                             , otherwise the accounting rate of the counterpart when the item is not a payment or bank transaction and the counterpart is one
                             , otherwise the rate of the currency table at the document date of an invoice-like document, or at the accounting date otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the rate is kept at full precision.
rounding.precision: Full precision; the residual converted with it is rounded to the counterpart currency.
rounding.step: The conversion of the company-currency residual is rounded to the counterpart currency after the multiplication.

result.name: the rate at which the item is offered in the counterpart currency
result.unit_or_currency: units of the counterpart currency per unit of the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is published together with the residual offered in the counterpart currency and is used again when the matched amount is converted back.

edge_cases.case: The payment register operation forces a rate.
edge_cases.outcome: That rate wins over both the accounting rate of the counterpart and the currency table, so the match reproduces exactly the figures the user saw.

edge_cases.case: Both items are payments or bank transactions.
edge_cases.outcome: The second branch does not apply and the currency table is used.

edge_cases.case: The converted residual rounds to zero in the counterpart currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is published for that currency.

worked_examples.description: An invoice kept in the company currency matched against a payment in another currency

inputs.item: an invoice receivable in euros on a receivable account
inputs.counterpart: a payment in United States dollars

worked_examples.narrative: The item is not a payment and the counterpart is one, so the invoice adopts the accounting rate of the payment, that is 1.10 dollars per euro, which is what lets an invoice kept in the company currency be matched in the currency of the payment.

worked_examples.description: A company-currency invoice matched against a foreign-currency item that is not a payment

inputs.counterpart: another invoice item in United States dollars

worked_examples.narrative: Neither branch above applies, so the rate of the currency table at the document date of the invoice-like document is used.

records.name: The available residuals of one item seen from a counterpart currency
records.purpose: Publishes, for one item, the residual it can offer in each currency together with the rate that reaches that currency, which is what allows the currency of the match to be chosen before any amount is computed.

operands.name: residual in the company currency
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: residual in the currency of the item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: the accounting rate of the item
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the item currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the accounting rate computation
operands.constraints: computed only when neither the balance nor the foreign amount is zero

operands.name: the currency of the counterpart item
operands.source: the item that is about to be matched against this one
operands.constraints: may equal the company currency or the currency of this item

operands.name: the rate to the counterpart currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the counterpart currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the rate-to-the-counterpart-currency choice
operands.constraints: needed only for an item kept in the company currency on a receivable or payable account

preconditions.condition: The item still has something open in at least one currency.
preconditions.otherwise: It publishes nothing and is considered exhausted.

preconditions.condition: The account of the item allows matching, or is a bank-and-cash or credit-card account.
preconditions.otherwise: Both residuals are zero and nothing is published.

procedure: When the residual in the company currency is not zero, publish the company currency with that residual and the rate one.

When the currency of the item differs from the company currency and the residual in the currency of the item is not zero, publish the currency of the item with that residual and the accounting rate of the item.

When the item is expressed in the company currency, sits on a receivable or payable account, has a non-zero residual in the company currency and the counterpart is in another currency: determine the rate to the counterpart currency, convert the company-currency residual at that rate, round the result to the counterpart currency, and publish the counterpart currency with that residual and that rate when the result is not zero; this is what lets an invoice kept in the company currency be matched in the currency of the payment.

Otherwise, when the currency of the item is the counterpart currency and differs from the company currency and the residual in the currency of the item is not zero, publish the counterpart currency with that residual and the accounting rate.
records.formula:
published( company currency )    = ( residual in the company currency , rate 1 )                              when that residual is not zero
published( item currency )       = ( residual in the item currency , accounting rate )                     when the item currency differs from the company currency and that residual is not zero
published( counterpart currency )= ( round_to_counterpart_currency( residual in the company currency × rate to the counterpart currency ) , that rate )   for a company-currency item on a receivable or payable account facing another currency, when the result is not zero
published( counterpart currency )= ( residual in the item currency , accounting rate )                     when the item currency is the counterpart currency and differs from the company currency and that residual is not zero

rounding.what: The company-currency residual converted into the counterpart currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the counterpart currency.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by the rate to the counterpart currency, before the result is tested against zero and published.

result.name: the residuals the item offers, one per currency, each with its rate
result.unit_or_currency: one amount per published currency, in that currency, together with a rate
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; the publication is the input of the currency choice and of the partial match.

edge_cases.case: The item has a zero company-currency residual but a non-zero foreign residual.
edge_cases.outcome: It publishes only its own currency; this is the shape of an exchange-difference item.

edge_cases.case: The converted residual rounds to zero in the counterpart currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is published for that currency.

edge_cases.case: The item is in the company currency and sits on an account that is neither receivable nor payable.
edge_cases.outcome: The third branch does not apply, so the item can be matched only in the company currency.

edge_cases.case: The item published nothing in the currency finally chosen for the match.
edge_cases.outcome: The item is considered exhausted and is dropped from the iteration.

worked_examples.description: An invoice item and a payment item, both in United States dollars, in a company keeping its books in euros
worked_examples.narrative: The debit item publishes the euro at 952.38 with the rate one and the dollar at 1 000.00 with the accounting rate of one thousand divided by nine hundred and fifty-two point three eight, that is 1.05; the credit item publishes the euro at minus 909.09 with the rate one and the dollar at minus 1 000.00 with the accounting rate 1.10.

records.name: Choosing the currency in which a match is made
records.purpose: Picks the currency in which two items will be matched, preferring a foreign currency that both sides can offer, so that a foreign-currency invoice and a foreign-currency payment settle each other exactly in that currency.

operands.name: the currency of the debit item
operands.source: the debit Journal Item
operands.constraints: may equal the company currency

operands.name: the currency of the credit item
operands.source: the credit Journal Item
operands.constraints: may equal the company currency

operands.name: the residuals published by each item
operands.source: the publication of available residuals of each item
operands.constraints: a currency counts as offered only when the item published something in it

preconditions.condition: Both items have published their available residuals.
preconditions.otherwise: The currency cannot be chosen.

procedure: When the currency of the debit item differs from the company currency and both items published a residual in it, make the match in the currency of the debit item.
Otherwise, when the currency of the credit item differs from the company currency and both items published a residual in it, make the match in the currency of the credit item.
Otherwise make the match in the company currency.
Consider exhausted, and drop from the iteration, any item that published nothing in the currency finally chosen.
records.formula:
reconciliation_currency = the debit currency    when it differs from the company currency and both items published a residual in it
reconciliation_currency = the credit currency   when it differs from the company currency and both items published a residual in it
reconciliation_currency = the company currency  otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the choice is between currencies.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the reconciliation currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides which of the two partial-match computations applies and therefore whether an exchange difference can arise.

edge_cases.case: Both items are in the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The match is made in the company currency.

edge_cases.case: The debit item is in a foreign currency the credit item cannot offer.
edge_cases.outcome: The debit currency is skipped and the credit currency, then the company currency, are considered.

edge_cases.case: One item published nothing in the chosen currency.
edge_cases.outcome: That item is considered exhausted and is dropped from the iteration.

edge_cases.case: The reconciliation currency is the company currency, both items share the same currency and at least one of them published nothing in that shared currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Exchange-line mode is detected first, and in that mode no rate is applied, because the exchange item is meant to change only the company-currency amount.

worked_examples.description: An invoice and a payment both in United States dollars
worked_examples.narrative: The debit currency differs from the company currency and both items published a residual in it, so the match is made in the dollar.

worked_examples.description: An invoice and a payment both in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: Neither side offers a currency different from the company currency, so the match is made in the company currency.

records.name: The matched amount and the fully-matched flags of one partial match
records.purpose: Determines how much of the two facing residuals is settled by one partial match and which of the two sides is thereby exhausted in the reconciliation currency.

operands.name: the debit residual in the reconciliation currency
operands.source: the residual the debit item published in that currency
operands.constraints: positive; written as the value D

operands.name: the credit residual in the reconciliation currency, sign-flipped to be positive
operands.source: the residual the credit item published in that currency, with its sign reversed
operands.constraints: positive; written as the value C

preconditions.condition: The reconciliation currency has been chosen and both items published a residual in it.
preconditions.otherwise: The item that published nothing is exhausted and is dropped from the iteration.

procedure: Take the debit residual in the reconciliation currency and call it the value D.
Take the credit residual in the reconciliation currency, reverse its sign so that it is positive, and call it the value C.
The matched amount in the reconciliation currency is the smaller of D and C.
The debit side is fully matched when D is at most C.
The credit side is fully matched when D is at least C.

Detect exchange-line mode first: the reconciliation currency is the company currency, both items share the same currency, and at least one of them published nothing in that shared currency; in that mode no rate is applied, because the exchange item is meant to change only the company-currency amount.
records.formula:
matched_amount_in_reconciliation_currency = min( D , C )
debit_fully_matched  = ( D ≤ C )
credit_fully_matched = ( D ≥ C )

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: both residuals are already at the precision of the reconciliation currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the reconciliation currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier when each residual was computed.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the minimum itself.

result.name: the matched amount in the reconciliation currency and the two fully-matched flags
result.unit_or_currency: the reconciliation currency, and two yes or no values
result.stored_or_displayed: The amount feeds the two currency-specific computations and, through them, the stored Partial Reconciliation; the flags decide which side may produce an exchange difference.

edge_cases.case: The two residuals are equal.
edge_cases.outcome: Both sides are fully matched and both flags answer yes.

edge_cases.case: One residual is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The matched amount is zero and the corresponding side is fully matched; the match is recorded only when it produced an amount.

edge_cases.case: Exchange-line mode is detected.
edge_cases.outcome: No rate is applied and only the company-currency amounts move.

worked_examples.description: An invoice receivable of 1 210.00 against a payment of 500.00, both in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The smaller of the two is 500.00, so the credit is fully matched and the debit is not.

worked_examples.description: An invoice and a payment of one thousand foreign units each
worked_examples.narrative: The two residuals are equal, so the matched amount is 1 000.00 dollars and both sides are fully matched in the reconciliation currency.

records.name: One partial match computed in the company currency
records.purpose: Computes the three amounts of a Partial Reconciliation when the match is made in the company currency, converting the matched amount into each item currency without ever exceeding what that item still has open.

operands.name: the matched amount in the company currency
operands.source: the smaller of the two facing residuals
operands.constraints: positive

operands.name: the rate published by the debit item
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the debit currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the publication of the debit item
operands.constraints: absent in exchange-line mode and whenever the item has no residual left in its own currency

operands.name: the rate published by the credit item
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the credit currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the publication of the credit item
operands.constraints: absent in exchange-line mode and whenever the item has no residual left in its own currency

operands.name: the debit residual in the debit currency
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the debit item
operands.source: the debit Journal Item
operands.constraints: caps the converted amount

operands.name: the credit residual in the credit currency
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the credit item
operands.source: the credit Journal Item
operands.constraints: sign-flipped to be positive; caps the converted amount

preconditions.condition: The reconciliation currency is the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The foreign-currency computation applies instead.

procedure: Take the matched amount as the smaller of the debit residual and the sign-flipped credit residual, both in the company currency.
Multiply the matched amount by the rate published by the debit item, round the product to the debit currency, and take the smaller of that value and the debit residual in the debit currency.

Multiply the matched amount by the rate published by the credit item, round the product to the credit currency, and take the smaller of that value and the sign-flipped credit residual in the credit currency.
Set the corresponding currency amount to zero whenever the rate is absent, which is the case in exchange-line mode and whenever the item has no residual left in its own currency.
records.formula:
matched_amount = min( D , C )
matched_debit_amount_in_debit_currency   = min( round_to_debit_currency( debit_rate × matched_amount ) , debit residual in the debit currency )
matched_credit_amount_in_credit_currency = min( round_to_credit_currency( credit_rate × matched_amount ) , − credit residual in the credit currency )

rounding.what: Each converted currency amount, before it is capped by the residual of its item.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the debit currency for the debit side, of the credit currency for the credit side.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by the rate and before the minimum with the residual of the item.

result.name: the matched amount in the company currency and the matched amount in each item currency
result.unit_or_currency: company currency, the currency of the debit item and the currency of the credit item
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Partial Reconciliation, where all three amounts are always positive.

edge_cases.case: The rate of a side is absent.
edge_cases.outcome: The currency amount of that side is zero.

edge_cases.case: The converted amount exceeds what the item still has open in its own currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The minimum caps it at the residual of the item, so no item is over-matched in its own currency.

edge_cases.case: The debit side is fully matched but keeps a residual in its own currency.
edge_cases.outcome: An exchange difference is produced that corrects the foreign residual only.

worked_examples.description: A plain partial match in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: Both items publish the company currency with the rate one, the matched amount is 500.00, the credit is fully matched and the debit is not; the stored match carries 500.00 in all three amounts, the new residuals are 710.00 and 0.00, and the credit item is dropped from the iteration.

records.name: One partial match computed in a foreign currency
records.purpose: Computes the three amounts of a Partial Reconciliation when the match is made in a currency other than the company currency, converting each side back into the company currency at the inverse of its own rate so that the difference between the two rates surfaces as an exchange difference.

operands.name: the matched amount in the reconciliation currency
operands.source: the smaller of the two facing residuals in that currency
operands.constraints: positive

operands.name: the rate published by the debit item
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the reconciliation currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the publication of the debit item
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: the rate published by the credit item
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the reconciliation currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the publication of the credit item
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: the debit residual in the company currency
operands.source: the debit Journal Item
operands.constraints: caps the debit side

operands.name: the credit residual in the company currency
operands.source: the credit Journal Item
operands.constraints: sign-flipped to be positive; caps the credit side

preconditions.condition: The reconciliation currency is not the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The company-currency computation applies instead.

preconditions.condition: Both rates are strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The conversion back into the company currency cannot be performed.

procedure: Convert each side back into the company currency using the inverse of its own rate, and compute a tolerance range around the result to absorb the rounding of the original amounts.
Take, for the debit side, the smaller of the middle of its converted range and the debit residual in the company currency.
Take, for the credit side, the smaller of the middle of its converted range and the sign-flipped credit residual in the company currency.
The matched amount in the company currency is the smaller of those two side amounts.
Apply the rounding-noise suppression when each side amount falls inside the tolerance range of the other.
Set the matched amount in the debit currency to the matched company amount when the debit item is in the company currency, and to the matched amount in the reconciliation currency otherwise.
Set the matched amount in the credit currency to the matched company amount when the credit item is in the company currency, and to the matched amount in the reconciliation currency otherwise.
records.formula:
debit_side_company_amount  = min( middle_of_the_debit_side  , debit residual in company currency )
credit_side_company_amount = min( middle_of_the_credit_side , − credit residual in company currency )
matched_amount             = min( debit_side_company_amount , credit_side_company_amount )
matched_debit_amount_in_debit_currency   = matched_amount                              when the debit item is in the company currency
matched_debit_amount_in_debit_currency   = matched_amount_in_reconciliation_currency   otherwise
matched_credit_amount_in_credit_currency = matched_amount                              when the credit item is in the company currency
matched_credit_amount_in_credit_currency = matched_amount_in_reconciliation_currency   otherwise

rounding.what: Each side of the matched amount converted back into the company currency, and the two bounds of each tolerance range.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: After each division by the rate of the side and before the minimum with the residual of that side.

result.name: the matched amount in the company currency and the matched amount in each item currency
result.unit_or_currency: company currency, the currency of the debit item and the currency of the credit item
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Partial Reconciliation, where all three amounts are always positive.

edge_cases.case: The two converted side amounts each fall inside the tolerance range of the other.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is pure rounding noise and the matched amount is replaced by the smaller of the two company-currency residuals, so no exchange difference is produced.

edge_cases.case: The two converted side amounts lie outside each other's ranges.
edge_cases.outcome: The smaller of them is matched and the difference is booked as an exchange difference.

edge_cases.case: One of the two items is in the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Its matched amount in its own currency is the company amount, not the reconciliation-currency amount.

worked_examples.description: An invoice booked at 1.05 foreign units per euro matched against a payment received at 1.10
worked_examples.narrative: Both sides publish the dollar, so the match is made in dollars for 1 000.00 and both sides are fully matched in that currency; converting back at one divided by 1.05 gives 952.38 and at one divided by 1.10 gives 909.09; the two differ by more than a rounding step and lie outside each other's tolerance ranges, so the matched amount in euros is the smaller, 909.09; the debit item keeps 43.29 euros with nothing open in dollars, which is why an exchange difference of 43.29 euros is prepared.

records.name: The tolerance range around a matched amount converted back into the company currency
records.purpose: Computes the interval within which a company-currency conversion of the matched amount is indistinguishable from another, so that the rounding of the original amounts is not mistaken for a genuine exchange difference.

operands.name: the matched amount in the reconciliation currency
operands.source: the smaller of the two facing residuals in that currency
operands.constraints: positive

operands.name: the rounding step of the source currency
operands.source: the currency the matched amount is expressed in
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: the rate of the side being converted
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the reconciliation currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the publication of that item
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The match is being made in a currency other than the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: No tolerance range is needed, because no conversion back takes place.

procedure: Take half the rounding step of the currency the matched amount is expressed in.
Subtract that half step from the matched amount, divide by the rate of the side, and round to the company currency: this is the low bound.
Divide the matched amount itself by the rate of the side and round to the company currency: this is the middle, which is the value actually used for that side.
Add the half step to the matched amount, divide by the rate of the side, and round to the company currency: this is the high bound.
Compute the three values separately for the debit side and for the credit side, each with its own rate.
records.formula:
half_step_of_source_currency = rounding_step_of_source_currency ÷ 2
low    = round_to_company_currency( ( matched_amount_in_reconciliation_currency − half_step ) ÷ rate )
middle = round_to_company_currency(   matched_amount_in_reconciliation_currency             ÷ rate )
high   = round_to_company_currency( ( matched_amount_in_reconciliation_currency + half_step ) ÷ rate )

rounding.what: The three converted values: the low bound, the middle and the high bound.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Each of the three after its own division by the rate, before the bounds are compared.

result.name: the low bound, the middle and the high bound of the converted side
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; the middle is the value used for that side and the two bounds are used only by the rounding-noise test.

edge_cases.case: The rate is close to one.
edge_cases.outcome: The range is roughly one rounding step wide, so only genuine differences survive the test.

edge_cases.case: The rate is large.
edge_cases.outcome: The range narrows in the company currency, because half a step of the source currency converts to less than half a step of the company currency.

edge_cases.case: The rounding steps of the two currencies differ.
edge_cases.outcome: The half step is always taken from the currency the matched amount is expressed in, that is the reconciliation currency.

worked_examples.description: The debit side of a match of 281.53 foreign units at the rate of twenty thousand foreign units per 377 554.00 euros
worked_examples.narrative: Converting the matched amount back at the rate implied by the debit item gives 5 314.64 euros, with a tolerance range from 5 314.54 to 5 314.73.

worked_examples.description: The credit side of the same match, at the rate implied by the credit item
worked_examples.narrative: Converting the same matched amount back at the rate implied by the credit item gives 5 314.62 euros, with a tolerance range from 5 314.53 to 5 314.71.

records.name: Rounding-noise suppression in a foreign-currency match
records.purpose: Replaces the matched amount when the two sides differ only by the rounding of the original amounts, so that no exchange-difference entry is produced and no residual is left open for a difference that does not exist.

operands.name: the converted amount of the debit side
operands.source: the middle of the tolerance range of the debit side
operands.constraints: already rounded to the company currency

operands.name: the converted amount of the credit side
operands.source: the middle of the tolerance range of the credit side
operands.constraints: already rounded to the company currency

operands.name: the tolerance range of each side
operands.source: the low and high bounds computed for each side
operands.constraints: each bound already rounded to the company currency

operands.name: the residual of each item in the company currency
operands.source: the two Journal Items
operands.constraints: the credit residual is sign-flipped to be positive

preconditions.condition: The match is being made in a currency other than the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The test does not arise, because no conversion back takes place.

procedure: Test whether the converted amount of the debit side falls inside the tolerance range of the credit side.
Test whether the converted amount of the credit side falls inside the tolerance range of the debit side.
When both tests answer yes, the difference is pure rounding noise and not a genuine exchange difference.

In that case replace all three values — the debit side amount, the credit side amount and the matched amount — by the smaller of the debit residual in the company currency and the sign-flipped credit residual in the company currency.
The consequence is that no exchange-difference entry is produced and no residual is left open.

when debit_side_company_amount lies within [ low of the credit side , high of the credit side ]
 and credit_side_company_amount lies within [ low of the debit side , high of the debit side ] :

records.purpose: Walks the items of one node, pairing debits with credits in the node order until one of the two lists is exhausted, which is what produces the sequence of partial matches.

operands.name: the items of the node, in the node order
operands.source: the reconciliation plan
operands.constraints: already sorted and split by currency

operands.name: the balance and the foreign amount of each item
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the item
operands.source: the Journal Items
operands.constraints: either one may be zero

preconditions.condition: The node holds at least one debit item and at least one credit item.
preconditions.otherwise: No pair can be formed and nothing is matched.

preconditions.condition: The children of the node have already been processed.
preconditions.otherwise: Items that belong to a nested plan would be paired before their own plan has been honoured.

procedure: Split the items of the node into a debit list, holding the items whose balance is positive or whose foreign amount is positive, and a credit list, holding the items whose balance is negative or whose foreign amount is negative, each keeping the node order.
Take the first debit item and the first credit item.
Compute one partial match between them.
Record the match when it produced an amount.
Advance the debit pointer when the debit item is exhausted, and the credit pointer when the credit item is exhausted.
Repeat until either list is exhausted.
records.formula:
debit list  = the items of the node whose balance > 0 or whose foreign amount > 0 , in node order
credit list = the items of the node whose balance < 0 or whose foreign amount < 0 , in node order
repeat: match( first remaining debit , first remaining credit ) , advancing each pointer when its item is exhausted , until either list is empty

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the loop itself; each partial match rounds its own amounts.
rounding.precision: The precisions of the currencies involved in each partial match.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, inside each partial match.
rounding.step: Not applicable to the loop.

When the credit side is fully matched, add the matched company amount to the residual of the credit item in the company currency.

Produce a correction only when the amount obtained is not zero at the precision of the company currency.
Correct the company-currency residual only: the foreign residual is not touched by this form of the difference.

operands.unit_or_currency: company currency, or the currency of the corrected item

preconditions.otherwise: The operation is refused with "You have to configure the 'Exchange Gain or Loss Journal' in your company settings, to manage automatically the booking of accounting entries related to differences between exchange rates."

procedure: Create a plain entry whose number is the placeholder, so that the number is taken at posting, in the exchange journal of the company, marked always tax exigible, in the company of the invoice-like entry among the two and otherwise in the company of the items.

Date it at the greater of the accounting dates of the two matched items, then push that date through the accounting-date rule of the exchange journal, then raise the running value to the date of each corrected item.

For each corrected item create a first item on the account of the corrected item: the company amount as a debit when it is negative and as a credit when it is positive, the foreign amount reversed in sign, the currency and the counterpart of the corrected item; give it the full-reconcile link of the corrected item and match it immediately with that item.

For each corrected item create a second item on the exchange expense account when the amount to fix is positive and on the exchange income account when it is negative: the company amount as a debit when it is positive and as a credit when it is negative, the foreign amount unchanged, the same currency and the same counterpart, and the analytic distribution when one was supplied.
Label both items "Currency exchange rate difference".
When the correction is expressed in the company currency, set the foreign amount of the pair to the company amount if the currency of the item is the company currency and to zero otherwise.
When the correction is expressed in the foreign currency, set the company amount of the pair to zero so that only the foreign amount is not zero.
Post the entry immediately when both matched items belong to posted entries, and otherwise leave it draft so that it is posted together with them.

item 1 : account of the corrected item , debit = company amount when it is negative else 0 , credit = company amount when it is positive else 0 , foreign amount = − the foreign amount to fix
item 2 : exchange expense account when the amount to fix is positive, exchange income account otherwise , debit = company amount when it is positive else 0 , credit = − company amount when it is negative else 0 , foreign amount = the foreign amount to fix

records.purpose: Decides which connected batches of matched items net to zero, so that each such batch receives one Full Reconciliation and the documents behind it can be reported as paid.

operands.source: the reconciliation just performed

operands.source: the Journal Items of the batch
operands.constraints: tested at the company precision when the batch uses more than one currency

operands.name: the residual of each item in its own currency

procedure: Take every item touched by the plan and extend the set with every item transitively matched with them through their matching numbers, ignoring imported numbers.
Group the extended set into connected batches: two items are in the same batch when they share a matching number.
For each batch, count an item as reconciled when it is already flagged reconciled.

Otherwise count an item as reconciled when it participates in at least one match and, for a batch that uses more than one currency, its residual in the company currency is zero at the company precision; or, for a batch that uses exactly one currency, its residual in that currency is zero at that precision.
Do not count an item that participates in no match at all, even when both its residuals are zero, which covers an item with a zero balance and a non-zero foreign amount.
Produce, for a batch in which every item counts as reconciled, one Full Reconciliation carrying every match and every item of the batch.
records.formula: batch_is_fully_reconciled = every item of the batch counts as reconciled , where an item counts as reconciled when it is already flagged reconciled , or it participates in at least one match and its residual is zero at the precision of the company currency (batch of several currencies) or of the single currency of the batch (batch of one currency)

rounding.precision: The company currency for a batch of several currencies, the single currency of the batch otherwise.
rounding.step: At each zero test, once per item.

preconditions.otherwise: Any write of a matching number that does not already start with the letter I is rewritten as the letter I followed by the supplied text, unless the caller explicitly bypasses the rule.

procedure: Take every match of the extended set, ordered by ascending identifier; the matches form an undirected graph whose vertices are items and whose edges are matches.
Maintain a mapping from item to component number and a mapping from component number to the list of its items.
For each match, look up the component of its debit item and of its credit item.
When both are known and different, merge the two components into the one with the smaller number and renumber every item of the larger component.
When only the debit item is known, add the credit item to that component; when only the credit item is known, add the debit item to that component.
When neither is known, create a new component whose number is the identifier of this match and which contains both items.
Write the matching number of every item: the decimal identifier of its Full Reconciliation when it has one, and otherwise the letter P followed by the component number.
Clear the matching number of every item of the extended set that ended up in no component.
records.formula:
component_number = the smallest match identifier of the connected component
matching_number( item ) = the decimal identifier of its Full Reconciliation when it has one
matching_number( item ) = "P" followed by the component number otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the numbers are whole identifiers.
rounding.precision: Whole numbers.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the matching number of each item
result.unit_or_currency: a decimal number, or the letter P followed by a decimal number, or the letter I followed by any text
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on each Journal Item and displayed as the label that links the items of one settlement.

edge_cases.case: Two components are merged by a later match.
edge_cases.outcome: The smaller component number wins, which makes the label stable as long as the earliest match survives.

edge_cases.case: A matching number written from outside the system.
edge_cases.outcome: It is prefixed with the letter I so that it cannot be confused with a real one; at posting the imported numbers are collected, grouped by number and account, and each group whose entries are all posted is reconciled with exchange differences and cash-basis entries suppressed, the account being switched to allow matching first when it does not, with a log of that configuration change.

edge_cases.case: An inconsistent matching number.
edge_cases.outcome: The validation refuses a number that is neither a decimal number nor the letter P followed by digits nor the letter I followed by anything; an imported number on an item that already participates in real matches, refused with "A temporary number can not be used in a real matching"; a partial number on an item with no match; a partial number on an item that has a Full Reconciliation; a decimal number on an item with no Full Reconciliation; a decimal number different from the identifier of the Full Reconciliation; and no number at all on an item that participates in matches.

worked_examples.description: Three items joined by two matches whose identifiers are seventeen and twenty-three
worked_examples.narrative: The first match creates a component numbered seventeen holding the two items; the second match finds its debit item already known and adds the third item to that component, so all three carry the letter P followed by seventeen, the smallest match identifier of the component.

worked_examples.description: The same three items once the batch nets to zero
worked_examples.narrative: Once a Full Reconciliation exists, each item carries its decimal identifier instead of the partial label.

records.name: The resolution of imported matching numbers at posting
records.purpose: Turns the matching labels carried by items loaded from outside into real matches, so that a ledger imported with its settlement history reaches the same residuals and the same Full Reconciliations as one built inside the system.

operands.name: imported matching number of an item
operands.unit_or_currency: a text beginning with the letter I
operands.source: the matching number written from outside the system on a Journal Item
operands.constraints: any write of a matching number that does not already begin with the letter I is rewritten as the letter I followed by the supplied text, unless the caller explicitly bypasses the rule

operands.name: account of each item carrying the number
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: the grouping is made on the pair of the number and the account, so the same imported number on two accounts makes two groups

operands.name: state of the entry of each item of a group
operands.source: the Journal Entry of each item
operands.constraints: every entry of the group must be posted before the group is resolved

operands.name: reconciliation flag of the account
operands.source: the Account
operands.constraints: switched on when it is off, and the configuration change is logged

operands.name: balance and foreign amount of each item of the group
operands.source: the Journal Items of the group
operands.constraints: they are what the reconciliation algorithm matches once the group is resolved

preconditions.condition: The matching number begins with the letter I, which marks it as written from outside.
preconditions.otherwise: The number is a real one produced by the component numbering of the matches and is not resolved; it is the decimal identifier of a Full Reconciliation or the letter P followed by a component number.

preconditions.condition: Every entry of the group formed by one imported number and one account is posted.
preconditions.otherwise: The group is left untouched, and the resolution is attempted again when the remaining entries of the group are posted.

preconditions.condition: The items of the group carry no real match yet.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused with "A temporary number can not be used in a real matching", because a temporary number may not sit on an item that already participates in real matches.

procedure: At posting, collect the distinct imported matching numbers found among the items being posted.
Group every item carrying one of those numbers by the pair of the number and the account, so that the same imported number used on two accounts forms two independent groups.
Take each group in turn and test whether every entry of the group is posted; leave the group untouched when at least one entry is still draft.
When the account of a resolvable group does not allow matching, switch the flag on and log that the configuration was changed.
Reconcile the items of the group with the reconciliation algorithm, with exchange differences and cash-basis entries suppressed.

Let the ordinary numbering of the matches replace the imported label: each item then carries the decimal identifier of the Full Reconciliation of its batch, or the letter P followed by its component number.
records.formula:
stored_matching_number = "I" + the supplied text          for every write that does not already begin with the letter I
group( item )          = ( the imported matching number of the item , the account of the item )
resolvable( group )    = every entry of the group is posted
matched amounts of a resolvable group = the amounts produced by the reconciliation algorithm on the items of the group, with exchange differences and cash-basis entries suppressed

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the resolution itself; the amounts of the matches it triggers are rounded by the reconciliation algorithm.
rounding.precision: The matched amount carries the precision of the company currency, and the two currency amounts of a match the precision of the currency of their side.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied by the reconciliation algorithm when it computes each partial match.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the grouping and the resolution; rounding happens inside the matches that follow.

result.name: the matches created for each resolvable group, and the real matching number that replaces the imported label
result.unit_or_currency: Partial Reconciliations in the company currency and in the currency of each side, and one Full Reconciliation when the group nets to zero
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the matches of the items and as the matching number of each item; the imported label disappears once the group is resolved.

edge_cases.case: One entry of the group is still draft.
edge_cases.outcome: No match is created for that group; the whole group waits until every one of its entries is posted.

edge_cases.case: The account of the group does not allow matching.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is switched on before the group is reconciled and the configuration change is logged.

edge_cases.case: The same imported number appears on two different accounts.
edge_cases.outcome: Two groups are formed, one per account, and each is resolved on its own.

edge_cases.case: The group would produce an exchange difference.
edge_cases.outcome: Exchange differences are suppressed during this reconciliation, and so are cash-basis entries.

edge_cases.case: An imported number is written on an item that already participates in real matches.
edge_cases.outcome: Refused with "A temporary number can not be used in a real matching".

edge_cases.case: A caller writes a matching number that does not begin with the letter I and does not bypass the rule.
edge_cases.outcome: The stored value becomes the letter I followed by the supplied text, so that an imported label can never be confused with a real one.

edge_cases.case: The items of a resolvable group do not net to zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The matches are still created and the items keep a residual; the group receives the letter P followed by its component number instead of a Full Reconciliation identifier.

worked_examples.description: Two imported items on the payable account 400000, both carrying the label written from outside as REF42 and both belonging to posted entries

expected_outputs.reconciliation_flag_of_the_account: switched on and the change logged
expected_outputs.matching_number_after_resolution: the decimal identifier of the Full Reconciliation

worked_examples.narrative: The label supplied by the import is stored as the letter I followed by REF42. At posting the two items form one group, because they share that number and the account 400000. Both entries are posted, so the group is resolvable; the account did not allow matching, so the flag is switched on and the change is logged. The reconciliation algorithm matches the credit of 1 200.00 against the debit of 1 200.00 in the company currency, leaving a residual of 0.00 on each side, and the batch nets to zero, so one Full Reconciliation is created and both items carry its decimal identifier as their matching number in place of the imported label.

worked_examples.description: The same two items while the second entry is still draft
worked_examples.narrative: The group is formed but is not resolvable, because one of its entries is still draft. No match is created, the posted item keeps its residual of minus 1 200.00 and both items keep the imported label until the draft entry is posted.

records.name: The fiscal year of a company containing a date
records.purpose: Gives the first and the last day of the accounting year that contains a date, which is what the year-range numbering, the period boundaries and the year-end reports all rest on.

operands.name: the date
operands.source: the accounting date of the entry, or any date the caller asks about
operands.constraints: a valid date

operands.name: the fiscal-year end day
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: from one to thirty-one; reduced to the number of days of the month when it overflows

operands.name: the fiscal-year end month
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: from January to December

preconditions.condition: The company defines a fiscal-year end day and month.
preconditions.otherwise: The thirty-first of December is used, which makes the fiscal year the calendar year.

procedure: When the end month is December and the end day is thirty-one, the fiscal year is the calendar year of the date.
Otherwise build the end date from the year of the input date, the end month and the end day, reducing the day to the number of days of that month when it overflows.
When the input date is after that end date, the fiscal year runs from the day after the end date to the same day one year later.
Otherwise the fiscal year runs from the day after the equivalent end date of the previous year to that end date.
records.formula:
fiscal_year( date ) = the calendar year of the date                                          when the end month is December and the end day is 31
END = ( year of the date , end month , min( end day , number of days of that month ) )
fiscal_year( date ) = the day after END … the same day one year later                     when the date is after END
fiscal_year( date ) = the day after the END of the previous year … END                     otherwise

rounding.what: The end day only, when it overflows the month.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.method: The day is reduced to the number of days of that month in that year.
rounding.step: When the end date is built, before the comparison with the input date.

result.name: the first and the last day of the fiscal year containing the date
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it supplies the period boundaries of the year-range periodicities, the year part of a fresh chain and the partition key of a renumbering.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year ends on the twenty-ninth of February and the year asked about is not a leap year.
edge_cases.outcome: The day is capped at the twenty-eighth.

edge_cases.case: The date is exactly the end date.
edge_cases.outcome: It belongs to the fiscal year that ends on that day, because the test is strictly after.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year is the calendar year.
edge_cases.outcome: The first branch applies and no end date needs to be built.

worked_examples.description: A company whose fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of March
worked_examples.narrative: The third and the thirty-first of March are not after the end date of the thirty-first of March, so both fall in the year that runs from the first of April two thousand and twenty-five to the thirty-first of March two thousand and twenty-six; the first of April is after it and opens the following year.

worked_examples.description: A company whose fiscal year ends on the twenty-ninth of February, asked about a year that is not a leap year
worked_examples.narrative: The end day is reduced to the number of days of February in that year, that is twenty-eight.

records.name: The default values of a new opening entry
records.purpose: Fixes the journal, the reference and above all the date of the entry that carries the initial balance of every account, so that the opening balances sit just before the first day the company trades.

operands.name: the opening date of the company
operands.source: the company
operands.constraints: when absent, the first of January of the current year is used in its place

operands.name: the first miscellaneous journal of the company
operands.source: the journals of the company
operands.constraints: must exist

preconditions.condition: The company has at least one miscellaneous journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation fails with "Please install a chart of accounts or create a miscellaneous journal before proceeding."

procedure: Set the reference of the entry to "Opening Journal Entry".
Set the company of the entry to the company concerned.
Set the journal to the first miscellaneous journal of that company.
Set the date to the opening date of the company minus one day.
When the company has no opening date, take the first of January of the current year minus one day, that is the thirty-first of December of the previous year.
records.formula:
opening_entry_date = opening date of the company − 1 day
opening_entry_date = the first of January of the current year − 1 day = the thirty-first of December of the previous year , when the company has no opening date

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a whole date.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the reference, company, journal and date of the opening entry
result.unit_or_currency: a text, a company, a journal and a date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry that carries the opening balances.

edge_cases.case: The company has no miscellaneous journal.
edge_cases.outcome: The operation fails with the message asking for a chart of accounts or a miscellaneous journal.

edge_cases.case: The company has no opening date.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry is dated the thirty-first of December of the previous year.

edge_cases.case: The opening date is the first day of a month.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry is dated the last day of the previous month.

worked_examples.description: A new company that starts trading on the first of January two thousand and twenty-six
worked_examples.narrative: The opening date minus one day is the thirty-first of December two thousand and twenty-five, so the opening balances sit in the day before the company begins to trade.

records.name: The code of a created current-year-earnings account
records.purpose: Finds a free code for the account on which the opening entry is balanced, when the company has no account of the current-year-earnings type yet.

operands.name: the starting code
operands.source: the fixed starting value of the search, which is 999999
operands.constraints: decreased by one at each step

operands.name: the codes already used in the company
operands.source: the accounts of the company, including the archived ones
operands.constraints: an archived account still occupies its code

preconditions.condition: The company has no account of the type Current Year Earnings.
preconditions.otherwise: The existing account is used and no code is generated.

procedure: Start from the code 999999.
While an account with that code exists in the company, including the archived ones, decrease the code by one.
Create the account with the code obtained, the name "Profit or Loss Appropriation" and the type Current Year Earnings.
records.formula: code = 999999 − k , where k is the smallest whole number, counted from zero, for which no account of the company, archived ones included, carries that code

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the code is a whole number written as six digits.
rounding.precision: Six digits.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the code of the created current-year-earnings account
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the created Account, whose name is "Profit or Loss Appropriation" and whose type is Current Year Earnings.

edge_cases.case: The code 999999 is free.
edge_cases.outcome: It is used without any decrease.

edge_cases.case: An archived account holds a code in the range.
edge_cases.outcome: That code is skipped, because archived accounts are included in the test.

edge_cases.case: Several codes at the top of the range are taken.
edge_cases.outcome: The walk continues downwards until a free one is found.

worked_examples.description: A generic chart in which the highest code is already taken
worked_examples.narrative: The starting code exists in the company, so the walk decreases it by one and creates the account with the next code down.

worked_examples.description: A fresh chart with nothing in the range
worked_examples.narrative: The starting code is free, so it is used unchanged.

records.name: Updating the opening entry and its balancing items
records.purpose: Applies a set of requested opening balances to the opening entry and keeps it balanced by adjusting the two items on the current-year-earnings account.

operands.name: the requested pairs of a debit to set and a credit to set, per account
operands.source: the caller, typically an import of opening balances
operands.constraints: either member may be absent, which means that side is left alone

operands.name: the existing items of the opening entry
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of each account
operands.source: the opening Journal Entry
operands.constraints: indexed by the pair of account and side, the side being debit when the balance or the foreign amount is positive and credit otherwise

operands.name: the balance of each existing item on the balancing account
operands.source: the items of the opening entry on the current-year-earnings account
operands.constraints: their credit total minus their debit total initialises the running open balance

operands.name: the currency of each account and the rate at the date of the entry
operands.source: the account and the currency table
operands.constraints: used to convert a balance into the foreign amount of an item

preconditions.condition: No opening entry exists, or the existing one is still draft.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation is refused with the message that the opening balance cannot be imported because the opening entry is already posted.

preconditions.condition: The company has an account of the type Current Year Earnings.
preconditions.otherwise: One is created with the next free code counted down from 999999, the name "Profit or Loss Appropriation" and that type.

procedure: Refuse the operation when an opening entry exists and is not draft.
Index the existing items of the opening entry by the pair of account and side, the side being debit when the balance or the foreign amount is positive and credit otherwise.
Initialise the running open balance with the credit total minus the debit total of the existing items on the balancing account.
For every requested account, side and amount, make the amount positive for the debit side and negative for the credit side, and add it to the running open balance.
When the amount is zero for the company currency, delete every existing item of that account and side and subtract each deleted balance from the running open balance.
Otherwise, when such an item exists, subtract its old balance from the running open balance, update the first one with the new balance and the converted foreign amount, and delete the others.

Otherwise create a new item labelled "Opening balance" with that balance, that foreign amount, the currency of the account when the account forces one and the company currency otherwise; the conversion of a balance into the foreign amount uses the company currency converted to the account currency at the date of the entry.

Add the two balancing items on the current-year-earnings account, labelled "Automatic Balancing Line", the debit side being the greater of minus the running open balance and zero and the credit side being minus the greater of the running open balance and zero, with a foreign amount equal to their balance.
Write the collected commands on the existing entry, or create the entry with the default values when it does not exist.
records.formula:
running_open_balance = ( credit total − debit total of the existing items on the balancing account ) + sum of the requested amounts , a requested amount being positive on the debit side and negative on the credit side , each replaced or deleted existing balance being removed from the running total first
balancing_debit  = max( − running_open_balance , 0 )
balancing_credit = − max( running_open_balance , 0 )

rounding.what: Each requested amount, the converted foreign amount of each item and the two balancing amounts.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the balances, the currency of the account for the foreign amounts.
rounding.step: On each amount as it is written on an item, and on the balancing amounts once the running open balance is final; the zero test that deletes an item is made for the company currency.

result.name: the items of the opening entry, including the balancing items
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of each account
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the Journal Items of the opening Journal Entry, which balances by construction.

edge_cases.case: A requested amount is zero for the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Every existing item of that account and side is deleted and each deleted balance is removed from the running open balance.

edge_cases.case: Several items already exist for one account and side.
edge_cases.outcome: The first is updated and the others are deleted.

edge_cases.case: The opening entry is already posted.
edge_cases.outcome: The operation is refused.

edge_cases.case: The account forces a currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The item carries that currency and its foreign amount is the balance converted at the date of the entry; otherwise the item carries the company currency.

worked_examples.description: A new company giving opening balances to a bank account and a supplier account
worked_examples.narrative: The running open balance after the two requested amounts is ten thousand minus four thousand, that is 6 000.00, so the balancing item takes a credit of 6 000.00 and the entry balances.

worked_examples.description: The wider opening of the end-to-end example
worked_examples.narrative: Twelve thousand plus five thousand minus three thousand is 14 000.00, so the balancing item takes a credit of 14 000.00; the entry is posted and takes the first number of the December chain.

records.name: The amount receivable of a partner
records.purpose: Gives what a counterpart still owes the company, which is the figure shown on the partner ledger and the numerator of the days of sales outstanding.

operands.name: the residual in the company currency of each item of the partner
operands.source: the posted, unreconciled Journal Items of that partner whose account type is Receivable
operands.constraints: read in the company hierarchy of the active company

preconditions.condition: The active company hierarchy is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure cannot be scoped and is not meaningful.

preconditions.condition: The partner has at least one posted, unreconciled receivable item.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure is zero.

procedure: Select the Journal Items of the partner that are posted, are not reconciled, and sit on an account of the type Receivable.
Restrict the selection to the company hierarchy of the active company.
Add up their residuals in the company currency.
records.formula: partner_credit = sum of amount_residual over the posted, unreconciled items of that partner whose account type is Receivable, in the company hierarchy of the active company

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: each residual is already at the precision of the company currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each residual.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the sum.

result.name: amount receivable of the partner
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the partner and in the partner ledger; it is read in the company currency.

edge_cases.case: The partner has no such item.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is zero.

edge_cases.case: An item sits in another company of the hierarchy.
edge_cases.outcome: It is included, because the scope is the company hierarchy of the active company.

edge_cases.case: An item is reconciled.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, whatever its balance.

worked_examples.description: A customer with two open receivable items
