worked_examples.narrative: The two residuals add up to 12 100.00, which is what the customer still owes.

records.name: The amount payable of a partner
records.purpose: Gives what the company still owes a counterpart, shown as a positive figure on the partner ledger.

operands.name: the residual in the company currency of each item of the partner
operands.source: the posted, unreconciled Journal Items of that partner whose account type is Payable
operands.constraints: read in the company hierarchy of the active company; the residuals are negative

preconditions.condition: The active company hierarchy is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure cannot be scoped and is not meaningful.

preconditions.condition: The partner has at least one posted, unreconciled payable item.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure is zero.

procedure: Select the Journal Items of the partner that are posted, are not reconciled, and sit on an account of the type Payable.
Restrict the selection to the same company hierarchy as the receivable figure.
Add up their residuals in the company currency.
Reverse the sign of the sum, so that an amount owed is reported as a positive figure.
records.formula: partner_debit = − ( sum of amount_residual over the posted, unreconciled items of that partner whose account type is Payable, in the same hierarchy )

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: each residual is already at the precision of the company currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each residual.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the sum or in the sign reversal.

result.name: amount payable of the partner
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the partner and in the partner ledger; it is read in the company currency.

edge_cases.case: The partner has no such item.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is zero.

edge_cases.case: A payable item has a positive residual, for example an advance paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign reversal makes it reduce the reported amount payable.

edge_cases.case: An item is reconciled.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded.

worked_examples.description: A supplier with two open payable items
worked_examples.narrative: The two residuals add up to minus 4 200.00 and the sign reversal reports the amount payable as 4 200.00.

records.name: The total invoiced of a partner
records.purpose: Gives the untaxed turnover recorded against a counterpart and everything below it in the counterpart hierarchy, which is the figure the partner form shows as the business done with that counterpart.

operands.name: the untaxed subtotal of each customer invoice and credit note
operands.source: the customer invoices and credit notes of the partner and of every partner below it in the hierarchy
operands.constraints: draft and cancelled documents are excluded

preconditions.condition: The counterpart hierarchy of the partner is known.
preconditions.otherwise: Only the documents of the partner itself are counted.

procedure: Select the customer invoices and credit notes of the partner and of every partner below it in the hierarchy.
Exclude the documents that are draft and the documents that are cancelled.
Add up their untaxed subtotals.
records.formula: total_invoiced = sum of the untaxed subtotals of the customer invoices and credit notes of the partner and of every partner below it in the hierarchy, excluding draft and cancelled documents

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: each untaxed subtotal is already at the precision of its document.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each document total.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the sum.

result.name: total invoiced
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the partner; it is the denominator of the days of sales outstanding when the tax-included variant is used.

edge_cases.case: The partner has children in the counterpart hierarchy.
edge_cases.outcome: Their documents are included, so a parent counterpart shows the business of the whole group.

edge_cases.case: A document is still draft.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded.

edge_cases.case: A credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: It is included and reduces the total, because its untaxed subtotal carries the opposite orientation.

worked_examples.description: A customer with two posted invoices and one posted credit note
worked_examples.narrative: Forty thousand plus fifteen thousand minus five thousand is 50 000.00; the draft invoice is excluded.

records.name: The days of sales outstanding of a partner
records.purpose: Expresses what a counterpart still owes as a number of days of its own sales, which is the collection indicator shown on the partner.

operands.name: amount receivable of the partner
operands.source: the sum of the residuals of the posted, unreconciled receivable items of the partner
operands.constraints: positive or zero

operands.name: the tax-included total invoiced
operands.source: the sum of the signed company-currency totals of the sale documents of the commercial entity that are neither draft nor cancelled, in the active company
operands.constraints: the result is zero when this total is zero

operands.name: the earliest document date among those sale documents
operands.source: the sale documents of the commercial entity that are neither draft nor cancelled, in the active company
operands.constraints: when the partner has no such document the current date is used, so the day count is zero

operands.name: the current date
operands.source: the clock
operands.constraints: a valid date

preconditions.condition: The tax-included total of the sale documents is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The result is zero.

preconditions.condition: The partner has at least one sale document that is neither draft nor cancelled.
preconditions.otherwise: The earliest date used is the current date, so the day count is zero and the result is zero.

procedure: Take the earliest document date among the sale documents of the commercial entity that are neither draft nor cancelled, in the active company.
Subtract that date from the current date to obtain the number of days since the oldest invoice.
Divide the amount receivable of the partner by the tax-included total of those documents.
Multiply the quotient by the number of days since the oldest invoice.
records.formula:
days_since_oldest_invoice = today − ( the earliest document date among the sale documents of the commercial entity that are neither draft nor cancelled, in the active company )
days_sales_outstanding = ( partner_credit ÷ total_invoiced_tax_included ) × days_since_oldest_invoice

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the rule itself: the quotient is carried at full precision and multiplied by a whole number of days.
rounding.precision: The two monetary inputs are at the precision of the company currency; the day count is a whole number of days.
rounding.method: Not applicable: the result is displayed as a number of days.
rounding.step: No rounding step inside the formula.

result.name: days of sales outstanding
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the partner as a collection indicator.

edge_cases.case: The tax-included total is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero.

edge_cases.case: The partner has no sale document that is neither draft nor cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: The earliest date used is the current date, so the day count is zero and the result is zero.

edge_cases.case: The amount receivable is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The quotient is zero and the result is zero, whatever the day count.

worked_examples.description: A customer with 12 100.00 open on receivable accounts
worked_examples.narrative: Twelve thousand one hundred divided by sixty thousand five hundred is zero point two, multiplied by ninety days gives eighteen days.

records.name: Generating an unused account code
records.purpose: Finds a free code for a new account derived from an existing one, by increasing the digit run of the starting code and, when that is exhausted, by appending a copy marker.

operands.name: the starting code
operands.source: the account the new one is derived from
operands.constraints: split by the rule that the longest trailing run of non-digits is the tail, the digit run immediately before it is the number, and everything before is the head

operands.name: the original width of the digit run
operands.source: the starting code
operands.constraints: the candidates are written with leading zeros to that width and the walk stops when the number plus the step reaches ten raised to that width

operands.name: the codes already used
operands.source: the accounts of the active company, of its ancestors and of its descendants, together with the codes already handed out in this same operation
operands.constraints: a candidate is available only when no such account carries it and it has not already been handed out

preconditions.condition: The starting code carries a digit run.
preconditions.otherwise: The walk over candidates is skipped and the fallback codes are used.

preconditions.condition: At least one candidate or fallback is available.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation is refused with "Cannot generate an unused account code."

procedure: Split the starting code: the longest trailing run of non-digits is the tail, the digit run immediately before it is the number, and everything before is the head.
For each step counted from one, form the candidate as the head, the number increased by the step written with leading zeros to the original width, and the tail.
Continue while the number plus the step is strictly less than ten raised to the original width.

When the digit run is empty, or the walk is exhausted, form the fallback codes: the starting code followed by the marker for the first one, and the starting code followed by the marker and the step plus one for the next ninety-eight.

Take the first candidate that is available, availability meaning that no account with that code belongs to the active company, to any of its ancestors or to any of its descendants, and that the code has not already been handed out in this same operation.
records.formula:
candidate( k ) = head + ( number + k , written with leading zeros to the original width ) + tail , for k = 1, 2, 3 … while number + k < 10^(original width)
fallback( 0 ) = starting_code + ".copy"
fallback( n ) = starting_code + ".copy" + ( n + 1 )      for n = 1 … 98

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the number is a whole number and the leading zeros restore the original width.
rounding.precision: The original width of the digit run.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the generated account code
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the new Account; the code must be unique in the company and in every ancestor and descendant of it.

edge_cases.case: The starting code has no digit run.
edge_cases.outcome: The candidates are skipped and the fallback codes are used, the first being the starting code followed by the copy marker.

edge_cases.case: The digit run would overflow its width.
edge_cases.outcome: The walk stops and the fallback codes are used, so a code never grows a digit.

edge_cases.case: Two accounts are generated in the same operation.
edge_cases.outcome: A code already handed out in that operation is not available to the second one.

edge_cases.case: No candidate and no fallback is available.
edge_cases.outcome: The operation is refused with "Cannot generate an unused account code."

worked_examples.description: A code whose digit run can simply be increased
worked_examples.narrative: The number four hundred thousand plus one is 400001, written on six digits, and no account of the company or of its ancestors or descendants carries it, so it is used.

worked_examples.description: A code with no digit run
worked_examples.narrative: There is no digit run, so the fallback codes are used; the first is already taken, so the next one, which carries the step plus one, is used.

records.name: The balance of a liquidity journal that carries a foreign currency
records.purpose: Gives the figure the accounting dashboard shows for a bank, cash or credit-card journal whose account is kept in a currency other than the company currency, which is the balance of the account expressed in that currency.

operands.name: the foreign amount of each item on the default account of the journal
operands.source: the Journal Items on the default account of the journal, whatever journal they were booked in
operands.constraints: the entry must not be cancelled and the display type must not be a section, a subsection or a note

preconditions.condition: The journal carries a foreign currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The company-currency variant applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The journal has a default account.
preconditions.otherwise: No items can be selected and the balance is zero.

procedure: Select every Journal Item that sits on the default account of the journal, whichever journal it was booked in, because the aggregation is driven by the account and not by the journal.
Exclude the items whose entry is cancelled.
Exclude the items whose display type is a section, a subsection or a note.
Add up their foreign amounts.
records.formula: journal_balance = sum of amount_currency over the items on the default account of the journal whose entry is not cancelled and whose display type is not a section, subsection or note

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: each foreign amount is already at the precision of the currency of the journal.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency of the journal.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each item amount.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the sum.

result.name: the balance of the liquidity journal
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the accounting dashboard card of the journal, together with the number of items behind it.

edge_cases.case: An amount is booked on the bank account from another journal.
edge_cases.outcome: It is included, because the aggregation is deliberately not restricted to the journal itself; a transfer booked elsewhere on the same bank account is part of the bank balance.

edge_cases.case: An entry is cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: Its items are excluded.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no item on its default account.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance is zero.

worked_examples.description: A bank journal kept in United States dollars
worked_examples.narrative: The cancelled entry and the note are excluded, so the balance is one thousand minus two hundred and fifty, that is 750.00 dollars.

records.name: The balance of a liquidity journal kept in the company currency
records.purpose: Gives the figure the accounting dashboard shows for a bank, cash or credit-card journal whose account is kept in the company currency, which is the balance of the account in that currency.

operands.name: the balance of each item on the default account of the journal
operands.source: the Journal Items on the default account of the journal, whatever journal they were booked in
operands.constraints: the entry must not be cancelled and the display type must not be a section, a subsection or a note

preconditions.condition: The journal carries no foreign currency, or its currency is the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The foreign-currency variant applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The journal has a default account.
preconditions.otherwise: No items can be selected and the balance is zero.

procedure: Select every Journal Item that sits on the default account of the journal, whichever journal it was booked in.
Exclude the items whose entry is cancelled.
Exclude the items whose display type is a section, a subsection or a note.
Add up their balances in the company currency.
records.formula: journal_balance = sum of balance over the items on the default account of the journal whose entry is not cancelled and whose display type is not a section, subsection or note

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: each balance is already at the precision of the company currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each item amount.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the sum.

result.name: the balance of the liquidity journal
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the accounting dashboard card of the journal, together with the number of items behind it.

edge_cases.case: A transfer is booked on the bank account from a miscellaneous journal.
edge_cases.outcome: It is included, because the aggregation is driven by the account and not by the journal.

edge_cases.case: An entry is cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: Its items are excluded.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no item on its default account.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance is zero.

worked_examples.description: A bank journal in the company currency after an opening balance and a customer receipt
worked_examples.narrative: Twelve thousand plus nine hundred and nine point zero nine is 12 909.09 euros.

records.name: Whether a journal still has entries to secure
records.purpose: Tells the accounting dashboard whether a journal that secures its entries still holds an entry that has not been hashed, without walking the whole chain.

operands.name: the entries of the journal that the chain selection returns
operands.source: the same selection the hash verification uses
operands.constraints: the walk stops as soon as one entry is found

preconditions.condition: The journal secures its entries with a hash.
preconditions.otherwise: The indicator is not shown for that journal.

procedure: Run the chain selection of the hash verification over the journal.
Stop as soon as one entry is found that still has to be secured.
Report that the journal has entries to hash when the selection returned at least one such entry, and that it has none otherwise.
records.formula: entries_to_hash( journal ) = ( the chain selection of the hash verification, stopped at the first result, returns at least one entry )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the answer is a count stopped at one.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the journal still has entries to secure
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the accounting dashboard card of the journal.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no hashed entry at all.
edge_cases.outcome: Every entry of it that qualifies is still to secure, so the indicator answers yes as soon as one exists.

edge_cases.case: Every qualifying entry is already hashed.
edge_cases.outcome: The selection returns nothing and the indicator answers no.

edge_cases.case: The journal does not secure its entries.
edge_cases.outcome: The indicator does not apply.

worked_examples.description: A miscellaneous journal on which the hash has just been switched on
worked_examples.narrative: The selection finds an entry immediately and stops, so the dashboard reports that the journal still has entries to secure.

worked_examples.description: The same journal after the securing operation
worked_examples.narrative: The selection returns nothing, so the indicator disappears.

records.name: The total amount of an automatic transfer computed from the percentage
records.purpose: Gives the amount that a chosen share of the selected items represents, which is the figure the accountant reads when preparing a cut-off or a transfer.

operands.name: the percentage
operands.source: typed by the accountant, or computed from a typed total amount
operands.constraints: handled with two decimals, at most one hundred

operands.name: the sum of the balances of the selected items
operands.source: the Journal Items selected for the transfer
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

preconditions.condition: At least one item is selected.
preconditions.otherwise: The sum of balances is zero and the total amount is zero.

procedure: Add up the balances of the selected items.
Divide the percentage by one hundred.
Multiply the quotient by the sum of the balances.
records.formula: total_amount = ( percentage ÷ 100 ) × ( sum of the balances of the selected items )

rounding.what: The percentage, which is handled with two decimals, and the resulting amount.
rounding.precision: Two decimals for the percentage, the rounding step of the company currency for the amount.
rounding.step: The percentage is held at two decimals; the amount is rounded to the company currency when it is written on an item.

result.name: total amount of the transfer
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the transfer form; it and the percentage are inverse views of each other.

edge_cases.case: The percentage is one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: The total amount is the whole sum of the selected balances.

edge_cases.case: The sum of balances is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The total amount is zero, whatever the percentage.

edge_cases.case: The sum of balances is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The total amount is negative and the accrual account is deduced as a revenue account.

worked_examples.description: A full deferral of a revenue booked at the end of December
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred divided by one hundred is one, multiplied by minus 1 200.00 gives minus 1 200.00: the whole revenue is deferred.

worked_examples.description: A half deferral of the same revenue
worked_examples.narrative: Fifty divided by one hundred is one half, multiplied by minus 1 200.00 gives minus 600.00.

records.name: The percentage of an automatic transfer computed from the total amount
records.purpose: Gives the share that a chosen amount represents of the selected items, which is the inverse view of the total amount and the value actually applied to every item of the transfer.

operands.name: the total amount
operands.source: typed by the accountant, or computed from a typed percentage
operands.constraints: rounded to the company currency

operands.name: the sum of the balances of the selected items
operands.source: the Journal Items selected for the transfer
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

preconditions.condition: The sum of the balances of the selected items is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The percentage is one hundred.

procedure: Add up the balances of the selected items.
Divide the total amount by that sum.
Multiply the quotient by one hundred.
Take the smaller of the result and one hundred; the minimum with one hundred exists to absorb a rounding error that would otherwise produce a value slightly above one hundred.
Use one hundred when the sum of balances is zero.
records.formula:
percentage = min( ( total_amount ÷ sum of the balances of the selected items ) × 100 , 100 )
percentage = 100    when the sum of balances is zero

rounding.what: The percentage.
rounding.precision: Two decimals.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, with an explicit cap at one hundred.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by one hundred and before the value is applied to the items or written into a label.

result.name: the percentage of the transfer
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the transfer form and written into the label of every produced item, with two decimals, when it is not one hundred.

edge_cases.case: The sum of balances is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The percentage is one hundred.

edge_cases.case: A rounding error pushes the quotient slightly above one.
edge_cases.outcome: The minimum with one hundred caps it, so no transfer ever exceeds the selected amount.

edge_cases.case: The total amount equals the sum of balances.
edge_cases.outcome: The percentage is exactly one hundred and the labels omit the percentage.

worked_examples.description: A transfer of the whole selected amount

expected_outputs.label_shape: Cut-off followed by the source number, with no percentage

worked_examples.narrative: The quotient is one, so the percentage is one hundred and the labels of the produced items carry no percentage.

worked_examples.description: A transfer of a quarter of the selected amount

expected_outputs.label_shape: Cut-off followed by the source number and 25.00 per cent

worked_examples.narrative: Minus three hundred divided by minus one thousand two hundred is zero point two five, so the percentage is twenty-five and the labels carry it with two decimals.

records.name: The nature of the accrual account deduced from the sign of the selection
records.purpose: Decides whether an automatic transfer books its counterpart on a revenue accrual account or on an expense accrual account, from the sign of the amounts being transferred.

operands.name: the sum of the balances of the selected items
operands.source: the Journal Items selected for the transfer
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

preconditions.condition: At least one item is selected.
preconditions.otherwise: The sum is zero and the expense nature is deduced, because the test is on a strictly negative sum.

procedure: Add up the balances of the selected items.
Deduce the revenue nature when that sum is negative, because a credit balance is a revenue.
Deduce the expense nature otherwise.
records.formula:
account_type = revenue    when the sum of the selected balances is negative
account_type = expense    otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: only the sign of the sum is read.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency, at which the sum is already expressed.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the nature of the accrual account to use
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it selects which of the two accrual accounts of the transfer form is used on the produced items.

edge_cases.case: The sum is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The expense nature is deduced, because the test is on a strictly negative sum.

edge_cases.case: The selection mixes debits and credits.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the sign of the total decides, not the individual items.

edge_cases.case: The selection is a revenue booked as a credit.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is negative and the revenue accrual account, which is a deferred-revenue liability account, is used.

worked_examples.description: A revenue of 1 200.00 deferred to the following period
worked_examples.narrative: The sum is negative, so the revenue accrual account, a deferred-revenue liability account, is used.

worked_examples.description: An expense of 1 200.00 deferred to the following period
worked_examples.narrative: The sum is positive, so the expense accrual account is used.

records.name: The reported amounts of a change-of-period transfer
records.purpose: Computes, for each selected item, the share of its debit, of its credit and of its foreign amount that is carried into the other period by a cut-off.

operands.name: the percentage of the transfer
operands.source: the transfer form, either typed or derived from a typed total amount
operands.constraints: handled with two decimals, at most one hundred

operands.name: the debit of the source item
operands.source: the selected Journal Item
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: the credit of the source item
operands.source: the selected Journal Item
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: the foreign amount of the source item
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the source item
operands.source: the selected Journal Item
operands.constraints: may be zero

preconditions.condition: The percentage of the transfer has been fixed.
preconditions.otherwise: The reported amounts cannot be computed.

procedure: Divide the percentage by one hundred.
Multiply the debit of the source item by that share and round the product to the company currency: this is the reported debit.
Multiply the credit of the source item by that share and round the product to the company currency: this is the reported credit.
Multiply the foreign amount of the source item by that share and round the product to the currency of the item: this is the reported foreign amount.

Label the items produced from this source "Cut-off" followed by the number of the source entry when the percentage is one hundred, and "Cut-off" followed by the number of the source entry and the percentage written with two decimals otherwise.
records.formula:
reported_debit           = round_to_company_currency( ( percentage ÷ 100 ) × debit )
reported_credit          = round_to_company_currency( ( percentage ÷ 100 ) × credit )
reported_amount_currency = round_to_item_currency(    ( percentage ÷ 100 ) × amount_currency )

rounding.what: The three reported amounts, and the percentage written into the label.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the reported debit and credit, the currency of the item for the reported foreign amount, and two decimals for the percentage in the label.
rounding.step: Each product is rounded immediately after the multiplication, before the amount is written on an item.

result.name: the reported debit, the reported credit and the reported foreign amount
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the source item
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the items of the destination entry and of the cancelling entry.

edge_cases.case: The percentage is one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: The reported amounts are the amounts of the source item and the label carries no percentage.

edge_cases.case: The source item has a zero foreign amount.
edge_cases.outcome: The reported foreign amount is zero and the produced items carry no foreign amount.

edge_cases.case: The rounding of the share leaves a remainder.
edge_cases.outcome: Each amount is rounded independently at its own precision, so the two mirrored entries always carry the same rounded figures and both balance.

worked_examples.description: A full deferral of a revenue of 1 200.00

expected_outputs.label: Cut-off followed by the number of the source entry

worked_examples.narrative: The share is one, so the reported amounts equal the amounts of the source item and the label omits the percentage.

worked_examples.description: A quarter deferral of the same revenue

expected_outputs.label: Cut-off followed by the number of the source entry and 25.00 per cent

worked_examples.narrative: One quarter of 1 200.00 is 300.00, and the label carries the percentage with two decimals.

records.name: The items of the destination entry of a change of period
records.purpose: States the two items produced per source item in the entry dated at the chosen date, which is the entry that brings the deferred amount into the new period.

operands.name: the reported debit, credit and foreign amount of the source item
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the source item
operands.source: the reported amounts of the transfer
operands.constraints: already rounded

operands.name: the account of the source item
operands.source: the selected Journal Item
operands.constraints: reused unchanged on the first item

operands.name: the accrual account
operands.source: the transfer form, revenue or expense according to the deduced nature
operands.constraints: used on the second item

operands.name: the chosen date
operands.source: the transfer form
operands.constraints: the date of the destination entry

preconditions.condition: The accrual account matching the deduced nature is set on the transfer form.
preconditions.otherwise: The transfer cannot be produced.

procedure: Create the destination entry dated at the chosen date.

For each source item create a first item on the account of the source item, carrying the reported debit as its debit, the reported credit as its credit and the reported foreign amount as its foreign amount.

Create a second item on the accrual account, revenue or expense according to the deduced nature, carrying the reported credit as its debit, the reported debit as its credit and minus the reported foreign amount as its foreign amount.
Give both items the counterpart and the analytic distribution of the source item.

Label both items "Cut-off" followed by the number of the source entry when the percentage is one hundred, and "Cut-off" followed by the number of the source entry and the percentage written with two decimals otherwise.
After posting, reconcile the pairs of mirror items that share a label, a reconcilable account, a counterpart, a currency and an analytic distribution.
records.formula:
destination item 1 : account of the source item , debit = reported_debit , credit = reported_credit , foreign amount = reported_amount_currency
destination item 2 : the accrual account            , debit = reported_credit , credit = reported_debit , foreign amount = − reported_amount_currency

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: the reported amounts are already at the precision of their currency.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the debit and the credit, the currency of the source item for the foreign amount.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the reported amounts were computed.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the item construction.

result.name: the pair of items of the destination entry, per source item
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the source item
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as Journal Items of the destination Journal Entry, which balances because the two items mirror each other.

edge_cases.case: Several source items are selected.
edge_cases.outcome: One pair is produced per source item, all in the same destination entry.

edge_cases.case: The accrual account is reconcilable.
edge_cases.outcome: The mirror items of the two entries are reconciled with each other after posting.

edge_cases.case: The source item carries an analytic distribution.
edge_cases.outcome: Both produced items carry it unchanged.

worked_examples.description: A revenue of 1 200.00 deferred in full to January
worked_examples.narrative: The destination entry dated the first of January debits the deferred-revenue account in the cancelling entry and, here, debits the revenue account by 1 200.00 while crediting the deferred-revenue account by 1 200.00, which recognises the revenue in the new period.

records.name: The items of the cancelling entry of a change of period
records.purpose: States the two items produced per source item in the entry dated at the lock-safe equivalent of the source date, which is the entry that removes the deferred amount from the original period.

operands.name: the reported debit, credit and foreign amount of the source item
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the source item
operands.source: the reported amounts of the transfer
operands.constraints: already rounded

operands.name: the account of the source item
operands.source: the selected Journal Item
operands.constraints: reused unchanged on the first item

operands.name: the accrual account
operands.source: the transfer form, revenue or expense according to the deduced nature
operands.constraints: used on the second item

operands.name: the lock-safe equivalent of the source date
operands.source: the accounting date of the source entry pushed through the accounting-date rule for the chosen journal, with no tax involvement
operands.constraints: items whose source dates map to the same lock-safe date share one cancelling entry

preconditions.condition: The accrual account matching the deduced nature is set on the transfer form.
preconditions.otherwise: The transfer cannot be produced.

preconditions.condition: The lock-safe equivalent of the source date can be computed for the chosen journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The cancelling entry cannot be dated.

procedure: Compute the lock-safe equivalent of the source date: the source date pushed through the accounting-date rule for the chosen journal, with no tax involvement.
Group the source items whose lock-safe dates coincide into one cancelling entry per date.

For each source item create a first item on the account of the source item, carrying the reported credit as its debit, the reported debit as its credit and minus the reported foreign amount as its foreign amount.
Create a second item on the accrual account, carrying the reported debit as its debit, the reported credit as its credit and the reported foreign amount as its foreign amount.
Give both items the counterpart and the analytic distribution of the source item, and the same label as the items of the destination entry.
After posting, reconcile the pairs of mirror items that share a label, a reconcilable account, a counterpart, a currency and an analytic distribution.
records.formula:
cancelling item 1 : account of the source item , debit = reported_credit , credit = reported_debit , foreign amount = − reported_amount_currency
cancelling item 2 : the accrual account            , debit = reported_debit , credit = reported_credit , foreign amount = reported_amount_currency

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: the reported amounts are already at the precision of their currency.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the debit and the credit, the currency of the source item for the foreign amount.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the reported amounts were computed.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the item construction.

result.name: the pair of items of the cancelling entry, per source item
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the source item
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as Journal Items of the cancelling Journal Entry, which balances because the two items mirror each other.

edge_cases.case: Two source items map to the same lock-safe date.
edge_cases.outcome: They share one cancelling entry.

edge_cases.case: The source date falls in a locked period.
edge_cases.outcome: The accounting-date rule pushes the cancelling entry to a date that is not locked.

edge_cases.case: The accrual account is reconcilable.
edge_cases.outcome: The two accrual items, one in each entry, are reconciled with each other after posting.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice posted on the twentieth of December, deferred in full to January by an accountant working on the thirty-first of December

expected_outputs.reconciliation: the two deferred-revenue items are reconciled with each other

worked_examples.narrative: The lock-safe equivalent of the twentieth of December, computed in January in a journal numbering monthly, is the thirty-first of December; the cancelling entry of that date debits the revenue account by 1 200.00 and credits the deferred-revenue account by 1 200.00, the destination entry of the first of January does the reverse, and the two deferred-revenue items are then reconciled with each other.

records.name: The counterpart item of a change-of-account transfer
records.purpose: Computes, per counterpart and per currency, the single item booked on the destination account of a transfer, together with its analytic distribution.

operands.name: the balance of each selected item
operands.source: the selected Journal Items whose account is not already the destination account
operands.constraints: accumulated per counterpart and per counterpart currency

operands.name: the counterpart foreign amount of each selected item
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the item, or the currency the destination account forces
operands.source: the selected Journal Items
operands.constraints: when the destination account forces a currency different from the company currency, the counterpart foreign amount is the balance of the item converted into that currency at the date of the item

operands.name: the analytic percentage of each analytic account on the item
operands.source: the analytic distribution of the selected Journal Item
operands.constraints: handled with two decimals

operands.name: the destination account
operands.source: the transfer form
operands.constraints: may force a currency

preconditions.condition: The accumulated foreign amount or the accumulated balance of the counterpart and currency is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No counterpart item is created for that pair.

preconditions.condition: The account of the selected item is not already the destination account.
preconditions.otherwise: The item is not transferred; it is only reconciled afterwards against the matching counterpart item.

procedure: For every selected item whose account is not already the destination account, determine the counterpart currency: the currency of the item, unless the destination account forces a currency different from the company currency, in which case it is that currency and the counterpart foreign amount is the balance of the item converted into it at the date of the item.

Accumulate, per pair of counterpart and counterpart currency, the counterpart foreign amount, the balance, and, per analytic account, the quantity equal to the balance multiplied by the percentage of that analytic account.
For every pair whose accumulated foreign amount or accumulated balance is not zero, create the counterpart item on the destination account.
Set its debit to the accumulated balance rounded to the company currency when that balance is positive, and its credit to the negative of that balance when it is negative.
Set its foreign amount to the accumulated foreign amount, made to carry the sign of the balance.

Set, for each analytic account, a percentage equal to one hundred multiplied by the accumulated amount of that analytic account divided by the accumulated balance, or one hundred when the accumulated balance is zero.
Label it "Transfer from" followed by the display name of the source account when exactly one source account exists, and "Transfer counterpart" otherwise.
records.formula:
accumulated_balance( counterpart , counterpart currency ) = sum of the balances of the selected items of that pair
accumulated_analytic( analytic account ) = sum of ( balance × percentage of that analytic account )
counterpart item : account = the destination account , debit = the accumulated balance when positive , credit = − the accumulated balance when negative , foreign amount = the accumulated foreign amount carrying the sign of the balance
analytic percentage = 100 × ( accumulated amount ÷ accumulated balance ) , or 100 when the accumulated balance is zero

rounding.what: The accumulated balance written as the debit or the credit, the accumulated foreign amount and each analytic percentage.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the balance, the counterpart currency for the foreign amount, two decimals for the analytic percentages.
rounding.step: On the accumulated balance before it is written as a debit or a credit, on the converted foreign amount at the date of the item, and on each analytic percentage before it is written.

result.name: the counterpart item on the destination account, per counterpart and per currency
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the counterpart currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as a Journal Item of the transfer entry, which is a plain entry numbered with the placeholder, in the chosen journal, at the chosen date, referenced "Transfer entry to" followed by the display name of the destination account, in the deepest child company among the companies of the accounts used and the active company.

edge_cases.case: The accumulated balance is zero but the accumulated foreign amount is not.
edge_cases.outcome: The counterpart item is still created, and every analytic percentage is one hundred.

edge_cases.case: The selection uses more than one source account.
edge_cases.outcome: The label is "Transfer counterpart" instead of naming the single source account.

edge_cases.case: The destination account forces a currency different from the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The counterpart currency is that currency and each counterpart foreign amount is the balance of the item converted into it at the date of the item.

edge_cases.case: The destination account allows matching.
edge_cases.outcome: After posting, the items already on the destination account are reconciled with the matching counterpart items.

worked_examples.description: Two receivable items of the same customer transferred to a doubtful-debt account
worked_examples.narrative: The two balances accumulate to 1 000.00 for the pair of the customer and the company currency, so the counterpart item debits the doubtful-debt account by 1 000.00 and is labelled after the single source account.

records.name: The mirror item of a change-of-account transfer
records.purpose: Computes, per counterpart, currency, source account and analytic distribution, the item that empties the source account, so that the transfer entry balances and the source items can be matched away.

operands.name: the balance of each selected item
operands.source: the selected Journal Items whose account is not already the destination account
operands.constraints: accumulated per counterpart, item currency, account and analytic distribution

operands.name: the foreign amount of each selected item
operands.source: the selected Journal Items
operands.constraints: accumulated with the same grouping

operands.name: the source account
operands.source: the selected Journal Items
operands.constraints: reused on the mirror item

operands.name: the destination account
operands.source: the transfer form
operands.constraints: named in the label of the mirror item

preconditions.condition: The accumulated balance of the group is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No mirror item is created for that group.

procedure: Accumulate the source items per group of counterpart, item currency, account and analytic distribution.
For every group whose accumulated balance is not zero, create the mirror item on the source account.
Set its debit to the negative of the accumulated balance when that balance is negative.
Set its credit to the accumulated balance when that balance is positive.
Set its foreign amount to the accumulated foreign amount carrying the opposite sign of the balance.
Label it "Transfer to" followed by the display name of the destination account.

Post the entry, then reconcile, per counterpart, currency and source account, the source items with the matching mirror items when the source account allows matching, and the items already on the destination account with the matching counterpart items when the destination account allows matching.
records.formula: mirror item : account = the source account , debit = − the accumulated balance when it is negative , credit = the accumulated balance when it is positive , foreign amount = the accumulated foreign amount with the opposite sign of the balance

rounding.what: The accumulated balance written as the debit or the credit, and the accumulated foreign amount.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the balance, the currency of the items of the group for the foreign amount.
rounding.step: On the accumulated balance before it is written as a debit or a credit.

result.name: the mirror item on the source account, per counterpart, currency, account and analytic distribution
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the items of the group
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as a Journal Item of the transfer entry; it is matched with the source items when the source account allows matching.

edge_cases.case: The accumulated balance of a group is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: No mirror item is created for that group.

edge_cases.case: The source account does not allow matching.
edge_cases.outcome: The mirror item is created but nothing is reconciled on that account.

edge_cases.case: The selection spans several source accounts.
edge_cases.outcome: One mirror item is created per source account within each group, and the counterpart item is labelled "Transfer counterpart".

worked_examples.description: Two receivable items of the same customer transferred to a doubtful-debt account

expected_outputs.reconciliation: the two original items and the mirror item are reconciled together on the receivable account

worked_examples.narrative: The accumulated balance is positive, so the mirror item credits the receivable account by 1 000.00; after posting, the two original items and the mirror item are reconciled together on that account.

records.name: The order in which numbers are assigned when several entries are posted at once
records.purpose: Fixes which entry of a batch consumes which number, so that the numbering follows the accounting dates and not the order in which the entries were selected or created.

operands.name: the accounting date of each entry of the batch
operands.source: the Journal Entries being posted
operands.constraints: the first component of the sort key

operands.name: the reference of each entry
operands.source: the Journal Entries being posted
operands.constraints: the empty text when there is none; the second component of the sort key

operands.name: the original identifier of each entry
operands.source: the Journal Entries being posted
operands.constraints: the third component of the sort key, which orders entries created on the same date with the same reference by creation order

operands.name: the state and the number of each entry
operands.source: the Journal Entries being posted
operands.constraints: an entry is skipped when it is cancelled; a number that exists and is not the placeholder is a real number

preconditions.condition: The entry is not cancelled.
preconditions.otherwise: It is skipped and consumes no number.

preconditions.condition: The entry has an accounting date.
preconditions.otherwise: No number is assigned to it.

procedure: Sort the batch ascending by the accounting date, then by the reference or the empty text, then by the original identifier.
Walk the sorted list and skip every cancelled entry.
When the entry was never posted and its number does not match its accounting date under the date-alignment test, clear the number and continue with the next entry.
When the entry has an accounting date, has no number and is not draft, assign the next number of its chain.
After the walk, run the inverse of the number field: recompute the payment reference of every entry that now has a real number, and refresh the gap flags.
records.formula: sort key = ( accounting date , reference or the empty string , original identifier ) , ascending on all three components

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counters assigned are whole numbers.
rounding.precision: The recorded counter length of each chain.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the number assigned to each entry of the batch
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the Journal Entries; the payment references and the gap flags are refreshed afterwards.

edge_cases.case: An entry already carries a number that was cleared by hand.
edge_cases.outcome: It takes the next number of its chain in its position in the sorted order, not in its creation order.

edge_cases.case: An entry was never posted and its number does not match its date.
edge_cases.outcome: Its number is cleared and it is skipped in this walk.

edge_cases.case: Several entries share an accounting date and have no reference.
edge_cases.outcome: They are ordered by their original identifier, that is by creation order.

worked_examples.description: Six draft entries posted in one operation on a chain whose highest number is the first of the period

inputs.note: the number of the first entry was cleared by hand

worked_examples.narrative: The sort key orders the batch by the fourth of March, then the three entries of the fifth of March in creation order, then the sixth and the seventh, so the entry created fourth takes the first number and the entry created first takes the second.

records.name: The date-alignment test of a number against an accounting date
records.purpose: Decides whether the year, the end year and the month written in a number agree with the period of the accounting date, which is what stops an entry keeping a number of the wrong period.

operands.name: the number of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: read with the shape of the deduced periodicity

operands.name: the accounting date of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: supplies the period boundaries and the month

operands.name: the number of characters the year and the end year occupy in the number
operands.source: the number itself
operands.constraints: used to truncate the years of the period before the comparison

preconditions.condition: The entry has both a number and an accounting date.
preconditions.otherwise: The test answers that the number matches.

preconditions.condition: The entry is posted, is not in quick-encoding mode, and its date is later than the bound set by the system parameter, which is by default the first of January nineteen seventy so that in practice the test always applies.
preconditions.otherwise: The check is not applied.

procedure: When the entry has no number or no accounting date, answer that it matches.
Read the number with the shape of its deduced periodicity to obtain the year, the end year and the month values.
Compute the period boundaries for that periodicity from the accounting date.
The year matches when the number carries no year, or when the year value equals the start year of the period truncated to the number of characters the year occupies in the number.
The end year matches under the same rule against the end year of the period.
The month matches when the number carries no month, or when the month value equals the month of the accounting date.
Answer that the number matches the date when the year, the end year and the month all match.
records.formula:
matches = ( the number carries no year   or year_value     = truncate( start year of the period , characters the year occupies ) )
      and ( the number carries no end year or end_year_value = truncate( end year of the period , characters the end year occupies ) )
      and ( the number carries no month  or month_value    = the month of the accounting date )

rounding.what: The years of the period, truncated to the number of characters they occupy in the number.
rounding.precision: The number of characters the year and the end year occupy in the number.
rounding.method: The remainder of the division by ten raised to that number of characters.
rounding.step: Before each of the two year comparisons.

result.name: the number is aligned with the accounting date
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; a negative answer either clears the number during a batch posting or refuses the write with "The *the date field label* (*the date*) you've entered isn't aligned with the existing sequence number (*the number*). Clear the sequence number to proceed." followed by the advice to select entries and use the resequence option from the actions menu, available in developer mode.

edge_cases.case: The number carries no year at all, as with a purely numeric number.
edge_cases.outcome: The year comparison is satisfied and only the remaining parts matter.

edge_cases.case: The number carries a two-digit year.
edge_cases.outcome: The year of the period is truncated to two digits before the comparison.

edge_cases.case: The entry was never posted and the number does not match.
edge_cases.outcome: The number is cleared during the batch posting and the entry is skipped in that walk.

worked_examples.description: A monthly number tested against a date of the same month
worked_examples.narrative: The year and the month both agree with the period of the accounting date, so the number is aligned.

worked_examples.description: The same number tested against a date of the following month
worked_examples.narrative: The month written in the number is three and the month of the accounting date is four, so the number is not aligned and either it is cleared or the write is refused.

records.name: The proposed number shown before posting
records.purpose: Shows a draft entry the number it would take, without consuming it, and only in the one situation in which that proposal cannot be wrong.

operands.name: the number currently on the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: the proposal is shown only when it is empty or is the placeholder value

operands.name: the accounting date of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: must be known

operands.name: the previous number of the chain under the strict search
operands.unit_or_currency: a text, or the absence of one
operands.source: the chain search with the relaxed flag off
operands.constraints: the proposal is shown only when there is none, that is when the entry would be the first of its period

preconditions.condition: The number of the entry is empty or is the placeholder value, the accounting date is known, and the chain has no previous number under the strict search.
preconditions.otherwise: No proposal is shown, because for any later entry the proposed value would be wrong as soon as another user posts first.

procedure: Show the proposal only when the number is empty or is the placeholder value, the accounting date is known, and the chain has no previous number under the strict search, that is when the entry would be the first of its period.
Compute the next template and its values exactly as at posting.
Increase the counter value by one and fill the template.
Show nothing in every other case.
records.formula: proposed_number = fill( the template computed as at posting , the values with the counter increased by one ) , shown only when the entry would be the first of its period

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the counter is a whole number padded to its recorded length.
rounding.precision: The recorded counter length of the chain.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the proposed number
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the draft entry as a placeholder value; nothing is written and no number is consumed.

edge_cases.case: The chain already has a previous number in the period.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is shown, deliberately, because the proposal would be wrong as soon as another user posts first.

edge_cases.case: The entry has no accounting date.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is shown.

edge_cases.case: The entry already carries a real number.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is shown, because there is nothing to propose.

worked_examples.description: The first draft entry of a fresh March chain in a miscellaneous journal

expected_outputs.template: MISC/ then the year on four digits then / then the month on two digits then / then the counter on four digits

worked_examples.narrative: The entry would be the first of its period, so the proposal is shown; the counter of the starting number is increased by one and the template is filled.

worked_examples.description: A second draft entry of the same period
worked_examples.narrative: The chain already has a previous number in the period, so nothing is proposed.

records.name: The numbering-holes indicator of a journal
records.purpose: Reports, per journal, whether an entry still correctable opens a hole in the numbering, so that the accountant is warned only about holes that can still be fixed.

operands.name: the fiscal lock date that applies to the acting user with the exceptions ignored, per journal
operands.source: the fiscal lock date computation run with exceptions ignored
operands.constraints: the grouping key of the journals

operands.name: the companies concerned
operands.source: for each group, the company of the journal and every descendant of it
operands.constraints: restricts which entries are examined

operands.name: the gap flag and the accounting date of each entry
operands.unit_or_currency: a yes or no value and a date
operands.source: the Journal Entries of those journals and companies
operands.constraints: only entries carrying the flag and dated strictly after the lock date count

operands.name: the numbering prefix of each such entry
operands.source: the Journal Entries
operands.constraints: the pair of journal and prefix is what is collected

preconditions.condition: The fiscal lock date of the journal can be computed for the acting user with the exceptions ignored.
preconditions.otherwise: The minimal representable date is used, so nothing is excluded.

procedure: Group the journals by the fiscal lock date that applies to the acting user with the exceptions ignored, for that journal.
For each group, collect the companies that are the journal company or a descendant of it.
Select the distinct pairs of journal and numbering prefix among the entries of those journals and companies that carry the gap flag and whose accounting date is strictly after that lock date.
Report that a journal has a hole when at least one such pair exists.
Open, from the indicator, the list of every entry of the journals and prefixes concerned, so that the user sees the hole in context rather than the single flagged entry.
records.formula: has_holes( journal ) = there exists at least one pair ( journal , numbering prefix ) among the entries that carry the gap flag, belong to the journal company or a descendant of it, and are dated strictly after the fiscal lock date of that journal computed with the exceptions ignored

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the comparison is between whole dates.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the journal has numbering holes
result.unit_or_currency: a yes or no answer, with the pairs of journal and prefix behind it
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as a dashboard indicator; the indicator is invalidated whenever the gap detection runs.

edge_cases.case: The hole is inside a locked period.
edge_cases.outcome: It is deliberately excluded, because its holes can no longer be corrected and reporting them would be noise.

edge_cases.case: The acting user holds a lock exception.
edge_cases.outcome: The grouping uses the fiscal lock date computed with the exceptions ignored, so the indicator does not vary with the exceptions.

edge_cases.case: The journal belongs to a parent company.
edge_cases.outcome: The entries of the descendant companies are examined too.

worked_examples.description: A miscellaneous journal with a hole opened after a deletion, part of it inside a locked period
worked_examples.narrative: The January entry is dated on or before the lock date and is excluded, the March entry is strictly after it and is kept, so the journal reports a hole and the list opened by the indicator shows every entry of the March prefix.

records.name: The display name of a journal entry
records.purpose: Composes the text by which an entry is identified in lists, links and printed documents, including for a draft document that has no number yet.

operands.name: the state of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: decides which parts are appended

operands.name: the document type of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: its label is used for a draft entry

operands.name: the number of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: used for a posted or cancelled entry

operands.name: the reference of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: used for a draft entry; the word "Unknown" is used when there is none

operands.name: the counterpart name and the accounting date
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: appended only when the full display mode is requested

preconditions.condition: The state of the entry is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The name cannot be composed.

procedure: Start with an empty list of parts.
When the entry is draft, append the label of the document type prefixed by the word "Draft" and a space, the label of a plain entry being "Journal Entry".
When the entry is draft, append in parentheses the reference when there is one, and otherwise the word "Unknown", which is what identifies a draft document that has no number yet.
When the entry is cancelled, append the number and then the word "(Cancelled)".
When the entry is posted, append the number.
When the full display mode is requested, append the counterpart name and the accounting date.
Join the parts with spaces.
records.formula: display_name = the parts joined by spaces , the parts being : "Draft " + the label of the document type and the reference or "Unknown" in parentheses (draft) ; the number and "(Cancelled)" (cancelled) ; the number (posted) ; and, in the full display mode, the counterpart name and the accounting date

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the display name of the entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed wherever the entry is referred to, including in printed documents and in the text of validation messages.

edge_cases.case: A customer invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: Its document-type label is "Invoice" and not "Customer Invoice", so that the name printed to a customer says simply Invoice.

edge_cases.case: A customer credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: Its document-type label is "Credit Note" and not "Customer Credit Note", for the same reason; the labels of the remaining types are Journal Entry, Vendor Bill, Vendor Credit Note, Sales Receipt and Purchase Receipt.

edge_cases.case: A draft entry with no reference.
edge_cases.outcome: The word "Unknown" is shown in parentheses.

worked_examples.description: The three states of a customer invoice referenced by an order number
worked_examples.narrative: A draft shows the word Draft, the document-type label and the reference in parentheses; a posted entry shows its number; a cancelled entry shows its number followed by the word in parentheses.

worked_examples.description: A draft plain entry with no reference
worked_examples.narrative: There is no reference, so the word Unknown is shown in parentheses.

records.name: Whether a journal item is tax exigible
records.purpose: Decides whether an item is reportable in the tax report now rather than at payment time, which is what separates ordinary taxes from taxes exigible on payment.

operands.name: whether the entry is marked always tax exigible
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: true for every entry that is not an invoice-like document and that collects no cash-basis values

operands.name: the originating tax of the item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: its exigibility on payment is read

operands.name: the taxes of the item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: their exigibility on payment is read

operands.name: the tax grids of the item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: an item that only has grids is exigible

operands.name: whether the entry is itself a cash-basis entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry
operands.constraints: makes the item exigible

preconditions.condition: The item belongs to a Journal Entry whose tax marking is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The first test cannot be evaluated.

procedure: Answer yes when the entry the item belongs to is marked always tax exigible, which is the case for every entry that is not an invoice-like document and that collects no cash-basis values.
Answer yes when the item carries neither an originating tax nor any tax, that is when it only has grids.
Answer yes when the entry is itself a cash-basis entry.
Answer yes when the originating tax of the item is not exigible on payment.
Answer yes when at least one of the taxes of the item is not exigible on payment.
Answer no in every other case.
records.formula:
tax_exigible( item ) = ( the entry is marked always tax exigible )
                    or ( the item carries neither an originating tax nor any tax )
                    or ( the entry is a cash-basis entry )
                    or ( the originating tax of the item is not exigible on payment )
                    or ( at least one of the taxes of the item is not exigible on payment )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the answer is a yes or no value.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the item is tax exigible
result.stored_or_displayed: Held on the Journal Item; it decides whether the item is reported in the tax report now rather than at payment time.

edge_cases.case: An item carries a mixture of cash-basis and ordinary taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: It is reportable, because the last two tests are deliberately at least one; this is why mixing the two on one item while they share a grid is forbidden.

edge_cases.case: An item carries only tax grids.
edge_cases.outcome: It is exigible by the second test.

edge_cases.case: A plain entry that collects no cash-basis values.
edge_cases.outcome: It is marked always tax exigible, so all its items are exigible.

worked_examples.description: An item of an invoice carrying one ordinary tax

taxes: one tax that is not exigible on payment

worked_examples.narrative: At least one of the taxes of the item is not exigible on payment, so the item is reportable now.

worked_examples.description: An item of an invoice carrying only a tax exigible on payment
worked_examples.narrative: No test is satisfied, so the item is reported at payment time and not now.

records.name: Whether a journal item or a journal entry affects the tax report
records.purpose: Decides whether an item, and therefore its entry, touches the tax report, which is what makes the Tax Return Lock Date apply and what the accounting date rule consults.

operands.name: the taxes carried by the item
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: at least one is enough

operands.name: whether the item is a tax line
operands.source: the display type of the Journal Item
operands.constraints: a tax line always affects the report

operands.name: the grids carried by the item and their applicability
operands.source: the Journal Item
operands.constraints: a grid whose applicability is taxes is enough

preconditions.condition: The item is loaded with its taxes and its grids.
preconditions.otherwise: The three tests cannot be evaluated.

procedure: Answer yes for an item when it carries at least one tax.
Answer yes for an item when it is a tax line.
Answer yes for an item when it carries at least one grid whose applicability is taxes.
Answer yes for an entry when at least one of its items affects the tax report.
records.formula:
affects_tax_report( item ) = ( the item carries at least one tax )
                          or ( the item is a tax line )
                          or ( the item carries at least one grid whose applicability is taxes )

affects_tax_report( entry ) = at least one of its items affects the tax report

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the answer is a yes or no value.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the item, or the entry, affects the tax report
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is used by the tax lock check and by the accounting date rule.

edge_cases.case: An item carries a grid whose applicability is not taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: That grid alone does not make the item affect the tax report.

edge_cases.case: A plain entry with no tax anywhere.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not affect the tax report, so the Tax Return Lock Date is not consulted for it.

edge_cases.case: An entry with one taxed item among many.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole entry affects the tax report.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice with a product line carrying a tax and a tax line

grids: a grid whose applicability is taxes

worked_examples.narrative: The product line carries a tax and the tax line is a tax line, so both affect the report and the entry does too; the Tax Return Lock Date is therefore consulted for this entry.

worked_examples.description: A plain accrual entry with no tax
worked_examples.narrative: No item carries a tax, is a tax line, or carries a grid whose applicability is taxes, so the entry does not affect the tax report.

records.name: The number of journal items behind the liquidity journal balance
records.purpose: Counts the items the dashboard balance of a liquidity journal is made of, so that the card can show how many movements sit behind the figure.

operands.name: the items on the default account of the journal
operands.source: every journal, because the aggregation is driven by the account
operands.constraints: the entry must not be cancelled and the display type must not be a section, a subsection or a note

preconditions.condition: The journal has a default account.
preconditions.otherwise: No items can be selected and the count is zero.

procedure: Select every Journal Item on the default account of the journal, whichever journal it was booked in.
Exclude the items whose entry is cancelled.
Exclude the items whose display type is a section, a subsection or a note.
Count the remaining items and report the count together with the balance.
records.formula: item_count = the number of items on the default account of the journal whose entry is not cancelled and whose display type is not a section, a subsection or a note

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is a whole count.
rounding.precision: A whole number.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the number of items behind the balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the accounting dashboard card of the journal, next to the balance.

edge_cases.case: An amount is booked on the bank account from another journal.
edge_cases.outcome: It is counted, because the aggregation deliberately ignores the journal of the item: an amount booked on the bank account from another journal is part of the bank balance.

edge_cases.case: The entry of an item is cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: The item is not counted.

edge_cases.case: The account has no item at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The count is zero and the balance is zero.

worked_examples.description: A bank journal after an opening balance, a customer receipt and one cancelled entry
worked_examples.narrative: The cancelled entry and the note are excluded, so two items sit behind a balance of 12 909.09.

records.name: The running balance of the last statement of a liquidity journal
records.purpose: Gives the balance the bank account has reached according to the last statement plus everything booked after it, which is the second figure the dashboard card of a liquidity journal shows.

operands.name: the closing balance of the most recent statement of the journal that has a first-line index
operands.source: the statements of the journal, taken in descending date then descending identifier order
operands.constraints: read as zero when no such statement exists

operands.name: the first-line index of that statement
operands.source: the same statement
operands.constraints: the transactions counted are those whose internal index is greater than or equal to it

operands.name: the amounts of the transactions of the journal that belong to no statement
operands.source: the transactions of the journal
operands.constraints: their entry must not be cancelled and their internal index must be greater than or equal to the first-line index of that statement

preconditions.condition: The journal has at least one statement with a first-line index.
preconditions.otherwise: The closing balance is read as zero and only the transactions belonging to no statement are added.

procedure: Take the statements of the journal in descending date order and then descending identifier order, and keep the most recent one that has a first-line index.
Read its closing balance, or zero when no such statement exists.

Add the amounts of the transactions of the journal that belong to no statement, whose entry is not cancelled, and whose internal index is greater than or equal to the first-line index of that statement.
Report the pair made of whether anything at all was found and the resulting amount, which is what the card shows.
records.formula:
running_balance = the closing balance of the most recent statement of the journal that has a first-line index, taken in descending date then descending identifier order
                + the sum of the amounts of the transactions of the journal that belong to no statement, whose entry is not cancelled, and whose internal index is greater than or equal to the first-line index of that statement

rounding.what: Nothing further is rounded: the closing balance and each transaction amount are already at the precision of the currency of the journal.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency of the journal.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier on each amount.
rounding.step: No rounding step in the sum.

result.name: the running balance of the last statement
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the accounting dashboard card of the journal, together with the indication of whether anything at all was found.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no statement with a first-line index.
edge_cases.outcome: The closing balance is read as zero and only the transactions belonging to no statement are added.

edge_cases.case: A transaction belongs to a statement.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not added again, because its effect is already inside the closing balance.

edge_cases.case: The entry of a transaction is cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: That transaction is excluded.

worked_examples.description: A bank journal whose last statement closes at 12 000.00 and which has two later transactions outside any statement
worked_examples.narrative: The transaction whose internal index is below the first-line index of the statement is excluded; twelve thousand plus nine hundred and nine point zero nine minus two hundred and fifty is 12 659.09.

records.name: The outstanding payment accounts of a journal
records.purpose: Gives the two sets of accounts on which money in transit sits for a journal, which the dashboard card and the payment matching both read.

operands.name: the money-in payment method lines of the journal
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: each carries an outstanding account

operands.name: the money-out payment method lines of the journal
operands.source: the journal
operands.constraints: each carries an outstanding account

preconditions.condition: The journal defines payment method lines.
preconditions.otherwise: Both sets are empty.

procedure: Read the outstanding account of every money-in payment method line of the journal and collect them into the inbound set.
Read the outstanding account of every money-out payment method line of the journal and collect them into the outbound set.
Report the two sets.
records.formula:
inbound_outstanding_accounts  = the set of outstanding accounts of the money-in method lines
outbound_outstanding_accounts = the set of outstanding accounts of the money-out method lines

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded: the result is two sets of accounts.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the inbound and the outbound sets of outstanding accounts
result.stored_or_displayed: Read by the accounting dashboard card of the journal and by the payment matching.

edge_cases.case: Two method lines share one outstanding account.
edge_cases.outcome: The account appears once, because the result is a set.

edge_cases.case: The journal has money-in lines only.
edge_cases.outcome: The outbound set is empty.

edge_cases.case: The journal carries a foreign currency.
